**NEW.** Match Text Formatting (the Match button of the Formatting panel: it takes up the look of the letters selected and gives all of it, the font, bold, italic, the lines, the colour, the height, the slant, the tracking and the width, to the next letters selected, one step of the editor's undo; Esc puts the brush down), AutoCAPS (letters typed, pasted or imported go in as capitals, the words there left alone) and Import Text (the Tools panel: a `.txt` or `.rtf` file of 32 KB at most put in at the caret, over the selection, one undo step; `CadMTextImport` keeps from an RTF the font where it is not the document's default, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, the colour, the size as a ratio of the MTEXT's height, paragraphs and tabs, and drops paragraph formatting, tables, pictures, headers, footnotes and the other character effects) in the MTEXT editor, all three greyed before.
**NEW.** The MTEXT editor's own Find and Replace, which replaces the small popup of the Tools panel and opens with Ctrl+H too: Find what, Replace with, Match case, Whole words only, Use wildcards (`*`, `?`, `#`, `@`, `[AB]`), Match diacritics (off, "cafe" finds "café") and Match half/full width forms (off, "ABC" finds "ＡＢＣ"), and Find Next, Replace (the match selected is replaced and the next one selected) and Replace All (one undo step, the text put in not searched again). The dialog stays open beside the words and closes with the editor. `CadMTextEditor.FindNext`, `Replace` and `ReplaceAll` take a `CadMTextFindOptions`; a symbol or stack counts as one place, so a match after a stack is now selected at its place, where it was selected as many places late as the stack has extra letters (two for 1/2).
**NEW.** Spell check in the MTEXT editor, as the Spell Check panel of AutoCAD 2021's Text Editor tab: a red wavy underline under each word not in the dictionary as the words are typed (the toggle of the panel turns it off), a right-click on one gives the words nearest it, Add Word and Ignore All before the editor's menu, and Edit Dictionaries shows the main dictionary and the custom dictionary file with its words, to which Add and Delete write at once. The custom dictionary is `sample.cus` of the settings folder (`%AppData%\GeometryHelper\Drawing`), a text file of words one to a line, which SPELL and Check Spelling now start with too (the first Add makes it; before, SPELL asked for a file each time). The dictionary is public as `CadSpellDictionary` (`IsMisspelled`, `Suggest`, `Check` of a `CadMTextEditor`, `Add`, `Remove`, `IgnoreAll`).
**CHANGED.** The built-in English dictionary of SPELL, Check Spelling and the editor's spell check is the SCOWL word lists in American and British spelling, 92 465 words in a file of 270 KB inside the library (the notice of Kevin Atkinson's English Speller Database is in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`), where it was about 700 English words and drafting terms, which stay in it; the words nearest a misspelled one are ranked by how near, then a swap of two letters, letters missing, letters added, how common the word is, its length and its letters ("wrold" gives world, "Helo" Hello, "recieve" receive, "frist" first), the same every time. The dictionary is read, 92 465 words, in about 25 ms when the first word is checked. In `TextEditorViewModel` (not in a package) `IsFindShown` is gone with the popup, and `Spell Check` and `Edit Dictionaries` are no longer greyed.
**NEW.** DWGPROPS in the presenter, AutoCAD 2021's Drawing Properties dialog: General (type, location, size as `12.50KB (12 800 bytes)`, dates, the Read-only and Hidden boxes, greyed), Summary (Title, Subject, Author, Keywords, Comments, Hyperlink base), Statistics (Created, Modified, Last saved by, Revision number, Total editing time as `1 hour, 30 minutes`) and Custom (name and value rows, Add and Delete). OK writes the Summary and Custom tabs through `DxfDatabase.SummaryInfo` as one undo step (the header of a drawing of R2004 or later, the DWGPROPS record of an older one); a custom property with no name or a name used twice (letters of either case the same) is refused in the footer. New public `CadDrawingPropertiesRequest`; with no window the command says `DWGPROPS is shown by the window.`
**NEW.** A DWG of R2004 or later keeps the drawing's properties in its `AcDb:SummaryInfo` section, written and read as AutoCAD 2021 lays it out: eight texts (title, subject, author, keywords, comments, last saved by, revision, hyperlink base) as UTF-16 counted with their end mark (the code page's bytes in R2004), the time spent as days and milliseconds, the dates made and saved as a Julian day and the milliseconds of it, the custom properties and two whole numbers of nought. The writer reproduces the bytes of the sections AutoCAD saved of a drawing in code (R2018 and R2004, checked byte for byte; the dates from `$TDUCREATE` and `$TDUUPDATE`), codes the section 4 in R2007 as it does the application information, and AutoCAD 2021 reads the properties back from all five versions and finds 0 errors with `AUDIT`. Before this a DWG saved from the presenter lost its title, author and custom properties; they now survive a save as DXF and as DWG. A drawing of R2000 keeps them in the DWGPROPS record among its objects, as before.
**CHANGED.** A save from the presenter sets `$TDUPDATE` and `$TDUUPDATE` to the time and `$LASTSAVEDBY` to the login name, each where the header has the variable, as AutoCAD's save does, so that Drawing Properties shows when and by whom the drawing was saved.
**NEW.** HYPERLINK and -HYPERLINK in the presenter, in the words of AutoCAD 2021's own string table. HYPERLINK asks `Select objects:` and shows Insert Hyperlink, or Edit Hyperlink with Remove Link where an object has a link: Existing File or Web Page (the address, Browse…, the named location), View of This Drawing (a link with no address and the view as its place) and E-mail Address (`mailto:` with its subject), and Text to display; an address, text or place over 255 characters is refused as AutoCAD refuses it. -HYPERLINK asks `Enter an option [Remove/Insert] <Insert>:`, `Enter hyperlink insert option [Area/Object] <Object>:`, `Overwrite existing hyperlinks? [Yes/No] <Yes>:`, `Enter hyperlink <current drawing>:`, `Enter named location <none>:` and `Enter description <none>:`; Area draws a closed rectangle on the layer URLLAYER carrying the link, and Remove says `2 hyperlinks deleted.` The links are the extended data of PE_URL as AutoCAD writes them. With the cursor over an object with a link a tooltip shows its text and `CTRL + click to follow link`; Ctrl+click follows it (a web or mail address or a file opens with the system's program, a DXF or DWG opens in the presenter, a view is restored), and the Edit shortcut menu of such an object has Hyperlink: Open, Copy Hyperlink and Edit Hyperlink…. New public `CadHyperlinks`, `CadHyperlinkTarget`, `CadHyperlinkTargetKind`, `CadHyperlinkRequest` and `CadHyperlinkKind`; `MainViewModel.FollowHyperlink`, `HyperlinkTooltip` and `OpenLink`.
**NEW.** GROUPEDIT in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 asks it (probed through its console): `Select group or [Name]:`, then `Enter an option [Add objects/Remove objects/REName]:` until Enter; Add and Remove ask the objects as -GROUP's options do, REName the new name. The Home tab's Group Edit button, greyed before, runs it, and so do the Add to Group and Remove from Group items of the Edit shortcut menu's Group submenu, also grey before.
**NEW.** ATTREDEF, the Express Tools command, in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's own ATTREDEF.LSP does it (run in its console to check the prompts and the result): `Enter name of the block you wish to redefine:`, `Select objects for new Block...`, `Specify insertion base point of new Block:`. The block is defined again from the objects and each reference of it is put anew at the same point, scale, rotation and normal: an attribute whose tag the new block has keeps its value, a new one is given its default, one the block lacks is dropped; the new references are on the current layer, as AutoCAD's are. One undo step.
**NEW.** MEASUREGEOM Quick and Mode in the presenter (`Enter an option [Distance/Radius/Angle/ARea/Quick/Mode/eXit] <Distance>:`, `Move cursor or [...] <eXit>:`, `Always default to quick measure behavior? [Yes/No] <No>:`, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks them). The dimensions of what the cursor is over are drawn beside it as the prompt's preview: a line's length, the angle where another line meets it, the distance across to a parallel line near, a circle's or arc's radius, and inside a closed boundary the width and height through the cursor and the area; a click writes the reading on the command line. A simple version: lines, circles, arcs and the straight sides of polylines, and no Volume option.
**NEW.** CLEANSCREENON and CLEANSCREENOFF, and Ctrl+0 to switch between them: the ribbon, Properties and the Drawings list hidden, each remembered as it was, the command line kept.
**NEW.** Cut, Copy and Paste of table cells in the presenter (Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and the Table Cell menu): the cells selected are held as a snapshot (`CadTableCellClip`: each cell's words, number with its kind, unit and format, block with scale, turn and attribute values, field or formula, its own alignment, text height, style, colour, fill and borders, and the merges within them), Cut empties the cells as Delete does, and Paste gives them to a range from its top left cell, filling a range of whole multiples with them and moving the references of a pasted formula by the rows and columns it moved (`=Sum(A1:A3)` copied from A4 into B5 is `=Sum(B2:B4)`, `$` holds a reference). One undo step each; cells over the table's last row or column are left out. MATCHCELL (Match Cell) asks `Select source cell:` and `Select destination cell:` and gives each destination the source's look and data format. `CadTableEditor.Copy`, `Cut`, `Paste` and `MatchCell` do it from code.
**NEW.** Cell Locking in the presenter and in the library: `DxfCellState` (Content Locked 1, Format Locked 16, the flags of a linked cell and of a content or format read only or changed after an update) and `DxfTable.GetCellState`, `SetCellState` and `TryFindCellState` (the first cell of a range locked in a way, one reading of the TABLECONTENT for the range: checking 1 000 cells before an edit cost 235 ms asked cell by cell and 0.23 ms so), which read and write the 90 after the LINKEDTABLEDATACELL_BEGIN of the cell in the TABLECONTENT (a table of none is given one, as `SetDataLink` gives it, the flag of a linked cell kept). The tab's Cell Locking menu and the right-click Locking submenu set Unlocked, Content Locked, Format Locked and Content and Format Locked; a cell locked in its content refuses typing (TABLEDIT says so before it opens), Delete, Cut, Paste, Autofill and an inserted block, field or formula, one locked in its format its alignment, fill, borders, data format, cell style, Match Cell and Paste. The locks of a table AutoCAD wrote are kept and honoured; they reach a DXF and a DWG of R2007 or later.
**NEW.** Data Format of table cells in the presenter: the Table Cell Format dialog (Custom Table Cell Format; Angle, Currency, Date, Decimal Number, General, Percentage, Point, Text and Whole Number, each with its options: units, angle units, precision, decimal and thousands separators, prefix, suffix, conversion factor, zeros to leave out, date format, and a sample), and each kind chosen in the Data Format menu given its usual format at once. A number of a format with `%ps[prefix,suffix]` or `%ct8[factor]` is now shown with its prefix, suffix and factor in the cell (`%lu2%pr2%ps[$,]%th44` of 1234.5 is `$1,234.50`, `%lu2%pr0%ps[,%]%ct8[100]` of 0.5 is `50%`); the library showed such a number to six places and ignored them. `CadTableEditor.SetDataFormat` does it from code.
**NEW.** Cell styles of tables in the presenter and the library. The Cell Styles box lists the table style's cell styles (Title, Header, Data and those a user made) with Create New Cell Style and Manage Cell Styles (New, Rename, Delete); choosing one gives the cells its look (alignment, text height, style and colour, fill, borders) as their own overrides and its id in their TABLECONTENT; By Row/Column takes it back. `DxfTableStyle.GetCellStyleNames`, `AddCellStyle`, `RemoveCellStyle`, `RenameCellStyle`, `GetCellStyleId`, `GetCellStyleName` and `GetCellStyleLook` (`DxfCellStyleLook`) keep the user's cell styles in the table style's CELLSTYLEMAP (id 101 on), and `DxfTable.GetCellStyleId` and `SetCellStyleId` the style a cell takes. `CadTableEditor.SetCellStyle`, `CreateCellStyle`, `DeleteCellStyle` and `RenameCellStyle` do it from code. A DXF keeps the user's cell styles; a DWG of R2010 or later keeps the three, as its writer does.
**NEW.** Cell Borders of table cells in the presenter: the Cell Border Properties dialog (the lines All, Outside, Inside, Bottom, Left, Top and Right, or No Border, given a lineweight and a colour; the linetype, double line and spacing are greyed, as the DXF of R2000 to R2018 holds no group for them). `CadTableEditor.SetCellBorders` does it from code.
**NEW.** Insert Block, Field and Formula in table cells in the presenter and the library. The Insert a Block in a Table Cell dialog (the block, AutoFit or a scale, a rotation angle, the cell's alignment) makes the cell a block cell (`DxfTable.SetBlockTableRecord`: the block (340), its scale (144), the count of its attributes (179) and each non-constant attribute's definition (331) and text (300), before the value as AutoCAD 2021 writes them); Insert Field shows the Field dialog and keeps the field in the cell (`DxfTable.GetFieldCode`, `SetFieldCode`, `GetFieldCells`); Insert Formula (Sum, Average, Count, Cell, Equation) runs EDITTABLECELL, which asks for the cells and writes `=Sum(A3:B4)` as `SetFormula` does. The cell shows what the field or formula comes to (`DxfTable.SetFieldValue` writes the value and keeps the field), and every formula and field of a table is worked out again after each edit of it and when the drawing is opened or saved (FIELDEVAL), in the order they read one another's cells: `=Sum` , `Average` and `Count` of ranges, cell references (`B3`, `$B$3`), `+ - * / ^` and the functions of the AcExpr fields; words in a cell a formula reads, or a division by nought, show `#####`. The follow-ups the fields work left, a formula over table cells and the update of table cells, are done.
**NEW.** MATCHCELL and EDITTABLECELL in the command registry (302 commands). EDITTABLECELL is AutoCAD's name; the presenter implements its formula part (`_EditTableCell _ExecuteOneAction _Operation _InsertFormula`).
**FIXED.** A block cell AutoCAD wrote (`171 2`, then `92 0`, `340`, `144`, `179`) was written to a DWG of R2010 or later as a text cell: the writer read the block's handle only where it stood straight after the cell's turn, and AutoCAD writes it after the cell's overrides and its `92`. The block is kept now (the values of its attributes are still left out of a DWG), and the state of a cell in the TABLECONTENT reaches the DWG's cells.
**NEW.** XLINE Offset in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 asks it (probed through its console): `Specify offset distance or [Through] <Through>:`, `Select a line object:` (a line, ray, xline or the straight segment of a polyline nearest the pick; anything else is `No usable object selected`) and `Specify side to offset:` or `Specify through point:`, an xline made at each until Enter. A line from (0, 0) to (10, 5) offset 5 to its left gives the xline based at (-2.2361, 4.4721) along (0.8944, 0.4472), as AutoCAD listed it; the distance or Through is the default of the next run. XLINE Ang also has Reference (`Enter angle of xline (0) or [Reference]:`), the angle counted from a line object. The Ang prompt used to omit `or [Reference]`.
**NEW.** REVERSE in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 does it: lines, polylines (lightweight, 2D and 3D) and splines run the other way, each bulge turned over and each segment's widths swapped, `Object direction has been reversed.` once for the run. A helix is passed over: the presenter does not read one.
**FIXED.** PEDIT Reverse of a closed polyline kept its first vertex where it was; AutoCAD 2021 (and its REVERSE) puts the vertices in the other order throughout, so the square (0, 0), (10, 0), (10, 10) becomes (10, 10), (10, 0), (0, 0). PEDIT Reverse and REVERSE share one body now.
**NEW.** SETBYLAYER and the variable SETBYLAYERMODE in the presenter, in the words of AutoCAD 2021's own string table: `Current active settings:`, `Select objects or [Settings]:`, `Change ByBlock to ByLayer? [Yes/No] <Yes>:`, `Include blocks? [Yes/No] <Yes>:` and `1 object modified, 2 objects did not need to be changed.` Colour, linetype, lineweight, transparency, material and (with named plot styles) plot style are set to ByLayer; ByBlock ones only where asked; with blocks included the objects of the block definitions and the attributes are changed too. Settings is the typed form of the dialog (`Enter a property to toggle [Color/LType/LWeight/Transparency/Material/PStyle] <done>:`), and the variable holds the bits (255 at first). AutoCAD's console runs no SETBYLAYER, so the flow and the count of nested objects are read from its strings and help, not probed.
**NEW.** CHPROP in the presenter (`Enter property to change [Color/LAyer/LType/ltScale/LWeight/Thickness/TRansparency/Material/Annotative]:`, probed through AutoCAD 2021's console), sharing its questions with CHANGE's Properties option, which keeps Elev. A drawing of named plot styles has PLotstyle in both.
**NEW.** CHSPACE in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks it (probed through a layout and a viewport): objects move between model space (through the viewport) and the paper, scaled and placed as the viewport shows them (`Set the SOURCE viewport active and press ENTER to continue.:`, `Ignoring 3 selected viewport(s)`, `1 object(s) changed from MODEL space to PAPER space.`, `Objects were scaled by a factor of 0.1 to maintain visual appearance.`). A twisted viewport turns the objects with its view. `** Command not allowed in Model Tab **` on the Model tab.
**NEW.** BURST and TXTEXP, the Express Tools commands, in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's own BURST.LSP and TXTEXP.LSP do them. BURST explodes block references with their attributes kept as TEXTs of the values they show, what is on layer 0 going to the reference's layer and what is ByBlock taking its colour and linetype. TXTEXP turns TEXT and MTEXT into polylines on layer 0: SHX strokes as open polylines, TrueType letters as closed polylines of their outlines (read from the font's `glyf` table, curves cut into six pieces each), where AutoCAD goes through a metafile.
**NEW.** Associative arrays and ARRAYEDIT in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 stores and edits them (checked against AutoCAD itself: its console made arrays and its `AssocArray` API read back what was written here). ARRAYRECT, ARRAYPOLAR and ARRAYPATH (and the types of ARRAY) with ASsociative Yes make one INSERT of an anonymous block of items (an INSERT of the source block for each item, the source objects held in it from the base point) and, in the drawing's associative network, an `ACDBASSOCACTION` with an `ACDBASSOCARRAYACTIONBODY` (the kind of parameters, each item's matrix and INSERT, the INSERT's matrix), the values by name, dependencies on the blocks, the INSERT and the path curve, and the `BaseNormal`, `Origin`, `basePoint` and `RowProfile` parameters; levels and the elevation between rows are built in them. AutoCAD 2021 loaded the DXF of 8 arrays made here (rectangular with levels and elevation, polar clockwise and unrotated with rows and levels, path along a line from its end, an arc by Divide, a polyline of lines and arcs of both senses, a circle with two source objects, an edited, a copied and a moved and turned one): each was an associative array with the same counts, spacings and items (origin and X axis of every one), the action up to date, AUDIT 0 errors. The arrays of 34 DXF files AutoCAD 2021 wrote (rectangular with a row axis angle, polar clockwise or unrotated, path from the end, by Divide, unaligned, Vector and Normal tangents, over a line, arc, circle and polyline) are read back, the items made again from the parameters equal to AutoCAD's own matrices to a millionth. ARRAYEDIT asks `Select array:` and the options of the kind as AutoCAD's console does (Source, REPlace, Base point, Rows, Columns, Levels, RESet, eXit for a rectangular array; Items, Angle between, Fill angle, ROTate items for a polar one; Method, Items, Align items, Z direction for a path), each change one undo step with the items made again over the same INSERT: 3 columns 20 apart edited to 5 columns 40 apart stand at 0, 40, 80, 120 and 160. EXPLODE breaks an array into the source objects of each item; ERASE takes the action out of the network; MOVE, ROTATE and SCALE keep the array and its stored matrix; COPY and MIRROR make an array of its own; a path curve moved or stretched writes the array along it again. Selecting one associative array shows the contextual Array tab (Type, Columns or Items, Rows, Levels, Properties with Base Point, Reset Array, Rotate Items, Clockwise, Align Items, Divide), a value written in it one undo step named ARRAYEDIT. Written to DWG an array keeps its picture and loses its association (the objects of the network have no DWG layout yet); not built: Source and ARRAYCLOSE, replacing a single item, item overrides and the grips of an array. ASsociative still starts at No (ARRAYASSOCIATIVITY is kept and not read), so an array is separate objects until it answers Yes.
**NEW.** FIELD and UPDATEFIELD in the presenter, with fields as AutoCAD 2021 keeps them (the words every field gave for its format and the FIELD objects written were probed through its console; it has no FIELD or UPDATEFIELD, so their prompts are the presenter's). FIELD shows the Field dialog: the categories All, Date & Time, Document, Linked, Objects, Other and Plot, the names in each (CreateDate, Date, PlotDate, SaveDate; Author, Comments, Filename, Filesize, HyperlinkBase, Keywords, LastSavedBy, Subject, Title; Formula, Object with Select object and the properties of the object picked; DieselExpression, SystemVariable; Login, PageSetupName, PaperSize, PlotDeviceName, PlotOrientation, PlotScale, PlotStyleTable), the options of the field chosen, its preview and its field expression; OK asks `Specify start point of multiline text [Height/Justify]:` and makes an MTEXT of the field. A date is written by its letters (`M/d/yyyy h:mm tt` is 11/17/2026 3:21 AM), a number by `%lu` (scientific, decimal, engineering, architectural, fractional), `%pr`, `%ps[prefix,suffix]`, `%ct8[factor]`, `%ds`, `%th` and `%zs` (an area of 314.159265 is 314.16, 3.142E+02, A=314.16mm2 or 314 1/4; 50 inches `%lu4%pr0` is 4'-2"), an angle by `%au` (53.13 degrees is 53d8', 59.03g, 0.93r or N 36d52' E), words by `%tc`, a file name by `%fn`; a formula (`2*3+1` is 7, `(3+4)/2` 3.500000) and a DIESEL expression (`$(if,$(>,2,1),yes,no)`) are worked out; a field that cannot be shows `####`. UPDATEFIELD asks `Select objects:` and evaluates the fields of the TEXTs and MTEXTs selected again (`1 field(s) found. 1 field(s) updated.`, one undo step): the area of a circle changes in its text only then, or where FIELDEVAL says.
**NEW.** Fields in the MTEXT editor and in TEXTEDIT. The Field button of the Text Editor tab's Insert panel (greyed before) and Ctrl+F show the Field dialog and put the field at the caret as one place, shown as the words it came to on a grey ground and written as its code; a double click on a field is Edit Field; the right-click has Insert Field, Edit Field and Convert Field To Text. A TEXT edited in place shows its fields as their codes. The words an edit ends with make the fields, evaluate them and write the FIELD objects (the ACAD_FIELD dictionary of the extension dictionary and the drawing's ACAD_FIELDLIST), so that AutoCAD 2021 opens the drawing with live fields: its console read and saved the fields the presenter wrote, in a DXF and a DWG of R2004, R2007 and R2018, as the same groups.
**NEW.** FIELDEVAL and FIELDDISPLAY. FIELDEVAL (0 to 31, 31 at the start, kept in the drawing as a variable of its dictionary) holds the bits that evaluate fields on their own: 1 when the drawing is opened, 2 when it is saved, 4 when it is plotted, 8 for eTransmit, 16 on REGEN (a field made in the dialog is evaluated in every one, the date too; a field that cannot be evaluated keeps what it showed). FIELDDISPLAY 1, the start, draws the box of a text with a field on a light grey ground that is never plotted; 0 draws none. The Contents row of Properties sets plain words and takes a field out.
**FIXED.** A DWG with a field of an object's property (`\AcObjProp Object(...).Area`, the area, centre, layer or name of an object) read to a drawing with every such FIELD left out and its text field pointing at nothing: the values of the types point (16, 32) and object (64) were not read, and the object handle of the value (`ObjectPropertyId`) was not written. AutoCAD 2021's DWG of 38 such fields reads to the 153 FIELD and FIELDLIST records of its own DXF, and a DXF of them written as a DWG of R2004, R2007 and R2018 is read back by AutoCAD 2021 with each field resolved to its object.
**CHANGED.** `SetField` of a TEXT, MTEXT, attribute or dimension writes the FIELD objects as AutoCAD 2021 writes a field it has not evaluated, group for group (it was the DXF reference's reading of them: a text field in the state 5 with its `ACFD_FIELDTEXT_CHECKSUM` of the words the text has, each field in the state 37 shown as `####`, a date to be evaluated on demand only, the format of R2004 under group 4, no flags before R2007) and lists the fields in the drawing's ACAD_FIELDLIST, made where the drawing has none; the words of the text are still not changed. The checksum of words is the code of each letter times its place from one: 7540 for "Drawn 17/11/2026".
**NEW.** Drawing templates in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 has them. NEW shows Select Template: the `.dwt`, `.dwg` and `.dxf` files of the template folder with the description each was saved with, Browse for another folder, and Open with no Template - Metric or Imperial; the new drawing is Drawing1.dwg and takes the template's layers, styles, blocks, layouts with their page setups and variables as they are. With FILEDIA 0 NEW asks `Enter template file name or [. (for none)] <acadiso.dwt>:` (a name with no extension is a `.dwt`, looked for as typed then in the template folder; `acadiso` and `acad` stand for the built-in metric and imperial templates; a period asks `Enter measurement [English/Metric] <Metric>:`). QNEW, the quick access New button, Ctrl+N and the start screen start from the default template of Global settings without asking, the built-in metric template where none is set or found. The imperial template is new (`CadTemplate.CreateImperial`: inches, MEASUREMENT 0, limits 12 by 9, text 0.2, the dimension style Standard current with AutoCAD's own values in the header, as the metric one has ISO-25). `CadTemplate.FindIn`, `Find` and `DescriptionOf` list a folder's templates (by name, then extension), find one as typed and read the description of a `.dwt`. Global settings > Save and export has Template settings, the template folder (default `%AppData%\GeometryHelper\Drawing\Template`) and the default template for QNEW. `DrawingTemplateTests` (10), `DrawingTemplateWindowTests` (21).
**NEW.** SAVEAS to a drawing template. Save Drawing As lists AutoCAD Drawing Template (*.dwt) after the DWG types and the application menu's Save As › Drawing Template opens it with that type chosen, in the template folder and with the drawing's name given `.dwt`; Template Options asks the description and the measurement (English or Metric), and a DWG of AutoCAD 2018 is written with the description in its template section and MEASUREMENT as chosen; the drawing is then known by the `.dwt`, and Save writes it again with the same description. With FILEDIA 0 SAVEAS Template asks the file (`Save drawing as <Drawing1.dwt>:`), `Enter template description:` and `Enter measurement [English/Metric] <Metric>:`; it said `A drawing template (*.dwt) is not written here.` before. `CadDocument.SaveAsTemplate(path, description, metric, progress)`, `CadDocument.TemplateDescription` and `CadExportJob.Template` are new; a file named `.dwt` saved through `CadDrawingFile` is written as a DWG.
**NEW.** PUBLISH and -PUBLISH in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's Batch Plot: the Publish dialog (the Output tab's Batch Plot button and Print, Batch Plot in the application menu) lists the Model and layouts of the drawing open as `plan-level2-Model`, `plan-level2-Layout1`, each with a Page Setup (its own, one of the drawing's, or one imported from another drawing) and a Status; Add Sheets reads other DWG and DXF files with the presenter's readers, Remove, Remove All, Move Up and Move Down change the list, Include Model and Layouts choose what Add Sheets lists, and Publish to is the plotter named in the page setup (a printer this computer has, else a PDF of its own) or PDF, one multi-sheet file of a page each, the size of its own sheet, or a file each, with copies, output folder and file name. Load List and Save List read and write the .dsd sheet list of AutoCAD (the sections and keys read from AutoCAD 2021 and open sources, `Type` as its `SheetType`, what a list holds besides kept as it was, DWF and DWFx read as PDF with a note); -PUBLISH asks `Enter name of sheet list <file.dsd>:` and publishes the list at once. A drawing open with Layout1 on ISO A3 and Layout2 on ISO A1 and a file added with a layout on ISO A4 are one PDF of three pages of 1 190.5512 by 841.8898, 2 383.937 by 1 683.7795 and 841.8898 by 595.2756 points (`PublishWindowTests`, `PublishTests`). `CadPdfWriter.WritePages` takes the drawing of each page. Publish in background is a box that does nothing, and DWF and DWFx have no writer.
**NEW.** Plot style tables as files in the presenter: `.ctb` (colour-dependent, 255 styles) and `.stb` (named) tables read and written by `CadPlotStyleSheet` in the layout AutoCAD 2021 keeps them (the head `PIAFILEVERSION_2.0,CTBVER1,compress` or `STBVER1`, three numbers, the zlib stream of the text of nested blocks), each style with its colour, dithering, grayscale, pens, screening, linetype, adaptive adjustment, lineweight, line end, line join, fill and description; a table read and written again is the same text byte for byte, and the same file on the same runtime (the tables the presenter makes, 9 of them, and one edited in every way, are tested), and a note after a number and a screening of 255 in an AutoCAD table are read. A plot applies a table's colour, grayscale, screening (red at 50 per cent is #FF8080), lineweight, linetype and line end and join in a PDF, an image and a printout (`CadPlotStyleResolver`: a colour-dependent table by the colour of AutoCAD's index, a true colour by the nearest; a named table by the style an entity names, else its layer's, else Normal), and `monochrome.ctb`, `grayscale.ctb` and `acad.ctb` plot every one of the 255 colours and the true colours tried as the three tables made in code did. The tables live in a folder, Global settings > Save and export > Plot style tables folder (`PlotStyles` beside the settings file where empty), where the presenter writes its own `acad`, `monochrome`, `grayscale`, `Screening 25%`, 50 and 75 `.ctb` and `acad`, `monochrome`, `grayscale` `.stb`, never replacing one the user edited (none is a file of AutoCAD's); the Plot and Page Setup dialogs list the `.ctb` or `.stb` files of it by the drawing's `$PSTYLEMODE` with New... and Edit...; the Plot Style Table Editor has the General, Table View and Form View tabs, Save & Close, Save As... and, for a named table, Add Style and Delete Style; STYLESMANAGER and File > Print > Manage Plot Styles show the folder. New: `CadPlotStyle`, `CadPlotStyleSheet`, `CadPlotStyleFolder`, `CadPlotStyleResolver`, `CadPlotPen`, `CadPlotSettings.StyleSheet` and `EffectiveStyleSheet`, `CadDocument.PlotStyleFolder`, `GlobalSettings.PlotStyleFolder`, `CadStylesManagerRequest`. Not done: Edit Lineweights, the wizard's PCP and PC2 sources, CONVERTCTB, CONVERTPSTYLES, the fill style of a filled area, and the pens, dithering and adaptive adjustment a PDF cannot use.
**CHANGED.** `CadPlotSettings.StyleTable` is now a way in to `StyleSheet`, the file name of the table (group 7), which a page setup keeps whatever the name: `acad.ctb` or `site.ctb` was read as none and written back as none before; they are kept and plotted. -PLOT's `Enter plot style table name` lists and takes the tables of the document's folder, `<.>` for none (its default is the page setup's table), and the Page Setup Manager's details name the file. File > Print > Manage Plot Styles runs STYLESMANAGER, greyed before.
**NEW.** The Layer manager of the presenter lists Transparency, Plot Style, Plot and Description, and has AutoCAD 2021's filter tree. Transparency (0 to 90 per cent, in the cell), Plot (the printer icon) and Description are edits of the layer through `CadLayerEditor`, one undo step each; Plot Style reads `Color_7` and is grey in a drawing plotted by colour and is a list of the drawing's plot style names in one of named plot styles (`DxfLayerTableRecord.PlotStyleName`, `CadLayerEditor.SetPlotStyle`, and -LAYER PStyle, offered only in such a drawing: `Enter Plot Style Name or [?] <Normal>:`). The tree under All holds the filters the drawing keeps, nested as AutoCAD nests them, and All Used Layers, Unreconciled New Layers and Viewport Overrides; Invert filter and Apply to layers toolbar (the layer box lists only the layers of the filter) are in it. New Property Filter opens Layer Filter Properties (a name, rows of cells for every column, a live preview); a group filter is given layers by dragging them, "Add to Group Filter" or Select Layers; filters are renamed, changed, converted to a group and deleted, and the filter chosen is kept in the drawing as the current one. A filter is the XRECORD AutoCAD 2021 keeps (ACLYDICTIONARY: `AcLyLayerFilter` or `AcLyLayerGroup`, name 300, expression 301 as `NAME=="A*" AND COLOR=="1"`, layers 330, current 290, nested filters in the extension dictionary of its record) and AutoCAD read drawings of ours with the same tree, in DXF and DWG; the expressions pass the layers its own `LayerFilter.Filter` passed (`CadLayerFilters`, `CadLayerExpression`). The window is 1 380 wide (1 700 in a layout, the table scrolling sideways). Not here: the .ctb and .stb tables (the plot style names are those of the drawing's dictionary), and Select Layers takes the objects selected before the dialog is opened, where AutoCAD hides it and asks for them (`LayerFilterTests`, `LayerManagerFiltersTests`, `DxfLayerPlotStyleTests`).
**NEW.** LAYMRG, LAYDEL, LAYCUR and COPYTOLAYER in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks them (probed through it: the prompts, the warnings, the refusals and the messages). LAYMRG and LAYDEL (and -LAYMRG and -LAYDEL) pick layers by an object on each or by Name until Enter (`Selected layers: DOOR,TRIM.`, Undo), refuse the current layer and layer 0, show the warning and ask `Do you wish to continue? [Yes/No] <No>:`; LAYMRG puts every object of the layers on the target layer (model space, the layouts, the blocks' definitions and the attributes) and deletes them, LAYDEL erases the objects and the layers, one undo step, a layer a viewport freezes thawed there first. LAYCUR puts the objects selected on the current layer (`2 objects changed to layer "B" (the current layer).`). COPYTOLAYER copies them onto a layer named, listed with ? or taken from an object with =, made where the drawing has none (`Do you want to create it?`), and moves the copies by two points or Displacement. `CadLayerEditor.Merge` and `CadLayerEditor.DeleteWithObjects` do the same without the questions. A drawing with a line on WALL, a line and a circle on DOOR and a block holding a line on DOOR has all four on WALL after DOOR is merged into it (`LayerMergeAndDeleteCommandTests`, `LayerCurrentAndCopyToLayerCommandTests`). The dialogs the plain names open in AutoCAD are not built: they ask on the command line.
**NEW.** -DIMSTYLE and DIMUPDATE in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks them: the current style and its overrides (the variables that differ from the style's own), then ANnotative, Save (the variables, overrides and all, kept as a style that becomes current; `That name is already in use, redefine it? <N>:`), Restore (a style, or the style and overrides of a dimension picked), STatus and Variables (every variable with its value and what it is, or the overrides of a dimension), Apply (the current style and overrides given to the dimensions, leaders and frames selected, drawn anew) and ?. DIMUPDATE, the Annotate tab's Update, is Apply. With DIMTXT 6 over a style of 2.5, a dimension updated has its words 6 high (`DimStyleTypedCommandTests`). DIMALTMZF, DIMALTMZS, DIMMZF and DIMMZS, which AutoCAD lists, are not kept by the library and are not listed.
**NEW.** SCALETEXT, JUSTIFYTEXT and TXT2MTXT in the presenter. SCALETEXT scales each TEXT, MTEXT and attribute about a base point of its own as AutoCAD 2021's console asks and does it (probed: `Enter a base point option for scaling [Existing/Left/Center/Middle/Right/TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR] <Existing>:`, `Specify new model height or [Paper height/Match object/Scale factor] <2.5000>:`, `1 objects changed`): "HELLO" 5 high and 23.33 wide from (10, 10) taken to a height of 10 about Center starts at (-1.67, 10) with its centre still on (21.67, 10), about Middle at (10, 7.5), about TL keeps its top left; an MTEXT has its width scaled with it; Match object takes the height of a text picked, Scale factor a factor or a Reference pair, Paper height the sheet height of annotative text (`1 non-annotative objects ignored` of the rest). JUSTIFYTEXT gives every text a justification and leaves it drawn where it was (`Enter a justification option [Left/Align/Fit/Center/Middle/Right/TL/TC/TR/ML/MC/MR/BL/BC/BR] <Left>:`): the same "HELLO" justified Right is held by (33.33, 10), the end of its baseline, its first point kept; an MTEXT is attached by the matching corner of its words (Left the bottom left, Center the bottom middle, Right the bottom right, Middle the centre). TXT2MTXT combines the TEXT and MTEXT selected into one MTEXT at the top left of the top text, one paragraph each from the top down, the originals erased (the console runs no TXT2MTXT, so its Settings are the presenter's own: width, paragraphs or one run-on paragraph, erase, order). `TextToolsCommandTests` (33).
**NEW.** ATTDISP in the presenter (`Enter attribute visibility setting [Normal/ON/OFF] <Normal>:`, `Regenerating model.`): Normal shows the attributes that are not invisible, ON all of them, OFF none, every space drawn again, one undo step; the display read invisible ones as hidden whatever the drawing said. -ATTEDIT answered No to "Edit attributes one at a time?" edits the values together as AutoCAD 2021's does, where it said "not built here": `Edit only attributes visible on screen? [Yes/No] <Y>:`, the block, tag and value specifications, `6 attributes selected.`, `Enter string to change:` and `Enter new string:`; every occurrence is replaced, case kept apart ("HELLO ABC abc ABC" with ABC taken to xyz is "HELLO xyz abc xyz"), an empty string to change puts the new one at the front of every value, an empty new string takes the old one out. `AttributeDisplayTests` (6).
**NEW.** The MTEXT editor's Background Mask dialog, behind the Mask button of the Style panel and Background mask… under the colour, both greyed before: Use background mask, the border offset factor (1.0 to 5.0, 1.5 to start with), Fill Color with Use drawing background color or a colour of Select Color. The mask is shown in the editor at once and written with the words (group 90 flags 1 and 2, 45, 63 and 421), one undo step; public as `CadMTextMask`, `CadInPlaceEdit.NewMask` and `CadMTextEditorLayout.SetMask`. `MTextMaskTests` (7).
**FIXED.** A TEXT justified Middle (72 of 4) was drawn with its baseline on its point; AutoCAD 2021 holds it by the middle of its height too ("HELLO" 5 high held by (21.67, 12.5) stands on the baseline y = 10), so that it came out half its height too high. `JustifyText_KeepsATextWhereItIsDrawn_ForEveryJustification_ThoughTurned("Middle")` (red before).
**NEW.** More commands run inside another, as AutoCAD 2021 runs them transparently (probed through its console: 'DIST, 'ID, 'PDMODE, 'CLAYER, 'COLOR, 'LAYER, 'LINETYPE, 'LWEIGHT, 'UNITS typed at LINE's next point, and the nesting): DIST, ID, LAYER, COLOR, LINETYPE, LWEIGHT, UNITS, QUICKCALC, DSETTINGS and TEXTSCR join PAN, ZOOM, CAL, SETVAR and the settings, and the name of any system variable typed with an apostrophe asks its new value after ">>" (`'PDMODE`, `>>Enter new value for PDMODE <0>:`) as SETVAR does. A command that shows a dialog runs its command-line form while it waits, as AutoCAD's console does: 'LAYER asks -LAYER's options, 'COLOR, 'LINETYPE, 'LWEIGHT and 'UNITS those of -COLOR, -LINETYPE, -LWEIGHT and -UNITS. The command interrupted resumes with its prompt and the last point it had (a transparent ID does not move the point the line is drawn from, as in AutoCAD), and a fifth command inside four is "Commands may not be nested more than 4 deep", its text going to the prompt. 'MEASUREGEOM is still "** That command may not be invoked transparently **", as AutoCAD says. `TransparentCommandTests` (11).
**NEW.** 55 system variables typed by name or through SETVAR, with the range, the refusal and the start AutoCAD 2021's console gives them (every range probed): LUNITS 1 to 5, LUPREC 0 to 8, AUNITS 0 to 4, AUPREC 0 to 8, ANGBASE, ANGDIR, INSUNITS 0 to 24 and MEASUREMENT, UNITMODE, PLINEWID, PLINEGEN, FILLMODE, ELEVATION, THICKNESS, LIMCHECK, SPLFRAME, QTEXTMODE, ATTMODE, SPLINETYPE, SPLINESEGS, USERI1 to USERI5 and USERR1 to USERR5, kept in the drawing's header as one undo step; HPNAME, HPSCALE, HPANG, HPLAYER, HPASSOC, HPDOUBLE, HPGAPTOL, HPORIGINMODE, DIMLAYER, CIRCLERAD, POLYSIDES, TRIMEXTENDMODE, CMDECHO, EXPERT, HIGHLIGHT, PICKAUTO, PICKDRAG, OSNAPZ and ARRAYASSOCIATIVITY, kept by the session; SAVETIME and ZOOMFACTOR of Global settings; DISTANCE, AREA and PERIMETER, read only, from DIST and AREA; LASTPOINT, in the UCS. Where the presenter has the behaviour the variable drives it: PLINEWID is the width PLINE starts at, PLINEGEN is given to the polylines PLINE, RECTANG and POLYGON make, FILLMODE 0 draws solids, wide polylines and solid or gradient hatches by their outlines (every space drawn again), HPNAME, HPSCALE, HPANG, HPLAYER and the rest are the settings the next HATCH makes its hatch with (the dialog and -HATCH hold the same), DIMLAYER is the layer new dimensions go on (DIM's LAyer sets the same), CIRCLERAD, POLYSIDES and TRIMEXTENDMODE are what CIRCLE, POLYGON, TRIM and EXTEND start with, ZOOMFACTOR 60 is the 1.5 of the wheel step (1 + ZOOMFACTOR / 120), SAVETIME the autosave minutes (Global settings keeps 240 at most), and LUNITS, LUPREC, AUNITS, AUPREC, ANGBASE and ANGDIR are what UNITS sets and the points typed are read and written by. The others keep their value and do nothing else, as the presenter has no behaviour for them. A variable AutoCAD refuses is refused in its words (`Requires an integer between 1 and 5.`, `Cannot set PLINEWID to that value.`, `Cannot set HPNAME to that value.`). `MoreSystemVariableTests` (17), `SaveTimeZoomFactorVariableTests` (2).
**NEW.** ARRAYPATH and the PAth type of ARRAY in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks it (probed through its standard input over a line of 10 and paths of 100 and of two segments: the prompts, which end of the path the items begin at, where each lands and how it is turned), where it said "Path arrays are not built yet": the objects, `Select path curve:` (a line, arc, circle, ellipse, polyline or spline), and the options Method (Measure by a distance, with `Maximum items = 4` and Fill entire path, or Divide by a number of items), Base point, Tangent direction (two points, or Normal), Items, Rows (with Total and the incrementing elevation), Levels, Align items, Z direction and eXit, until Enter makes it, one undo step, the items as separate objects as ARRAYRECT's are. The items follow the path from the end nearest the pick, each carrying the place of the objects relative to the path's start and turned with the path: a line from (0, 0) to (10, 0) measured by 60 along a path that runs along Y = 100 and then up X = 100 has its third item from (200, 120) to (200, 130); rows lie to the left of the way the path runs and levels above. Associative arrays and the grips of an array are not built. The Array button of Home › Modify has Path Array in its menu.
**NEW.** OVERKILL and -OVERKILL in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console runs -OVERKILL (probed over lines, arcs, circles, points and polylines: what is a duplicate and what an overlap, which object stays, the tolerance, Ignore and the polyline options, and the words it writes): `1 duplicate(s) deleted` and `2 overlapping object(s) or segment(s) deleted`. Objects of the same place and properties are duplicates and the later stays; on one line or circle an object within another is deleted and those that overlap in part or meet end to end become one (lines 0 to 100 and 50 to 150 become 0 to 150, arcs of 300 to 40 and 20 to 100 degrees one of 300 to 100, arcs that make a whole circle a circle); a segment of a polyline takes part like a line, cut out of its polyline where it goes, and repeated vertices and collinear segments of a polyline join up. The options are Ignore (the nine properties), tOlerance (half the distance two points may be apart: 0.04 apart go at 0.1, 0.05 apart stay), optimize Plines (with segment width and Break polyline), combine parTial overlap, combine Endtoend and Associativity, kept in the new `CadCommandSession.Overkill` from one run to the next. OVERKILL shows the Delete Duplicate Objects dialog (the tolerance, nine Ignore boxes, six options; `OverkillWindow`, `OverkillViewModel`, `MainViewModel.ShowOverkill`) over the same settings. New public types: `CadOverkillSettings`, `CadOverkillIgnore`, `CadOverkillResult`, `CadOverkillRequest`. Polyline arc segments are compared whole only, and "Maintain associative objects" is kept as a setting and not acted on.
**NEW.** RECTANG asks its options in the presenter as AutoCAD 2021's console does (probed through its standard input: the prompts, their defaults, the modes line and the polylines it draws): Chamfer, Elevation, Fillet, Thickness and Width at the first prompt, Area, Dimensions and Rotation at the second. The modes stay for the next RECTANG and are listed when it starts (`Current rectangle modes:  Chamfer=1.0000 x 2.0000  Elevation=5.0000  Thickness=4.0000  Width=0.5000`); a chamfer and a fillet shut each other out, each offering the other's distance. A chamfer of 1 and 2 on the rectangle from (10, 10) to (40, 30) is the eight vertices (10, 11), (12, 10), (39, 10), (40, 12), (40, 29), (38, 30), (11, 30), (10, 28); a fillet of 2 the same points with arcs of a bulge of tan(22.5 degrees), its sign following the winding; where a side is too short the rectangle is the plain one of eight vertices, two at each corner, as AutoCAD draws it. Area works the other side out of the area with the corners' share added back (200 on a length of 20 gives a width of 10.6 with a chamfer of 2 and 3), Dimensions gives the sides and the other corner only the quadrant, Rotation (typed or by Pick points) turns the sides about the first corner and stays as a mode. `RectangleOptionsTests` (18).
**NEW.** WIPEOUT in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks and writes it: `Specify first point or [Frames/Polyline] <Polyline>:`, the points of a closed outline (`Specify next point or [Close/Undo]:`), Polyline (`Select a closed polyline:`, refused with `The polyline must be closed and made up of only line segments.` where it is open or of arcs, then `Erase polyline? [Yes/No] <No>:`, the erase in the same undo step) and Frames (`Enter mode [ON/OFF/Display but not plot] <ON>:`), and the variable WIPEOUTFRAME 0, 1 or 2, one undo step. The command frames the points in the square on their own box at its lowest corner, as AutoCAD's command writes it, where `DxfWipeout.SetFrom` lays it on the box and the origin both; the first wipeout makes the variables of wipeouts. The frames of wipeouts are drawn in the entity's colour over their mask until WIPEOUTFRAME is 0, where they were never drawn. `WipeoutCommandTests` (15).
**NEW.** `DxfWipeoutVariables`, the WIPEOUTVARIABLES of a drawing (the entry ACAD_WIPEOUT_VARS of the named object dictionary): `ShowFrames` reads and writes group 70 as 0 or 1, and `GetWipeoutVariables(database)` makes them where the drawing has none, frames shown, its class listed, as AutoCAD 2021 does when WIPEOUT Frames is first used. A drawing read gives the object as one of that type; it was a `DxfUnknownObject`. WIPEOUTFRAME 2, shown and not plotted, is written as 1, as AutoCAD 2021 writes it. `DxfWipeoutVariablesTests` (4).
**NEW.** OOPS in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console runs it (probed after ERASE, BLOCK and WBLOCK): the objects the last ERASE, BLOCK or WBLOCK took out come back, in the space they were erased from, with no prompt and no message, in one undo step. Only the last set comes back: a second OOPS does nothing, and neither does one after the erase was undone (nothing is put back twice); the polyline WIPEOUT Polyline erases is not among them. The objects come back as copies, so their handles are new. `OopsCommandTests` (9).
**FIXED.** The share told while a DWG of 4 096 objects or more is read could jump from 0.045 to 0.54 with nothing between: its objects are decoded in chunks of 512 on several threads and only the calling thread told, so when the others took the chunks before it ended its own a file of 6 030 objects (12 chunks) told 0, 0.045, 0.54 on a machine of 24 cores, and a stop asked for by a share (the bar, a test that cancels at 0.2) was answered only at 0.54. Each thread now tells the share as it ends a chunk, one at a time, each adding its own chunk, and nothing after a stop is asked for: some ten shares come within that stretch, a step of a chunk (0.04) apart, and a stop told by a share is answered within one. `DisplaySpeed26Tests` (the stop test red before, one added for the steps).
**CHANGED.** `TransformBy` of a TEXT, ATTDEF or ATTRIB held by a second point (centred, right, middle, aligned, fitted, bottom, middle or top of its ink) keeps the words readable under a mirror, as AutoCAD 2021's does; it was mirrored with its normal turned over and its words backwards. Probed in its console on 196 texts of 14 justifications, in 4 planes at 3 angles, under 7 mirrors (a vertical and a level line, a slanting one, a mirror across the plane of the text, across a tilted plane and one turned about z), and on the same texts moved, turned and turned about x: every group but the two points is the same (an angle out of the plane of the text stays as ezdxf gives it, -26.6 where AutoCAD writes 333.4), and the points are the same where a font is not asked. The first point (10) is worked out from the second (11) first, as `Realign` does, and both points are carried by the turn-over and the mirror: "ABC" 3 high centred on (30, 45), its first point (26, 45), across x = 40 stands at (45.555, 45) held at (49.555, 45) (AutoCAD turns it over about its own measure of the ink, 8.445 wide; the drawing's fonts measure 8 in txt.shx, so there the points are (46, 45) and (50, 45)); across y = 30 it stands at (26, 12) held at (30, 12). A text whose two points are the ends of its baseline (aligned, fitted, or held by its right end) is turned over across the middle of the two points, so that the first is the second mirrored and the second the first, with no font to ask: aligned on (20, 40) and (40, 48) across x = 40 it runs from (60, 40) to (40, 48) turned to 338.2 degrees, and held by its right end at (30, 45) from (22, 45) it stands at (50, 45) held at (58, 45), as AutoCAD wrote them. One held by its middle (72 of 4), turned across its upright, is mirrored as it stands: its second point is the mirror of the old, and its first stays where the mirror alone takes it ((26, 43.5) held at (30, 45) becomes (54, 43.5) held at (50, 45)), AutoCAD's own result. Across its baseline each is turned over about the middle of its height like the rest. Where no font measures the ink the turn-over needs, the text is written backwards or upside down, it is an attribute of several lines, or its justification is 3, 4 or 5 with a vertical mode (which AutoCAD reads with none), it is mirrored as before. `DxfJustifiedTextMirrorTests` (8, 7 red before).
**CHANGED.** `TransformBy` of an annotative TEXT and MTEXT keeps the words readable under a mirror in every context, as AutoCAD 2021's does (24 annotative texts and 18 annotative MTEXTs of 3 planes at 1:1 and 1:2 under 10 transformations: every group of the records, and of the contexts but for the texts' ink and an angle out of its plane written a whole turn lower, the same). A TEXT turns each context over by the words at that context's height: "ABC" at 1:1 and 1:2 (3 and 6 high) at (20, 40) across x = 40 stands at 52 and 44, their ink 8 and 16 wide (AutoCAD, 8.445 and 16.89: 51.555 and 43.109), the record turned over as the default context. An MTEXT is turned over about its point in its record and in each context, each held by the other side of its box (1 becomes 3 in the record and in both contexts of one held by its top left) and its direction reversed in each; contexts were mirrored as the record was before, with their words backwards. `DxfAnnotativeMirrorTests` (3, red before).
**FIXED.** `TransformBy` of a POINT left its symbol angle (group 50) as it was; AutoCAD 2021 writes the angle the image of its x axis makes in the system of the new normal, from nought to a whole turn: 180 across x = 40 and across z = 0, 112.62 across a line at 56.31 degrees, 150 for a symbol of 30 degrees across x = 40, 30 for a turn of 30 degrees, and none where it is nought. Probed on 10 points of 5 planes and two angles under 10 transformations, with the matrix of `GeoTransform3.Mirror`, whose -0 made `NormalGroups` write an explicit normal (0, 0, 1) on a LINE, POINT, circle or arc that AutoCAD leaves with none: a nought below nought is nought now. `DxfMirror9Tests` (red before).
**FIXED.** `TransformBy` of an MTEXT left its direction (11) out wherever it equalled the world's x axis put into the new plane, and kept one the record had; AutoCAD 2021 leaves it out only where it is the world's x axis itself, and writes it otherwise (an MTEXT with none turned 25 degrees about y reads along (0.906, 0, -0.423) and is written with that 11; one along x of the normal (0, 1, 0) moved has its 11 of (1, 0, 0) taken out). `DxfMirror9Tests` (red before).
**FIXED.** `TransformBy` of a heavy POLYLINE (`DxfPolyline2d`) and a LEADER under a mirror turned the normal over where AutoCAD 2021 takes the image of the old one, as it does for a circle, an arc, a LWPOLYLINE and a SOLID, and the heavy POLYLINE kept its bulges where AutoCAD changes their sign: (60, 10), (80, 10), (80, 30) with the bulges 0, 0.5, -0.3 at the elevation 3 across x = 40 is (20, 10), (0, 10), (0, 30) with 0, -0.5, 0.3 and the normal (0, 0, 1), not (0, 0, -1) with the bulges as they were. Probed on 10 heavy polylines and 5 leaders of 5 planes under 10 transformations, every group the same but the groups AutoCAD adds. The presenter's MIRROR keeps what it drew but for the arrowhead of a leader, a triangle written from the other corner (compared on the display lists of 18 kinds of entity mirrored, MIRRTEXT 0 and 1, across three lines). `DxfMirror9Tests` (red before).
**CHANGED.** The sign of the half turn of a hatch's pattern angle (52), which AutoCAD 2021 writes as +180 or -180 by the sign of a nought in its sums (30 becomes 210 or -150, the same angle), is worked out as AutoCAD's sums come to it: the image of the old x axis along the new y axis, in the systems of the arbitrary axis algorithm, taking the sign of that sum. The rule it replaces (-180 for any normal pointing down before and after) was right for the normal (0, 0, -1) turned 280 to 350 degrees about x and wrong for the others: a probe of 14 normals under 117 turns about x, y and z (198 half turns of the pattern angle) found it wrong in 28 (a normal (0, -1, -1) turned 45 degrees about x is 210, not -150, a normal (-1, 0, 0) turned 100 degrees about y the same), and the new sum is the same as AutoCAD's in all 198, the hatch of the normal (0, 0, -1) among them. `DxfHatchHalfTurnTests` (5, 2 red before).
**NEW.** COPY has Array and mOde, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks them (probed): `Specify base point or [Displacement/mOde] <Displacement>:`, `Specify second point or [Array] <use first point as displacement>:`, and after each copy `Specify second point or [Array/Exit/Undo] <Exit>:`. Array asks `Enter number of items to array:` (2 to 32767, the original counted, `Requires an integer between 2 and 32767.` for the rest) and `Specify second point or [Fit]:`: a point is the step from one copy to the next (4 items and the point 30 along make copies at 30, 60 and 90), Fit puts the last copy at the point and the others evenly between (3 items to (207, 10) from (200, 0) put one at (203.5, 5)), and Array turns back to the step; the whole array is one entry for Undo. mOde sets the new variable COPYMODE (0 Multiple, the default; 1 Single, where COPY makes one copy and ends); in Single mode the base point prompt also offers `Multiple` for one run. `CopyArrayAndModeTests` (12 tests); the prompt and results were read from AutoCAD's console. Differences: the number offered the second time in a run reads `<3>` where AutoCAD writes `or [3]`, and the ghost while the second point is chosen shows one copy, not the array.
**NEW.** SELECTSIMILAR and ADDSELECTED, with the variable SELECTSIMILARMODE. SELECTSIMILAR asks `Select objects or [SEttings]:` (or takes the objects selected before it) and selects every object of the space of the same kind and, by the bits of SELECTSIMILARMODE, of the same Color (1), Layer (2), Linetype (4), Linetype scale (8), Lineweight (16), Plot style (32), Object style (64) or Name (128); 130, Layer and Name, is the default and 0 matches the kind alone, as AutoCAD 2021 does (probed on lines and circles: a line BYLAYER and one in the layer's colour are not alike under 1). SEttings shows the Select Similar Settings dialog, eight boxes that set the mode. ADDSELECTED asks `Select object:` and runs the command that draws that kind (`_.circle`) with the layer, colour, linetype, linetype scale and lineweight of the object as the drawing's own, which come back when it ends. The Edit menu's Add Selected and Select Similar run them. A keyword with lower-case letters before its capitals (mOde, eXit) is now taken by those letters and the capitals together (`MO`, `EX`) at every prompt. `SelectSimilarAndAddSelectedTests` (11 tests), `SelectSimilarWiringAndTextWindowTests`.
**NEW.** TEXTSCR, which F2 runs: the text window, the command history in one resizable list that follows the command line while it is open, with Copy (Ctrl+C) for the rows chosen or all of them; F2 or Esc inside it closes it. F2 is the 25th default key.
**NEW.** What was grey in the ribbon and the menus with a working command behind it is wired: Table (Home, Annotation, TABLE), Manage Attributes (BATTMAN) and Block Editor (BEDIT) of Insert, QuickCalc (QUICKCALC; in the Command menu it opens the palette beside the running command), Quick Properties (QUICKPROPERTIES), Add Selected and Select Similar of the Edit menu, Add Current Scale, Delete Current Scale and Add/Delete Scales... of Annotative Object Scale (AIOBJECTSCALEADD, AIOBJECTSCALEREMOVE, OBJECTSCALE on the objects selected), and Save As, Other Formats (EXPORT). Still grey, with no command behind them: SteeringWheels, Action Recorder, Convert PS to MS, Add to Group and Remove from Group (no GROUPEDIT), Group Edit, Synchronize Multiple-scale Positions, Edit Constraint, Set and Generate Boundary of a hatch, Edit Xref In-place, the underlay buttons, Edit Attribute Multiple (no global -ATTEDIT), Drawing Template and Batch Plot.
**NEW.** DIMBREAK Manual breaks an ordinate dimension and an arc length dimension as AutoCAD 2021 does, where the presenter kept the line of its picture nearest the middle of the two points and numbered it 3 for every dimension of these kinds. The leader of an ordinate is 0 (a leader jogged to the side has three legs: 0 the leg from the point, 1 the jog, 2 the last leg, numbered by where they stand from the point, so that a leg already cut in pieces is still one), the extension lines of an arc length dimension 0 at the first end of the length and 1 at the second, its arc 3. Probed in AutoCAD's console fed through standard input (about 100 breaks of ordinates of both datums, straight and jogged, and of arc length dimensions of 60 and 90 degrees, 250 out): the line broken is the one nearest the first point (a tie to the lesser number: a pick level with both rays of an arc of 90 degrees takes ray 0, one beside the jog and the last leg of a jogged leader takes the jog), both points are carried along it and the stretch between them is left out where at least one falls on what the dimension draws of the line. The X ordinate of (20, 30) with its leader to (20, 200), broken from (60, 70) to (60, 90), has its leader out from 70 to 90 (pieces from 30.0625 to 70 and from 90 to 200.09, 91 of 0); jogged 60 across, from (60, 100) to (60, 120), its first leg out from 100 to 120; an arc length dimension of an arc of 50 from 0 to 90 degrees put 250 out, from (100, 25) to (140, 35), its first ray cut from 100 to 140 (91 of 0), from (200, 100) to (150, 200) its arc cut from 0.4636 to 0.9273 radians (91 of 3), and on an arc of 60 degrees, whose rays run along the middle of the arc at 30 degrees, from (130, 10) to (200, 20), its first ray from (114.33, 37.141) to (171.16, 69.952). A break kept in the BREAKDATA is drawn again on the same line where the dimension is drawn anew. The numbers are those of 17 rows of picks about 20 units or more from the lines, all equal to AutoCAD's (on an arc AutoCAD carries a pick along its radius, which leaves the stretch cut as it is); a pick within about 15 units (a window 700 across) of such a line AutoCAD's console moves to its middle or its end before it breaks, the break of the leader above from (20, 70) to (20, 90) kept as one point at 115.076 and cutting nothing, which depends on its view and is not copied (the presenter takes the points as they are given). `DimBreakManualOrdinateArcRowsTests` (18, 17 of them red before the change, most on the line number alone).
**NEW.** `DxfDimension.GeometricExtents` gives the box of the dimension's picture where it stands, as AutoCAD 2021's does; it threw "has no shape the library reads" for every dimension. The block of the picture (`DimBlock`) placed as `Explode()` places it, the points of definition on the layer Defpoints (which `Explode()` leaves out) among it: a level dimension from (0, 0, 0) to (100, 0, 0), its line at y = 20, fills (0, 0, 0) to (100, 20.18, 0), the points at its ends reaching down to y = 0 and its extension lines up to 20.18; AutoCAD's box for the linear, aligned, angular, ordinate, radius, diameter and arc length dimensions of 8 probes are the same to 1E-6, and a dimension whose block holds nothing with extents throws, as AutoCAD throws. DIMBREAK Auto names the objects whose box meets the dimension's by it, where it measured the block by hand. `DxfDimensionAndMLeaderExtentsTests` (3 for the dimension, 2 red before; the third keeps the throw for a block with nothing in it).
**FIXED.** `DxfMLeader.GeometricExtents` counts the arrowheads and the words, as AutoCAD 2021 does, where it was the box of the vertices and the point of the words alone: the parts `Explode()` draws it with are in the box, and measured words (the drawing's `FontSearchPath`) with the landing gap more beyond them on the side away from their leader. A multileader from (0, 0) to a landing at (100, -1.25), words "TEXT" 2.5 high in txt.shx, arrowheads of 0.18 fills (0, -2.5, 0) to (109.706667, 0.027748, 0) in AutoCAD and in the library, where the points alone gave (0, -1.25) to (100.45, 0): the words 9.166667 wide past the landing, the gap of 0.09 after them, the arrowhead's corners 0.0277 above the line. Compared with AutoCAD on 12 multileaders (one and two leaders, a bend, the leader on the left or the right of the words, a landing gap of 0.5, a dogleg of 2, words 5 high), every box equal to 1E-6; with no font the words add nothing, as before. The one test of the old box (a multileader of the sample drawing, its second leader on the right of the words, drawn to an arrowhead at (850, -10)) now holds the arrowhead: (780, -10) to (850, 10), where it ended at 800. `DxfDimensionAndMLeaderExtentsTests` (2 for the multileader, red before).
**FIXED.** A dimension that keeps a break made by hand and is scaled (SCALE) is drawn again, as AutoCAD 2021 draws it, its offsets and arrowheads as its style sets them and not scaled with the picture: a level dimension from (0, 0) to (100, 0), its line at y 20, scaled by 2, has its extension lines from 0.0625 to 40.18 (AutoCAD's console: from (0, 0.0625) to (0, 40.18)), where the picture scaled had them from 0.125 to 40.36, and by 0.5 from 0.0625 to 10.18, where it had 0.03125 and 10.09. The points of the break go with the scale (from (20, 20) to (25, 20) to (40, 40) and (50, 40)). AutoCAD's console draws every break by hand again as a stroke of no length at the middle of its line after such an edit, which the presenter does not copy. Left: a level dimension with no break scaled by 2 has its picture scaled by the library's `TransformBy` (extension lines from 0.125), where AutoCAD draws it anew (from 0.0625). `DimBreakScaleCopyTests` (2, red before).
**FIXED.** A dimension copied (COPY, MIRROR, ARRAY) with a BREAKDATA has one of its own, as AutoCAD 2021's COPY gives it, where the copy had none and was drawn with the original's picture, its breaks where the original's were: the copy names the same objects (each of them names its BREAKDATA among its reactors), the points of a break by hand are carried by the move, and a copy that keeps a break at an object is drawn again, broken where those objects cross it now. A level dimension from (0, 0) to (100, 0), its line at y 20, broken at a line at x 30 from y -5 to 50 and copied 100 to the right has a line from 100.18 to 199.82 whole, a line at x 130 the BREAKDATA does not name breaking nothing; copied 60 down, whole; copied 10 up, across the line, broken there from 29.9375 to 30.0625 (probed in AutoCAD's console, four copies). `DimBreakScaleCopyTests` (3, 2 red before; the one of the copy moved across the line passes before too, as the copy moved straight up kept the original's break at the same x). Left: a multileader copied keeps the breaks of the picture it was copied from and has no BREAKDATA of its own; AutoCAD's console draws the copy moved across the line 0.12125 higher than it stands (its line at y 30.12125 for 30, unexplained, the break at 29.9375 and 30.0625 as here), where the presenter draws it where it stands.
**FIXED.** The picture of an arc length dimension whose words have no height has no arc symbol: the symbol (DIMARCSYM 0, before the words) was an arc of radius 0.8 times the height of the words, which is no shape for nought. `DimBreakScaleCopyTests` (1, red before).
**FIXED.** The DXF text a DWG is turned into, and the text of a `DxfDatabase` saved, holds the same bytes under .NET Framework 4.8, .NET 8 and .NET 10. Under .NET Framework 56 of 186 DWGs (96 of AutoCAD's own samples, the 71 test files, 16 written by AutoCAD in 2018's form and three of 60 000 to 300 000 entities written for the check) gave another text than under .NET 8 and 10 (the Floor Plan Sample is 28 bytes longer there); none does now, and the text of .NET 8 is what it was, byte for byte (the 186 DXFs compared with `cmp` under the three runtimes). The 834 lines that differed in the 53 of the 183 that are not the big ones came from four faults of the Framework's own number routines, which the library had trusted. (1) 571 numbers half way between two texts of 17 digits (6.9212722778320312|5 is a double exactly, a float's) went up there where .NET Core 3.0 and later send them to the even digit: 6.9212722778320313 for 6.9212722778320312. (2) 93 numbers whose 15 digits read back to the double (2926.731493) were written with 17 (2926.7314929999998), the Framework's `double.Parse` reading those 15 digits a unit off in the last bit, as it does for about one decimal of 6 to 15 digits in a thousand. (3) 60 numbers were written with 15 digits that do not read back, the same parse making the next double of the text: -0.068897637795275607 was written -0.0688976377952756, so that the DXF did not hold the number of the DWG. (4) 110 negative noughts lost their sign (`0.0` for `-0.0`). Its `ToString("G15")`, `"G16"` and `"G17"` are not correctly rounded either (the 16 digits are made from 15 or 17 rounded already): of 300 000 texts of each of eleven kinds of doubles 2 761 to 10 415 had a wrong digit. The digits are now worked out by `ExactDigits`, in whole numbers on every runtime (the first 17 by one product of 128 bits, and in `BigInteger` for a number under 1E-11, from 1E15 up or subnormal), whether a text reads back is judged in integers by the check `Numbers.Exact` already had, and no runtime formatting or parse is used for a number. The writer of the DXF of a DWG (`DwgDxfWriter`, which had left a number whose 15 digits came within a sixteenth of half the distance to its neighbour of being read back to the Framework's parse, about 6 in 100, to the old way) and `Numbers.Exact` (every number a `DxfDatabase`, the exporters and the presenter write) both use it. 55 000 000 doubles of eleven kinds (decimals of 1 to 15 digits typed in and worked out, rounded to 0 to 16 places, floats, dyadic fractions, neighbours of powers of ten and two, bit patterns of any exponent, the edges 1E-4 and 1E14, numbers of 1E15 and over) were written by the DXF writer, by `Numbers.Exact` and by `DwgDxfWriter.Number`: the digest of the texts is the same under .NET 8, .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8 and is that of the older code under .NET 8, where it was another under .NET Framework in all eleven kinds; 3 300 000 of them under each of the three runtimes, with their texts of 1 to 17 digits, were also judged by a reference in `BigInteger`, none different, and under .NET 8 that reference is `ToString("G1")` to `("G17")` for all of them. A coordinate of three decimals is written in 61 ns under .NET 8 as it was and 76 ns where 99 under .NET Framework, a float's 72 ns where 213 and 90 where 252, and `Numbers.Exact` takes 141 ns where 273 under .NET 8 and 172 where 436 under .NET Framework (a whole number 18 where 97, and 33 where 158); a number under 1E-11, which a drawing has by the dozen (6.123233995736766E-17) and not by the million, is slower in the DXF of a DWG, 837 ns where 339 under .NET 8 and 1 430 where 1 020 under .NET Framework. `DxfRuntime1Tests` (12 tests, 10 red with the older code: the half-way numbers, the Framework's parse wrong both ways, the negative nought, a drawing saved, 220 000 numbers against the reference, the digits of 1 to 17 places).
**FIXED.** The DWG written from a DXF read its numbers with the parse of the runtime (`DwgRecord.Double`), so that under .NET Framework a decimal of 6 to 15 digits in a thousand was a unit off in the last bit in the DWG (-0.999778 became the double above it), and the DWG made of one text was not the same file under .NET 8. It reads with the library's own exact parse (`Numbers.TryRead`, as the DXF reader does) and falls back on the runtime's for what that does not read; under .NET 8 the result is the same. `ADecimalOf6To15Digits_IsReadByTheDwgWriterAsTheDoubleNearestIt` and `TheNumbersTheDxfOfADwgHolds_ReadBackAsTheDoublesTheyWereWrittenFrom` (55 000 numbers), both red with the older code.
**CHANGED.** The normal of a CIRCLE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE and SOLID that `TransformBy` mirrors (and so `GetTransformedCopy`, MIRROR3D and everything that mirrors through them) is the image of the old normal, as AutoCAD 2021 takes it; the library turned it over, the cross product of the images of the axes, as ezdxf does. Probed with `TransformBy` on 48 entities of the planes (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0), (1, 1, 1), (1, 2, 3) and (0, 0, -1) under 13 transformations (mirrors across x = 40, y = 30, z = 0, z = 5, a tilted plane and a slanting line, a mirror turned about z, a mirror scaled by 2, turns about x, y and z, a move and a scaling): every circle, arc, polyline and SOLID is AutoCAD's in every group, to 1E-9. A circle at (50, 50, 0) mirrored across x = 40 stands at (30, 50, 0) with the normal (0, 0, 1), where it had the normal (0, 0, -1) and a centre of (-30, 50) in its system; mirrored across z = 0 it keeps its centre (50, 50, 0) and has the normal (0, 0, -1). An arc about (60, 30) from 30 to 120 degrees across x = 40 runs from 60 to 150 degrees about (20, 30), with the normal still (0, 0, 1); across z = 0 it runs from 60 to 150 on the normal (0, 0, -1) about (-60, 30) in its system, the same arc. A polyline with the bulges 0.5 and -0.3 has -0.5 and 0.3 where it keeps its normal, and so does one whose normal is turned over. A thickness keeps its sign (a circle 2 thick across z = 0 is 2 thick, not -2). A transformation that is no mirror gives the same bits as before. The presenter's MIRROR keeps what it drew: probed in its console, AutoCAD's own MIRROR leaves these normals as `TransformBy` does (a circle across x = 40 has no 210), so the entities it mirrors now have the normal up where they had it down, and the display lists of all 48 mirrors of eight kinds (MIRRTEXT 0 and 1, three lines) are the same but that of an arc, drawn from the other end (start 1.047, sweep 1.571 where it was start 2.618, sweep -1.571: the same 60 to 150 degrees). `DxfMirrorNormalTests` (24, 21 red before), `MirrorNormalTests` (6 in the viewer's); the tests that asked for the turned-over normal in `DxfArcTests` and `DxfCircleTests`, and the viewer's test that said AutoCAD left a mirrored arc seen from below, ask for the image now.
**CHANGED.** `TransformBy` of an MTEXT keeps the words readable under a mirror, as AutoCAD 2021's does (probed on 8 MTEXTs of the planes (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0), (1, 1, 1) and (0, 0, -1), held by top left, middle centre and bottom right, under the 13 transformations above): the MTEXT is turned over about its point before the mirror, across its upright where its direction mirrored and reversed reads, in the system of the image of the normal, in the half of the circle it reads in now, else across its baseline, and the point it is held by goes to the opposite side of its box, left for right or top for bottom. An MTEXT along x at (20, 40) held by its top left, mirrored across x = 40, stands at (60, 40) reading along (1, 0, 0) held by its top right; across y = 30 it stands at (20, 20) held by its bottom left; across z = 0 it has the normal (0, 0, -1), reads along (-1, 0, 0) and is held by its top right; turned 34.4 degrees and mirrored across the line through (20, 5) and (30, 20) it reads along (0.204, 0.979) held by its bottom left. The new normal is the image of the old one as for a circle. Nothing but the mirrors changes. An MTEXT with contexts (an annotative one) is turned over in each context as well (see the entry on annotative texts above). The presenter's MIRROR under MIRRTEXT 1 mirrors an MTEXT in its plane as AutoCAD's does (probed: normal (0, 0, -1), direction (-1, 0, 0), held as before), by the reflection across its own plane that `TransformBy` no longer makes. `DxfMirrorNormalTests`, `MirrorNormalTests` (the MTEXT test that asked for the turned-over normal now asks for the readable MTEXT).
**FIXED.** The direction of an MTEXT scaled (group 11) was written scaled (1.65, 1.13 for (0.825, 0.565) scaled by 2); AutoCAD 2021 keeps it of unit length. `AnMTextScaled_KeepsItsDirectionOfUnitLength` (red before).
**CHANGED.** `TransformBy` of a TEXT, ATTDEF or ATTRIB keeps the words readable under a mirror, as AutoCAD 2021's does, where the drawing's `FontSearchPath` measures them and the text is aligned left on its baseline: it is turned over in its own plane before the mirror, across its upright where its baseline mirrored and reversed reads in the half of the circle it reads in now, through the middle of the box of its ink, else across its baseline through the middle of the ink's height. "ABC" 3 high at (20, 40), its ink 8 wide in txt.shx, across x = 40 stands at (52, 40) reading along x with the normal (0, 0, 1) (AutoCAD wrote 52 in its MIRROR3D and its MIRROR with MIRRTEXT 0), where the library wrote (-60, 40) on the normal (0, 0, -1), its words backwards; across z = 0 it is at (28, 40) on the normal (0, 0, -1), its first point (-28, 40) in its system; across y = 30 at (20, 17); turned 34.4 degrees and mirrored across x = 40 it is turned to 325.6 at (53.397, 44.517), as AutoCAD's MIRROR wrote it. Probed on 16 texts of 4 planes, 6 justifications and flags under 13 transformations: a text AutoCAD moves by its width reads its ink where the drawing's fonts give it; in the console's own font it wrote 8.445, not 8, so that the numbers differ by the width and by nothing else. Where no font measures the words, the text is backwards or upside down, it is of a justification AutoCAD reads with no vertical mode, it is mirrored as before (its normal turned over, its words backwards); the texts held by a second point and the annotative ones are turned over as the entries above say. `DxfTextMirrorTests` (5).
**FIXED.** A mirror that also scales left the pattern scale (41) of a hatch scaled; AutoCAD 2021 leaves it as it was, whatever the scale (a mirror scaled by 2 keeps 2, where a scaling alone makes 4). Probed on 18 hatches (user, ANSI31, HONEY, SOLID, gradient, annotative, in 6 planes) under a mirror scaled by 2, MIRRHATCH 0 and 1: 41 was the only group that differed (but for the extra groups AutoCAD writes after the loops of a gradient). `AHatchMirroredAndScaled_LeavesItsPatternScale_WhereAScalingAloneDoublesIt` (red before).
**FIXED.** The pattern angle (52) of a hatch of normal (0, 0, -1) turned by half a circle in its plane, as by 300 degrees about x, was written +180 over (30 became 210); AutoCAD 2021 writes -180 once the new normal points down (30 becomes -150), and 210 up to 270 degrees (probed over turns of 190 to 350 degrees about x and y of 18 hatches: the only hatch that differed was this one, from 280 degrees on). The rule is the one that fits the probe, a hatch pointing down turned to point down; any other half turn is written as it was (the 180 of other hatches matched). `AHatchPointingDown_TurnedAboutXByMoreThanHalfACircle_...` (red before).
**FIXED.** A hatch made annotative on a normal other than (0, 0, 1) wrote the direction of the pattern of its context (10, 20, 30) in the system of its plane, (0.866, 0.5, 0) for a pattern at 30 degrees; AutoCAD 2021 writes a vector of the world (probed with -HATCH ANnotative in a UCS turned 90 degrees about x: a hatch of normal (0, -1, 0) holds (0.866, 0, 0.5)). A hatch in the plane of the drawing is as it was, bit for bit. `AHatchMadeAnnotativeOnANormalOffTheZAxis_HoldsTheDirectionOfItsPatternAsAVectorOfTheWorld` (red before).
