What stays open: AutoCAD's `Annotative = True` through its API writes a context direction of (0, 0, 0), which the library does not follow.

**NEW.** The grip menus of a linear dimension: its extension line origins offer Stretch, Continue Dimension and Baseline Dimension, its arrowheads those and Flip Arrow, and the grip of the words of a dimension Stretch, Move Text Only, Move with Leader, Move with Dim Line, Above Dim Line, Center Vertically and Reset Text Position, with the command line texts and prompts of AutoCAD 2021's grip table (`** CONTINUE DIMENSION **` and `Specify endpoint of dimension line:`, `** FLIP ARROW**` and `Pick to flip arrowhead:`, `** MOVE TEXT ONLY **` and `Specify destination point:`, `** ABOVE DIMENSION LINE **`, `** CENTER VERTICALLY **`, `** RESET TEXT POSITION **`, each with its `Pick to ...:`). Continue and Baseline run DIMCONTINUE's and DIMBASELINE's row from the origin beside the grip, in the style of the dimension: a level dimension of 100 from (0, 0) to (100, 0) with its line 30 below, continued from its second origin to (300, 0), gets one of 200 from (100, 0) on the same line, and based on its first origin one of 300 from (0, 0) a DIMDLI further out. Flip Arrow writes the flag AutoCAD keeps in groups 74 and 75 of the dimension and draws as AutoCAD 2021 draws it, which was probed by reading a DXF with the flags set into its console, on dimensions of 100, 12, 1 and 0.3 with arrowheads of 0.18: an arrowhead inside the extension lines goes outside with a line an arrowhead long beyond it and the dimension line drawn from its tip to where it began, one outside goes inside with a line on inward from its back and the short line it stood on taken away, and ticks do not move. The three Move items put the words where DIMTEDIT puts them under DIMTMOVE 2, 1 and 0, keeping the DIMTMOVE as an override where the style's is another; Above and Center write DIMTAD 1 and 0 as an override and bring words put by hand back onto the line. AutoCAD's own menu is not in its console, so which items each grip offers, and what Above, Center and the Move items write into the dimension, are the presenter's reading of its strings and its documentation, not checked in the GUI. `GripMenuDimensionTests` (15).
**NEW.** The grips of the boundary of a hatch that follows no objects, as AutoCAD 2021's `GetGripPoints` gives them after the grip of the middle (probed on a rectangle 100 by 60, with an arc segment, with edges, with a circle and with an associative one): for each loop a vertex and the middle of the segment leaving it, so that a rectangle 100 by 60 has (50, 30), then (0, 0), (50, 0), (100, 0), (100, 30), (100, 60), (50, 60), (0, 60), (0, 30), a loop of one circle its four quadrants, and a hatch that follows an object only the one at its middle. Dragging one is what AutoCAD's `MoveGripPointsAt` does to it: a vertex moves alone, the middle of a straight segment takes both its ends along, that of an arc segment bends the arc through the point (the bulge 0.5 arc from (100, 0) to (100, 60) dragged to (122, 35) has its middle at (122.4021, 30), as AutoCAD gives it), a quadrant makes the radius the distance to the point (87, 35 about (50, 30): 37.3363). The loop stays a loop of a polyline or of edges. A 2D POLYLINE fitted with a curve or a spline has a grip on each vertex of its frame, as AutoCAD gives them (four for the frame (0, 0), (100, 0), (100, 60), (0, 60), not the seven or thirteen vertices of the curve), and dragging one straightens it, moves the vertex and fits it again as AutoCAD does: a curve-fit one dragged at its second vertex to (107, 5) has its added vertex at (55.2375, -32.4975) and bulges 0.2976 and 0.2985, a cubic spline-fit one thirteen vertices with (77.625, 31.875) in the middle, a quadratic one refitted as the cubic SPLINETYPE 6 gives, all to AutoCAD's four decimals. Neither has a menu. `GripMenuHatchBoundaryTests` (10) and four tests in `GripMenuPolyline2dTests`.
**NEW.** Lengthen and Radius of the hover menu have Copy and Undo, as the stretch of a grip has them: `Specify end point or [Base point/Copy/Undo/eXit]:` and `Specify radius or [Base point/Copy/Undo/eXit]:`. With Copy on, each point makes a copy of the line or the arc with the edit (a line from (0, 0) to (100, 0) lengthened by (150, 40) and (180, 40) gives lines to 150 and 180 beside the one to 100), the header says `** LENGTHEN (multiple) **`, Undo takes the last copy back and does nothing before one is made, and the whole run is one undo step.
**CHANGED.** Remove Vertex of the hover menu of a polyline's or a spline's vertex asks for a pick, as AutoCAD 2021's strings say: `** REMOVE VERTEX **` and `Pick to remove vertex:` (`** REMOVE FIT POINT **` and `Pick to remove fit point:` for a fit point, `** REMOVE CONTROL VERTEX **` and `Pick to remove vertex:` for a control vertex of a spline); any point picked takes the vertex out, Enter or Esc leaves it. It took it out at once. A 2D POLYLINE fitted with a curve or a spline, which had no grips, has those of its frame (see above) and refuses `AddVertex`, `RemoveVertex` and `ConvertToArc` of `CadGrips`. A hatch that follows no object has more than one grip. The three tests that said "at once" now say the pick.
**NEW.** MIRROR3D in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console asks it (probed: the prompts, the words that refuse a point, and the objects mirrored with each option): objects, then `Specify first point of mirror plane (3 points) or [Object/Last/Zaxis/View/XY/YZ/ZX/3points] <3points>:`, a point answering as the first of three and Enter asking for it, then `Delete source objects? [Yes/No] <N>:`. A plan has no Z, so three points lie in the XY plane, and three collinear ones are refused ("The three points are collinear.", the third asked again) as two that coincide are ("The 1st and 2nd point coincide.", "The two points coincide." for Zaxis); Object takes the plane of a circle, an arc or a 2D polyline ("Improper type of object picked." for a line); Last the plane last used, the XY plane through the origin where there was none (probed); View, XY, YZ and ZX a point `<0,0,0>` by default, the YZ and ZX planes square to the x and y axes of the UCS. Each object moves as its `TransformBy` mirrors it, a line from (0, 0) to (0, 50) across the YZ plane through (40, 0) running from (80, 0) to (80, 50) and a line across the XY plane keeping its points with the normal (0, 0, -1), as AutoCAD writes it; a hatch follows MIRRHATCH as MIRROR does (the line of a user pattern at 30 degrees stays at 30 with 0, comes to 150 with 1, across the YZ plane through the origin, as AutoCAD's 18-object probe wrote it). `Mirror3DCommandTests` (11).
**CHANGED.** `DxfHatch.TransformBy` leaves the lines of the pattern as they were under a mirror, as AutoCAD 2021's own `TransformBy` does while its MIRRHATCH is 0, its default, where it reflected them as MIRRHATCH 1 does; the new `DxfHatch.TransformBy(GeoTransform3, bool mirrorPattern)` asks for the reflected form. Probed with `TransformBy` on 13 hatches (user pattern, ANSI31-like and three-line patterns with dashes, SOLID, gradient, one scale and two, in the planes of normals (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0), (1, 1, 1), (1, 2, 3)) under 6 mirrors (across a vertical plane, the YZ and ZX planes, the plane of the hatch, a tilted plane, and a mirror turned about z) with MIRRHATCH 0 and 1: every hatch, line of the pattern and context of the library is AutoCAD's, in both, to 1E-9, but for the extra groups AutoCAD writes after the loops of a SOLID and a gradient. A mirror that also scales (a mirror across the vertical plane, doubled) leaves the pattern scale (41) as it was in AutoCAD and doubles it here; no command makes one, and it stays open. A line at 30 degrees through (0, 0), offset (-1, 1.732), across the line through (20, 5) and (30, 20) stays as it was and comes to 82.6198649480404 with `true`; the loops, the seed points, the normal and the direction of the pattern of each context are reflected either way, and a transformation that is not a mirror is the same for both. Anything else that mirrors a hatch through `TransformBy` (a grip's MIRROR, a transformed copy) leaves the lines too; the presenter's MIRROR still follows MIRRHATCH. `DxfHatchReflectionTests` (the reflecting test now asks `true`, 4 new).
**FIXED.** The direction of the pattern of an annotative hatch's context (10, 20, 30) was turned with every transformation; AutoCAD 2021 leaves it as it was where the transformation takes the x and y axes of the hatch's own system (those of its normal) straight to those of the new normal's, and turns it with the hatch elsewhere. A hatch of normal (0, 1, 0) turned 40 degrees about z, or the plane of the drawing turned 40 degrees about x, keeps (-0.866, 0, 0.5) or (0.866, 0.5, 0), where one of the plane of the drawing turned about z, or any hatch turned about its own normal, turns it ((0.866, 0.5, 0) becomes (0.342, 0.940, 0) at 40 degrees), and a mirror reflects it. 463 pairs of 11 annotative hatches in 6 planes and 6 kinds of transformation (turns about x, y, z and two slanting axes by 6 angles, mirrors, a move, a scaling), where the direction could tell, are on this rule in AutoCAD 2021's `TransformBy` and the same in its ROTATE command (the 79 of them where AutoCAD leaves the direction were all turned before, the cases the last round left open among them). `DxfHatchReflectionTests`.
**NEW.** More grips have AutoCAD 2021's hover menu, with the words, command line texts and prompts of its grip table (read from the string tables of `acdb24res.dll` and `acadres.dll`; the console has no `MultiModesGripPE`, so its `GetGripPoints` gave the grips and the strings gave the menus). The end of a line or an arc offers Stretch and Lengthen (`** LENGTHEN **`, `Specify end point or [Base point/eXit]:`, `Specify end point of arc` for an arc): a line from (0, 0) to (100, 0) lengthened at its end by a click at (150, 40) runs to (150, 0), a click behind the other end is refused, and an arc of radius 20 from 0 to 90 degrees lengthened at its end by a click at (290, 30) about (300, 0) ends at 108.4 degrees. The middle of an arc offers Stretch and Radius (`** RADIUS **`; an arc of radius 20 given a point 35 from its centre has radius 35, the centre and the angles kept). A spline has a vertex grip on each fit point, or on each control point where it has no fit data (a cubic through four points has four, as AutoCAD's `GetGripPoints` gives), and its menu is Stretch Fit Point, Add Fit Point and Remove Fit Point, or Stretch Vertex, Add Vertex and Remove Vertex, grey at two fit points or at a degree and one control points; Add says `** ADD FIT POINT **` and `** ADD CONTROL VERTEX **`. A hatch has one grip at the middle of the box its loops fill (50, 30 for a rectangle 100 by 60, as AutoCAD) with the menu Stretch, Hatch Scale, Hatch Angle and Origin Point (`** HATCH SCALE **`, `** HATCH ANGLE **`, `** ORIGIN POINT **`; the scale and angle keep the pattern's origin, the origin is laid as HATCHSETORIGIN lays it); a solid fill has Stretch alone and no menu. A 2D POLYLINE of straight and arc segments has the grips and the menus of a light polyline (the seven grips of four vertices that AutoCAD gives it): stretch, Add Vertex (a half circle from (0, 0) to (20, 0) given (10, -10) becomes two quarter circles), Remove Vertex, Convert to Arc and Convert to Line; one fitted with a curve or a spline has none. `GripMenuLineArcTests` (14), `GripMenuHatchTests` (10), `GripMenuSplineTests` (9) and `GripMenuPolyline2dTests` (10). Left: the dimension menus (Continue Dimension, Baseline Dimension, Flip Arrow, the text moves), the spline's small grip that switches fit points and control vertices, the vertex grips of a hatch boundary, the Copy and Undo of Lengthen and Radius, and Ctrl cycling. How the cursor becomes a scale or an angle in Hatch Scale and Hatch Angle, and what Radius keeps, are not in AutoCAD's strings and are not checked in its window.
**CHANGED.** Convert to Line in the hover menu of an arc segment of a polyline asks for a pick, as AutoCAD 2021's string says (`** CONVERT TO LINE **`, `Pick to convert to line segment:`): any point picked makes the segment straight, Enter or Esc leaves the arc. It was done at once. Remove Vertex, whose string is `Pick to remove vertex:`, stays at once; `GripMenuLineArcTests` has the two tests of the pick, both of which fail without the change, and the older test of Remove Vertex and Convert to Line now says the pick.
**CHANGED.** A DWG of many entities or of many blocks opens faster: the entities are written into the DXF it is turned into on up to eight threads, and the list of its blocks is no longer walked once for each block. A DWG of 300 000 lines and circles with coordinates of three decimals (10.1 MB, 39.7 MB as DXF) opens the first time in a process in 0.53 s where 0.65 (.NET 8), 0.55 s where 0.68 (.NET 10) and 0.79 s where 1.05 (.NET Framework 4.8), and the next time in 0.47 s where 0.66, 0.37 s where 0.52 and 0.74 s where 0.90; one of 300 000 entities of seven kinds (8.1 MB, 46.9 MB) in 0.65 s where 0.77, 0.67 s where 0.77 and 0.82 s where 1.00 the first time, and 0.47 s where 0.64, 0.42 s where 0.56 and 0.92 s where 1.18 the next; medians of 9 runs (5 for the next time) with the older build alternated, the machine busy. A drawing of 20 000 linear dimensions, 20 000 hatches and 20 000 splines (3.7 MB, 34 MB as DXF; each dimension has a block of its own) opens in 0.68 s where 1.55 (.NET 8), 0.75 s where 1.57 (.NET 10) and 1.2 s where 2.2 (.NET Framework), and the next time in 0.56 s where 1.42, 0.55 s where 1.42 and 0.79 s where 2.0. The writing of the blocks and the entities, the part of the opening this changes, takes 46 ms where 167 for the lines and circles (.NET 8; 48 ms where 166 under .NET 10, 62 where 245 under .NET Framework), 51 ms where 191 for the seven kinds and 39 ms where 837 for the dimensions, hatches and splines. The DXF made of each of 186 DWGs (96 of AutoCAD's own samples, the 71 test files, 16 written by AutoCAD in 2018's form, and three of 60 000 to 300 000 entities) is byte for byte what it was (SHA-256), under .NET 8, .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8, on one thread, two, three, eight and as chosen. Two things make the gain. The walk over the blocks, on the calling thread, only decides which entities are written, in what order and under which owner, and hands them on in runs of 1 024 as it goes; the other threads write the records of a run into a buffer of its own, and the buffers are put in the DXF in the order of the runs, so the bytes are those of one thread. The runs and the buffers are used again as they are done: a first version that kept them all added 10 MB, which was enough for the collector to make one more full collection, 150 ms, in a drawing of seven kinds, and was slower than the one thread. A file of fewer than 4 096 objects is written by the thread that reads it, as it was, and a token stopped is answered at the next entity. And the blocks were listed through a list asked whether it held each one already, 200 million comparisons for 20 000 blocks, 0.8 s of the 1.5 s the drawing of dimensions took; a set does it in 0.04 s, in the order of the blocks table, so that the DXF is the same. Measured and left as they were: the collector, which makes the same four to six collections, 100 to 150 ms of the first opening, with the entities written on threads as without (the objects, 570 bytes an entity, are kept until the DXF is written, and a no-GC region of the whole opening, 600 MB, took the pause out of the opening and made it 215 ms in the next collection, no gain; a latency mode of the collector that keeps back collections of the full heap made 960 collections of the small ones); `DwgJit.Hot` on the dimension, hatch and spline decoders (the decoding of the drawing above 305 ms where 292, the opening the same within the noise, and no change for a small drawing); and the copy of the DXF's array, which a better estimate does not take away (a DXF is 1 to 84 times the size of the objects in 186 drawings) and which costs no collection in the opening (an array made to size left the collections as they were, 0.59 s both). `DxfSpeed30Tests` (5, of which the one of the blocks was red with the list: 4 000 blocks 57 ms and 16 000 649 ms).

**CHANGED.** A DWG of many objects opens in about half the time the first time in a process, and a number that is not whole is written into the DXF it is turned into in a fifth of the time under .NET Framework 4.8. A DWG of 300 000 lines and circles with coordinates of three decimals (11.2 MB, 41 MB as the DXF it is turned into) opens the first time in a process in 0.65 s where 1.28 (.NET 8), 0.71 s where 1.27 (.NET 10) and 0.88 s where 1.35 (.NET Framework 4.8), and the next time in 0.56 s where 0.64 (.NET 8), 0.60 s where 0.55 (.NET 10, within the noise) and 0.72 s where 1.15 (.NET Framework), medians of 9 runs with the older build alternated; one of 300 000 entities with worked-out coordinates of 17 digits (12.4 MB, 51 MB as DXF) opens the first time in 1.0 s where 1.7 (.NET 8, the machine busy), 0.69 s where 1.40 (.NET 10) and 0.88 s where 1.69 (.NET Framework), and the next time in 0.85 s where 1.02, 0.53 s where 0.66 and 0.72 s where 1.47. The DXF made of each of 274 DWGs (167 of AutoCAD's own samples and the test files, 107 more of the harness), of 1 001 written by the library in six versions and of three of 20 000 to 300 000 entities is byte for byte what it was (SHA-256), under .NET 8, .NET 10 and .NET Framework 4.8, on one thread, on eight and as chosen. Four things make the gain. The objects of a file of 4 096 or more are decoded on up to eight threads (as many as the machine has), each of its own `DwgObjectReader`, which holds the object it is reading, taking 512 at a time: they are put back in the order of the file before a byte is written, the first broken object told is the first of the file and not the first met, a stopped token is answered at the next object, and a failure that is not a broken object is that of the lowest object, as one thread would have it. The decoders share nothing they change (the tables of colours, of types and of line weights, the check sums and the grammars of the ACIS data are read only, the one cache that was written, of the grammars, was under a lock, and the offsets by handle that a table's style looks up are made once, under a lock), and a file of fewer objects is decoded by the thread that reads it, as it was. On the drawing above the objects take 0.37 s on one thread and 0.19 s on eight (.NET 8, the first opening); the whole first opening takes 0.76 s on one thread, 0.60 on four and 0.60 on eight (.NET 8) and 0.92, 0.81 and 0.82 s (.NET Framework), and the next opening 0.59, 0.57 and 0.60 s (.NET 8) and 0.76, 0.66 and 0.65 s (.NET Framework): the collector, which has to walk the 300 000 objects as they are kept, is one thread under the workstation collector and takes half of the time the objects take once they are warm (under the server collector the same objects take 0.097 s on one thread and 0.035 on eight). A number that is not whole, from 0.0001 up to 1E14 in size, is written as bytes in whole-number arithmetic under every runtime, where .NET Framework made two strings of it and tried its 15 digits back through `double.Parse` and .NET Core one string of the shortest text: 81 ns where 381 for a coordinate of three decimals and 73 ns where 685 for a worked-out one (.NET Framework), 52 ns where 118 and 62 where 251 (.NET 8), 49 where 88 and 57 where 190 (.NET 10). Its digits are the mantissa times a power of five over a power of two, exact, and the 15 digits bring the number back where they lie within half the distance to its neighbour; a number that is a power of two, or exactly half way between two texts, is left to the way it was written before. .NET Framework's parse is not exact (about one in a thousand of the nearest doubles of a decimal of 6 to 15 digits is read a unit off in the last of 64 bits, by up to 0.005 of that half distance in 5 300 cases found), so the older text had 17 digits for those, and a number whose 15 digits come within a sixteenth of half the distance of being read back is left to the old way under .NET Framework, about 6 in 100 of them, so that the text is the older one to the byte: 900 000 000 numbers of eleven kinds (decimals of 1 to 15 digits typed in and worked out, rounded to 1 to 6 places, the neighbours of powers of ten and of the bounds, dyadic fractions, bit patterns) were written as the older code wrote them, 300 000 000 under each of the three runtimes, none different. The handles written are kept in a table made once for the number of objects (`DwgHandleSet`, 8 MB for 300 000) where a `HashSet<ulong>` grown by adding made an array of every size on the way, 20 MB, the larger of them large objects each of which has the collector look at the whole heap: one full collection less in the writing of the DXF (100 ms of the first opening). And some sixty methods that the objects pass through by the hundred thousand, the bit reader, the readers of the common data, of the LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, POINT, TEXT, INSERT and LWPOLYLINE, and the writers of the DXF, ask the compiler to compile them fully at the first call (`MethodImplOptions.AggressiveOptimization`, which .NET Framework ignores), where under .NET Core a method runs as unoptimised code until it has been called 30 times and the runtime has had 100 ms with no new method to compile, which a first reading is mostly over before: 0.75 s to 0.60 (.NET 8) and 0.92 to 0.66 (.NET 10) in the first opening of the drawing above, the next opening as it was. Measured and left as they were: the one full collection that the DXF's reading (`DxfDatabase`) still makes in the first opening (26 to 29 ms), which comes of the copy of the array the DXF is written in when a quarter of it or more is unused (a DXF 3.7 times its DWG, where the array is made for 7 times) and went away with the array made to size, which no estimate short of the DXF written gives; the contexts an MTEXT and an INSERT keep (a tuple of 48 bytes the first time one is asked for, which saves a walk of the record for each asking and needs the object kept as the check, so that it would cost a thread-safety check for 48 bytes); and the walk over the records for linked columns (6 ms in a display of 1 000 000 entities). `DxfSpeed28Tests` (10, of which the one of bytes a number allocates and the two that .NET Framework's parse is held to were red on the older code or with the safety margin taken out, and the one of the first broken object red with the first met).
**NEW.** A table with a number (a whole number or a real), a general value with nothing in it or a field in a cell is a table in a DWG of R2000 and R2004, as it is in R2007, where `DxfVersionConverter` wrote it as the block it is drawn with. The cell of those versions knows only words: a number stands as the text it shows (the 302 of its value, `12` and `2.500000` in `tclean`), a general value as no words and a field as its handle (344) where the words would stand. The data table keeps the value of each as AutoCAD writes it (a number its flags 6, its type and its data, a general value 5 and 512, a field the value of the last field of the chain of its first children, `93=4 90=8 94=0 300=yyyy 302=2026` for a year and `93=1 90=0` for a field not worked out), and the TABLECONTENT of those versions holds a value of the type 512 with its words in 1 (`90=512 1=`). The ACAD_TABLE, TABLECONTENT, TABLEGEOMETRY and data table of `tclean`, `tcustom`, `ttable`, `tstyles` and of two tables with a date, a file name, an author and a save date in their cells, written as R2000 and R2004, are those of AutoCAD 2021's own files of the same drawings (read by the reader) group for group, but for the proxy graphics of R2000, the masks of the data table of `tcustom` and the size of the value of a date field (92: 16 in R2018, 8 in its R2000 and R2004 files, left at 16); AutoCAD's DXFOUT of those 12 files is its DXFOUT of its own files, and the 42 files of 14 drawings (the seven table drawings, two with fields and five tables with a property set at a time) written as R2000, R2004 and R2007 open with AUDIT 0 (42 of 42). A cell that names a field the drawing does not hold (the R2018 file of a table whose cell was given a field code as its text, `Cell.TextString = "%<\AcVar Filename \f \"%fn6\">%"`, holds such a handle; AutoCAD's own R2000 file of it holds none) is written with no words: the handle written would be a null one, the cell read as one with words past the end of the table's data, and AutoCAD refused the file (ErrorStatus 53). A table with a link to data, a value of another kind or a text of more than 250 characters in its content is still the block it is drawn with. `DwgTableValuesOfOlderVersionsTests` (18 tests, 16 red before: the table was the block, the masks were not AutoCAD's, the view colours were lost; the other 2 keep R2007 as it was).
**CHANGED.** The mask of a cell in the data table of a table written as R2000 or R2004 is 0 for what the table gives the cell, as AutoCAD's is. A cell holds in its flags and groups a value that the table's own overrides give every cell, or that the style gives the row across the edge where two kinds of row meet (the lineweight of 0.35 under a title is also the one over the header), as one it set; the mask counts the alignment, the background colour and the borders a cell sets, so that the cells of `ttable`, `tstyles` and `tclean` (12, 15 and 12) have the 0 of AutoCAD's own files, where the mask gave `ttable` a mask to each of its 12 cells and `tstyles` to 6 of its 15. The data of the rule: AutoCAD's masks of 168 cells of three tables with one property set on a cell at a time (a lineweight alone on a top border 0x400, a colour 0x40, the same of the opposite side on the cell across) and of `tall` and `tcell` are of what was set one property at a time, which the file does not show (a border set whole has 0x4440), so the whole side is kept, as before; a value set that is the one the style gives is counted by AutoCAD (`tcustom`: 2 of 15 cells have a mask, 10 differ here). Three tests of the DxfSave group that made a table with a field the block it is drawn with now do it with a link to data, and `DxfSpeed11Tests` pins a new hash for the R2000 save of the second round of its edited table (a table now, a block before; the first two rounds hold a text of 300 characters in their content and stay blocks).
**FIXED.** The colours of a view style of an R2000 file survive its DXF: AutoCAD keeps the index of each colour in the object of its R2000 file, where its DXF of R2000 has no group for it, and the reader gave none, so that a DWG of R2000 read and written again lost them. The reader gives the index (62) in the DXF it makes, `DxfVersionConverter` leaves it out of the DXF it makes of R2000 from another version and keeps it for a DWG, and the DWG written is AutoCAD's bytes in the object's data. A DXF of R2000 saved from a drawing read from an R2000 DWG, which the converter does not touch, holds the 26 groups 62 of the two view styles of `views`; AutoCAD opens it with AUDIT 0.
**FIXED.** A table of R2000 or R2004 read from a DWG goes up to R2007 and later as a table when a cell overrides a look: the reader of a DWG gives the overrides of a cell between its state (178) and its rotation (145), where `DxfVersionConverter` expected them after its words as AutoCAD's DXF has them, and made such a table the block it is drawn with. A whole number and a general value in its content go up with the flags AutoCAD gives them (6 and 5), where they made it a block too.
**NEW.** UNDO's Auto, Control, BEgin and End work in the presenter as AutoCAD 2021's console has them (probed through its standard input, UNDOCTL read after each step: 5, 13 in a group, 0 and 3 under None and One, 49 with Auto off). BEgin makes the commands that follow, to End, one group, taken back and put again as one by U, UNDO and REDO and written `GROUP LINE CIRCLE LINE` (the steps in the order they were made; the group made of ERASE and ERASE is `GROUP ERASE ERASE`); U inside an open group takes one step of it (`LINE`) and the group stays open; a second BEgin closes the open group and starts a new one; End with no group open says nothing. Control asks `Enter an UNDO control option [All/None/One/Combine/Layer] <All>:`. None turns U off, `U command disabled.  Use UNDO command to turn it on`, and UNDO then writes `Auto = Off, Control = None` and asks that option alone (anything else is `Invalid option keyword.`, Enter is All); One keeps the last command alone (the steps before it are gone, U writes the name and `Everything has been undone`) and UNDO asks `Enter an option [Control] <1>:`, refusing 2, nought, text and BE with `Requires an integer value 1, or option keyword.`; what was done while None was on cannot be undone once All is back, and All turns Auto on again. Auto asks `Enter UNDO Auto mode [ON/OFF] <On>:` (`<Off>` when it is off) and is kept and shown, there being no menu macro of several commands to group; Combine and Layer ask `Combine zoom and pan operations? [Yes/No] <Yes>:` and `Combine layer dialog operations? [Yes/No] <Yes>:` (`Yes or No, please.` to other text), Combine No making each real-time zoom and pan of the wheel and the middle button a step of its own, as UNDOCTL's 16 does. The names of the steps UNDO 2, UNDO Back and U take back stand on one line, `LINE LINE`, and `UNDO 5` over two steps writes `LINE LINE` and then `Everything has been undone`, where each name was a line; REDO says `Nothing to redo` (it had a full stop) and `Everything has been redone` after the last step it brings back. A keyword prompt can have words of its own for text it cannot take. `UndoControlTests` (16), all of which fail without the change. Left: AutoCAD's REDO must follow the U or UNDO before it (`REDO must immediately follow the U or UNDO command.`) and redoes all of that undo, where the presenter's redoes one step at a time as before; Layer's combining of the layer dialog's operations is kept and shown only.

**NEW.** LAYOFF's and LAYFRZ's Settings change what a pick takes, as AutoCAD 2021's console does (probed over blocks three deep, a reference BO on LB holding a reference BI on LN that holds a line on LI, a line on L2 and a reference BZ on LN2 holding a line on layer 0; and a layout viewport worked through with MSPACE). Block selection: Block takes the layer of the block reference the object picked is in, the innermost (LN for the line in BI, LB for the line BO holds, LN2 for the line in BZ), Entity the object's own (LI, L2, and 0 for the line in BZ, which is asked about where 0 is current), None the reference picked (LB); a block with nothing nested is its own layer at all three. The nested object is the one whose box, put where the blocks draw it, holds the point within the pick aperture, the smallest where several do, as REFEDIT picks a nested object (`CadDocument.FindNestedPick`, internal). Viewports: in a viewport worked through, Vpfreeze (the default) freezes the layer in that viewport alone, `Layer "WALLS" has been frozen in this viewport.`, the layer still on and thawed in the others, and U thaws it there; Off at LAYOFF turns it off, and Freeze at LAYFRZ freezes it, everywhere; on the Model tab and on the paper of a layout the layer changes everywhere whatever the setting. A current layer is asked about as `Layer "WALLS" is current, do you want to Vpfreeze it? [Yes/No] <No>:`. FIXED. The same question for the global change was `Layer "0" is the current layer, do you want to turn it off?`, where AutoCAD says `Layer "0" is current, do you want to turn it off? [Yes/No] <No>:`, and LAYFRZ on the current layer said `Cannot freeze layer "0".  It is the CURRENT layer.` with two spaces where AutoCAD's LAYFRZ has one (-LAYER and the Layer manager keep their two: probed). `LayerSettingsPickTests` (23), of which 14 fail without the change. Left: the objects of an external reference are not gone into (the layer of the reference is taken); the settings are kept for the session, where AutoCAD keeps them between sessions.

**FIXED.** INT and APP clicked on the canvas over one object ask ` and` for a second, as they do for a point typed (INT or APP typed or chosen from the Shift+right-click menu, then a click within the aperture of one object alone; at `Select objects:` too): a click on the second object gives where the two cross, taken as it lies and not snapped by the snaps that are on, or says `No Intersection found for specified point.` and asks the prompt INT was typed at again; where two objects lie under the click the crossing is given at once, as before. An APP click used to pick the first object and ask nothing (Extended Apparent Intersection, which stays for APParent running). END typed at ` and`, or any other object snap, typed or chosen from the menu, is refused as AutoCAD 2021 refuses it (` and END`, then `Point or option keyword required.` or `Invalid point.` of the prompt INT was typed at, asked again; TT, FROM and the point filters are taken there, as before); the presenter took it as an override for the second pick. A box dragged at `Select objects:` while END waits took no snap at its first corner and left the override waiting; the corner the drag began at is snapped and the override spent, as a box clicked does. `ClickedIntersectionInterfaceTests` (10, 9 fail without the change) and `CanvasOverrideDragTests` (2, 1 fails without it). Not changed: NEArest typed at the aperture's edge gives the exact foot (probed at 1.30 to 1.375 from a line: (50, 0) each time, nothing from 1.377, the same cut for ENDpoint), and that cut is 10.5 pixels at 0.131 to the pixel, a rounding of the point to a pixel that the presenter, which has no pixels at a typed point, does not make; it keeps 10.

**FIXED.** The leader band of an angle's words put by DIMTEDIT follows the words' width, as AutoCAD 2021 draws it: "120°" put every 0.25 at 36 directions round an angle of 60 degrees from 0, 45, ... 315 degrees, its arc 30 out, had 373 of 26 384 probes with the leader wrong (Arial 255) where "60°" has 27 of 36 278, and the real DIMADEC words, wider still, had 4 to 11 per cent wrong, for in some directions the rule's own scaling with the words (the landing's sagitta, room squared over the radius) over-corrected until words 8 wide had a leader on the circle itself. The sagitta is now the landing of "60°" in the same style times the words' landing over the radius (the same number where the words are "60°"), and a table by direction, `WidthCorrections`, is added at nodes of how far the words' landing is over that of "60°": "6°" 0.18 under it, "120°", "60.0°", "60.00°", "60.000°", "60.0000°" and "60.000000°" 0.14, 0.29, 0.46, 0.64, 0.82 and 1.18 over it (read linearly between, held beyond), one table of 36 directions for every first ray (AutoCAD's edge for wider words moves the same on every first ray outside the circle; a table fitted to four first rays took the other four from 138 to 84 of 13 192), SHX and Arial together. Probes of AutoCAD 2021's pictures (the angle of 60 degrees from 0, 45, ... 315, words put every 0.25 at 36 directions, d from -7 to 16) with the leader wrong, before and now, SHX and then Arial: "6°" 141 and 182 to 94 and 70 of 17 680, "120°" 373 and 255 to 217 and 168 of 26 384, "60.0°" 666 and 469 to 309 and 245, "60.00°" 858 and 767 to 411 and 362, "60.000°" 1 218 and 998 to 560 and 469, "60.0000°" 2 127 and 1 491 to 788 and 606 (of 26 384 each), "60.000000°" (first rays 0, 90, 180 and 270) 1 771 and 1 379 to 505 and 445 of 12 648. Pictures differing from AutoCAD's, before and now: o7 5 358 to 5 202 of 55 872, o5 (angles of 30 to 150 degrees) 25 819 to 25 571 of 223 488, to5 5 005 to 5 004, aq 81 to 71 of 6 860, taq 64 to 58, e8 444 to 443 of 13 968, e12 119 to 117, te5 10 to 9; worse: e7 732 to 738 of 55 872, te8 308 to 312, e11 53 to 55, te11 104 to 105 (probes of the "60.0000°" variant within 0.25 of an edge), p2 6 to 8 of 576 (the two of the reflex angle), and a3g 246 to 250 of 3 856 (Arial 4 to 6: the first leader of the words put at 30 degrees with DIMADEC 0 to 6 is within 0.15 of AutoCAD's in all 16 styles, as it was within 0.05 before; the 242 other pictures differ in the arc point of the "60.000000°" words 4 high, which are not changed); every other set of the harness (tar1 to 26, r1 to 6, t1 to 11, ta2, ta8, ta9, tj1, tj2, j1, j2, a, a2, a3, a4 to a7, d1 to d5, td1 to td3, p1, e1, e3, e4, e5, e9, e10, e13, te3, ta7, o1, o2, o4, o6, to6, tw1 to 17, tm3, ts1, m to m6) is byte for byte what it was. a3g, which had no AutoCAD picture, now has one (a3g, ta3g: DIMADEC 0, 2, 4 and 6, DIMTXT 2.5 and 4, the words put at 30 degrees from 4 to 16 out). Not changed: the near rings of DIMTXT 4 (o6, to6: 1 483 and 950 wrong), which are no worse than the rings of the base style at the same landing (about 6 per cent at 1.5 landings out, 160 of 2 346 for "60°" of 2.5 at 8 out), so it is not the words' height but the nearest arcs, where the band's inside edge lies up to 7 deeper than the rule's at some directions (words across the vertex): a multiplier of the table or of the near correction per style (best 1.0 to 1.1 each) leaves them, and a cap on the corrections at 0.2 of the landing takes "120°" from 373 to 251 and the rings of o6 from 1 483 to 2 575; a test of the words' box against the circle was not built; and the jump of the band at the height of the arc's middle (d1: 11 of 279), whose wrong probes lie at the edges of the band at x -33.5, 33.5 and -21 more than at the jump (the band at x -21 has no jump in AutoCAD's picture where the rule has one of 2.1).

**NEW.** DIMBREAK breaks a multileader in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 does, and `DxfMLeader` keeps and draws the breaks. AutoCAD takes a multileader at "Select dimension to add/remove break or [Multiple]:" (Multiple takes dimensions only here); it was refused as "not a dimension". Probed through the .NET API and the console fed through standard input (about 150 breaks of leader lines of one, two and three vertices and of one and two leader lines): the break is kept in the leader line, after its vertices and before its index (90 the segment, 11 and 12 the start and the end of each break), and a BREAKDATA under ACAD_BREAKDATA in the multileader's extension dictionary names what it was made by, as for a dimension; AutoCAD's own `Explode` gives the line whole, and it is drawn cut. Auto breaks each leader line where an object of the space crosses it, a gap of the multileader style's break size (143) times the scale of the multileader, half either side of the crossing: a line from (0, 0) to (100, -1.25) crossed at x 40 is broken from (39.9375, -0.499219) to (40.0625, -0.500781), from (39.875, -0.498438) to (40.125, -0.501562) at scale 2; a circle of 5 about (70, 0) breaks it twice; the line is drawn from the back of its arrow, which no break reaches into, and the dogleg is not broken, though an object that crosses only the dogleg or only the arrow's tip is named in the BREAKDATA. Manual breaks the leader line and, in it, the segment nearest the first point, from the foot of the first point on the segment to the foot of the second: from (30, 0) to (35, 0) on that line from (29.9953, -0.374941) to (34.9945, -0.437432); a point beyond the end of the leader line is held at its end (from (30, 0) to (130, 0) leaves nothing from 30 on), one beyond a vertex between two segments breaks nothing, and so does a pair of points neither on the drawn segment; breaks that meet are one, kept as the points were picked (91 the leader line's index, 71 of 2); Remove takes the breaks and the BREAKDATA out. New: `DxfLeaderBreak`, `DxfMLeader.GetBreaks(leaderLineIndex)`, `SetBreaks(leaderLineIndex, breaks)` and `ExplodeBroken()` (`Explode()` is as it was); the breaks move, turn and scale with the multileader as they did. `DxfMLeaderBreakTests` (6, in the core suite) and `DimBreakMLeaderTests` (16, the numbers above from AutoCAD). Left: AutoCAD names every object whose extents meet the multileader's (or the dimension's) in the BREAKDATA of an Auto, the presenter those that cross it, which differs only in the objects named; DIMBREAK Multiple does not take a multileader.
**FIXED.** DIMBREAK Manual breaks a dimension as AutoCAD 2021 does, where it took the line nearest the middle of the two points and cut the picture's nearest line of any kind. Compared with AutoCAD 2021 in its console on about 400 breaks of linear, aligned, angular, radius and diameter dimensions (45 are kept as tests): the line broken is the one nearest the first point, among the extension lines (0 and 1), the dimension line or the arc of an angular dimension (3), the lesser number on a tie, where it was nearest the middle (a break from (0, 10) to (100, 10) is of the first extension line, 91 of 0, and cuts it at y 10 and no more, where it took the dimension line and took it out whole); both points are carried along that line and the stretch between them is left out where at least one falls on what the dimension draws of the line, the other held at its end (from (40, 20) to (120, 20) on a line drawn from 0.18 to 99.82 leaves 0.18 to 40), and nothing is cut where both are off it; the arc of an angular dimension is cut, which was left whole (from 22.5 to 45 degrees on an arc of 84.85, two arcs, the points of 91 of 3 as AutoCAD keeps them) and only where both points fall within it; the rays of an angular dimension are 0 and 1 as AutoCAD numbers them (the ray the angle is measured from counter-clockwise first of a vertex and two points, the one along the second line first of two lines) and the line a break is kept on (91) is the one cut; the centre mark of a radius or a diameter, which lies along its line, is no line that breaks (from (0, 0) to (35, 0) on a radius of 30 cuts the line from 30.18 to 35 and leaves the mark). A dimension drawn anew is broken again on the line kept. A line that only touches a dimension, a multileader's leader line or a leader with its end is found at the end (it was missed by the rounding of 1E-17 where the end lay on the line). `DimBreakManualRowsTests` (47: 45 rows from AutoCAD's numbers, 20 of them red before the change, and two for an angular arc broken by hand, drawn anew and removed, and for the centre mark of a radius). Left: AutoCAD takes a point picked near a point of the dimension (an extension line's origin, the dimension line's point) for that point, within some pixels of its view (from (0, 15) to (0, 5) it keeps the second as (0, 0), the first extension line broken from 15 to its origin), which the presenter's own snaps are for; DIMBREAK Auto on the arc of an angular dimension, which AutoCAD breaks (a circle across the arc of 84.85 at 33 and 39 degrees leaves three arcs), the presenter leaves whole.
**NEW.** XCLIP Clipdepth cuts a text, an MTEXT, a hatch, a solid and a 3D face that stand in a plane tilted out of the plan, as AutoCAD 2021 draws them (PNGOUT in plan of a text, an MTEXT, a hatch and a solid in a plane tilted 45 degrees about X, with front 20 and back 5: each is left glyph by glyph and pixel by pixel as the strip of the plan where the plane's height lies between the planes, the hatch's pixels at y 5.01 to 20.16 where the frame stands for -50 to 150). The height along the plane is a straight function of the plan, so the part that stays is a strip, bounded by the entity's extents grown and drawn in a clip region of its own inside the clip's. A hatch in a block nested in another, placed 10 higher, stays from y 15 to 30 (AutoCAD 2021: 14.8 to 30.4), and a hatch lying flat in the plan under a clip made in a system tilted 30 degrees about X, with front -30 and back -50, from y 75.36 to 115.36. A plane standing upright is seen edge-on in the plan and is drawn whole, as are an image and an OLE frame, which have no plane to cut by. A text whose font the drawing does not find has no extents, and is cut by the same strip, judged by its position and the reach of its words. The words and arrowheads of a dimension and the text of a table are cut as the entities of any block are.
**NEW.** The boundary of the clip of an external reference is kept in the drawing's own coordinates and goes with the content when the drawing's base point ($INSBASE) changes, as AutoCAD 2021 keeps and draws it (entget and PNGOUT of a drawing whose base point is (70, 0, 0), attached at (100, 0, 0) and clipped to the rectangle (130, 10) to (190, 40) of the world: the filter holds the inverse of the placing as a shift by -30, so that the boundary is the drawing's x 100 to 160; a boundary of 20 to 80 of a drawing reloaded with a base point of 70 where it had 0 stands from -50 to 10). `DxfBlockReference.ClipTo` writes it so, and `ClipOutline` gives the ring in the drawing's coordinates, where an ordinary block's stays measured from its origin (the shift by -100 there). The presenter places the ring by the base point the drawing has now, and XCLIP's New boundary makes a boundary picked at x 130 to 190 stand there whatever that base point is; the grips and the library, which have only the origin the host's block records, take that for the base point. The planes of Clipdepth of an external reference are kept in the drawing's coordinates the same way. A clip of an external reference made by an earlier version, which kept its boundary from the insertion point, is read as the drawing's own coordinates and stands a base point away where that is not the origin.
**FIXED.** A dashed circle, whole ellipse or closed polyline that Clipdepth, or the prism of a tilted clip, cuts across its start is two pieces there, and the pattern of the second begins again, as AutoCAD 2021 draws the whole: the linetype of a closed curve begins at its start (PNGOUT in plan of a DASHED circle and of a DASHED closed polyline tilted 45 degrees about X, and of a DASHED arc, each with the planes 10 and -10 and again with none: every pixel of every piece is on a dash of the whole, 156 of 156, 512 of 512 and 65 of 65). The piece that holds the start was one, its pattern carried across the start: a circle standing on its edge, radius 30, with front 10 and back -10 is three arcs, the one from the start with no phase, the one at x 78.28 to 80 starting 58.28 along and the one that ends at the start 118.28 along, where it was two arcs, the second starting 118.28 along and going on past the start with the pattern of the stretch before it. A dash is measured along the plan in the display, and along the curve's own length in AutoCAD (the dashes of the whole tilted circle start at multiples of 18.75 along its circumference, 3D), which the display does not do for a curve that does not lie flat.
**NEW.** The breaks DIMBREAK Auto made follow the objects they were made at, in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 draws a dimension or a multileader again from its BREAKDATA after an edit (probed in its console through standard input, about 150 edits of level dimensions and multileaders with a line across them): a line at x 30 across a level dimension from (0, 0) to (100, 0), its line at y 20, moved 10 to the right breaks the dimension line at x 40 (from 39.9375 to 40.0625) and no longer at 30, moved off it leaves the line whole while the BREAKDATA still names it, moved 60 down and back up breaks it again; erased, it is taken out of the BREAKDATA, which goes with its last object (two lines, one erased, leave the other's break and the BREAKDATA; both, a whole line and no extension dictionary). The dimension moved, turned or scaled is broken again where the lines it names cross it now: moved 10 up, at x 30 on its line at y 30; turned 30 degrees about (0, 0), from (29.9459, 40.3833) to (30.0541, 40.4458) on its line from (-9.8441, 17.4105); moved 50 to the right, away from the line, whole. A multileader does the same (a line at x 40 moved 10 to the right breaks the leader line from (49.9375, -0.6242) to (50.0625, -0.6258); the multileader moved 10 up, from (39.9375, 9.5008) to (40.0625, 9.4992)). An object the BREAKDATA does not name breaks nothing wherever it is drawn or moved to later, as in AutoCAD. A break by hand goes with a dimension: its points are carried by the move or the turn (from (60, 20) to (70, 20), the dimension moved 10 to the right, is kept from (70, 20) to (80, 20), probed with no view to draw in; with a view AutoCAD's console draws every manual break again as a stroke of no length at the middle of its line, which the presenter does not copy); a multileader keeps the points as picked and takes their feet on its leader line again where it moves (from (30, 0) to (35, 0), moved 10 up, from (30.1203, 9.6235) to (35.1195, 9.561)). `CadBreakFollow` is called by every edit, beside the follow of associative dimensions; an edit that cannot make a dimension's breaks again leaves it as it was and logs a Warn. `DimBreakFollowTests` (12) and `DimBreakMLeaderFollowTests` (5), 14 of them red before the change.
**FIXED.** DIMBREAK Auto names every object whose box meets the dimension's or the multileader's in its BREAKDATA, as AutoCAD 2021 does, where the presenter named only those that cross a line of it: a line from (10, 0.5) to (20, 15) inside the box of a level dimension from (0, 0) to (100, 0), its line at y 20, crosses nothing and is named all the same (and breaks the dimension line from 16.489 to 16.614 where it is moved 10 up); one clear of the box (from (60, 30) to (60, 40)) is not, and breaks nothing moved across. The objects are named newest first, as AutoCAD writes them (lines drawn as c, a, b and a circle e are named e, b, a, c), where the presenter named them oldest first. A point, a solid and a hatch are named by no one; another dimension is, and breaks one at the lines of its picture (a dimension from (20, -10) to (80, -10), its line at y 40, breaks one from (0, 0) to (100, 0) at 19.9375 to 20.0625 and 79.9375 to 80.0625 with its extension lines). AutoCAD takes about a pixel of its view beyond the box (between 0.5 and 0.7 at a window 700 across, between 0.05 and 0.1 at one 160 across), the presenter, with no view, none.
**FIXED.** DIMBREAK Auto breaks the arc of an angular dimension and of an arc length one, and the leader of an ordinate, as AutoCAD 2021 does; the presenter left the arcs whole. A line from (50, 50) to (100, 100) across the arc of an angle from 0 to 90 degrees of radius 84.85 leaves two arcs, from 0.002121 to 0.784662 and from 0.786135 to 1.568675 radians (the gap of the break size 0.125 along the arc), a circle of 5 about (70, 50) across it three (the second from 0.564081 to 0.676418), the same on an arc length dimension of radius 60 (two arcs about 0.785398 and three for the circle) and at the rays of both (a line at x 55 breaks a ray from 54.9375 to 55.0625); each kind of object that breaks a line breaks an arc, the words by the span of their box. Compared with AutoCAD on 29 breaks of angular, arc length and ordinate dimensions, the pieces equal to 1E-4. Left: Manual on an ordinate or an arc length dimension, which AutoCAD does not do as on a line (the leader of an ordinate and the rays of an arc length dimension are lines 0 and 1, and it puts the first point on the middle of the line and the second on the arc's end, the break of a leader picked from (20, 40) to (20, 50) kept as one point at 45.0763); the presenter keeps its nearest-the-middle rule there.
**CHANGED.** DIMBREAK Multiple takes dimensions and multileaders both, as AutoCAD 2021 does (both at "Select dimensions:", and "2 objects modified" for a level dimension and a multileader with a line across them, both broken); it asked `Enter an option [Break/Remove] <Break>:` and now asks `Select object to break dimensions or [Auto/Remove] <Auto>:`, which takes Auto, Remove, or the objects to break at picked one by one.**FIXED.** A linear dimension drawn level by AutoCAD, whose record has no group 50, and turned by `DxfEntity.TransformBy` (ROTATE, a mirror, a turn in code) measures along its new direction: group 50 is written then, where it stayed out and the dimension measured along x again wherever its picture was drawn anew (a level dimension turned 30 degrees has `Rotation` pi / 6, which was 0). `DxfDimensionTests`, one added, red before.
**NEW.** DIMBREAK breaks a multileader in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021 does, and `DxfMLeader` keeps and draws the breaks. AutoCAD takes a multileader at "Select dimension to add/remove break or [Multiple]:" (Multiple takes dimensions only here); it was refused as "not a dimension". Probed through the .NET API and the console fed through standard input (about 150 breaks of leader lines of one, two and three vertices and of one and two leader lines): the break is kept in the leader line, after its vertices and before its index (90 the segment, 11 and 12 the start and the end of each break), and a BREAKDATA under ACAD_BREAKDATA in the multileader's extension dictionary names what it was made by, as for a dimension; AutoCAD's own `Explode` gives the line whole, and it is drawn cut. Auto breaks each leader line where an object of the space crosses it, a gap of the multileader style's break size (143) times the scale of the multileader, half either side of the crossing: a line from (0, 0) to (100, -1.25) crossed at x 40 is broken from (39.9375, -0.499219) to (40.0625, -0.500781), from (39.875, -0.498438) to (40.125, -0.501562) at scale 2; a circle of 5 about (70, 0) breaks it twice; the line is drawn from the back of its arrow, which no break reaches into, and the dogleg is not broken, though an object that crosses only the dogleg or only the arrow's tip is named in the BREAKDATA. Manual breaks the leader line and, in it, the segment nearest the first point, from the foot of the first point on the segment to the foot of the second: from (30, 0) to (35, 0) on that line from (29.9953, -0.374941) to (34.9945, -0.437432); a point beyond the end of the leader line is held at its end (from (30, 0) to (130, 0) leaves nothing from 30 on), one beyond a vertex between two segments breaks nothing, and so does a pair of points neither on the drawn segment; breaks that meet are one, kept as the points were picked (91 the leader line's index, 71 of 2); Remove takes the breaks and the BREAKDATA out. New: `DxfLeaderBreak`, `DxfMLeader.GetBreaks(leaderLineIndex)`, `SetBreaks(leaderLineIndex, breaks)` and `ExplodeBroken()` (`Explode()` is as it was); the breaks move, turn and scale with the multileader as they did. `DxfMLeaderBreakTests` (6, in the core suite) and `DimBreakMLeaderTests` (16, the numbers above from AutoCAD).**FIXED.** DIMBREAK Manual breaks a dimension as AutoCAD 2021 does, where it took the line nearest the middle of the two points and cut the picture's nearest line of any kind. Compared with AutoCAD 2021 in its console on about 400 breaks of linear, aligned, angular, radius and diameter dimensions (45 are kept as tests): the line broken is the one nearest the first point, among the extension lines (0 and 1), the dimension line or the arc of an angular dimension (3), the lesser number on a tie, where it was nearest the middle (a break from (0, 10) to (100, 10) is of the first extension line, 91 of 0, and cuts it at y 10 and no more, where it took the dimension line and took it out whole); both points are carried along that line and the stretch between them is left out where at least one falls on what the dimension draws of the line, the other held at its end (from (40, 20) to (120, 20) on a line drawn from 0.18 to 99.82 leaves 0.18 to 40), and nothing is cut where both are off it; the arc of an angular dimension is cut, which was left whole (from 22.5 to 45 degrees on an arc of 84.85, two arcs, the points of 91 of 3 as AutoCAD keeps them) and only where both points fall within it; the rays of an angular dimension are 0 and 1 as AutoCAD numbers them (the ray the angle is measured from counter-clockwise first of a vertex and two points, the one along the second line first of two lines) and the line a break is kept on (91) is the one cut; the centre mark of a radius or a diameter, which lies along its line, is no line that breaks (from (0, 0) to (35, 0) on a radius of 30 cuts the line from 30.18 to 35 and leaves the mark). A dimension drawn anew is broken again on the line kept. A line that only touches a dimension, a multileader's leader line or a leader with its end is found at the end (it was missed by the rounding of 1E-17 where the end lay on the line). `DimBreakManualRowsTests` (47: 45 rows from AutoCAD's numbers, 20 of them red before the change, and two for an angular arc broken by hand, drawn anew and removed, and for the centre mark of a radius). Left: AutoCAD takes a point picked near a point of the dimension (an extension line's origin, the dimension line's point) for that point, within some pixels of its view (from (0, 15) to (0, 5) it keeps the second as (0, 0), the first extension line broken from 15 to its origin), which the presenter's own snaps are for.

**FIXED.** MLEADERALIGN's Distribute and specify Spacing measure the gap between two contents along a slanting line as AutoCAD 2021 does, and its make leader segments Parallel and its turning of leaders follow AutoCAD where a multileader has several leader lines. The multileaders were made through the .NET API in a plugin (the console hangs on MLEADER at its text editor), MLEADERALIGN was run on them in the console fed through standard input, and the text location and leader vertices of about 500 cases (Use current spacing, Spacing, Distribute and Parallel; one to five multileaders of words of one and several lines, in two scales, with leaders on either side, with two leader lines, and of blocks; lines of every slope) were compared with the presenter's: they now agree to 2E-3 where the words' ink is measured the same, the presenter measuring Arial to six places as AutoCAD does. The gap along the line is the distance the second box can slide along it from the first until the two just clear each other, past the first's right edge (past its own right edge where the line runs to the left) or past the first's top or bottom, whichever comes first, where it was the sum of the boxes' reaches along the line (which agrees only on a level or a plumb line): boxes 16 by 2.5 and 4 by 1 on a line at 45 degrees clear each other 3.5355 along it (the height decides); three blocks 16 by 2.5, 4 by 1 and 10 by 5 distributed from (0, 0) to (100, 100) have their left middles at (0, 0), (49.375, 49.375) and (100, 100), the first and the last exactly on the points (they were 0.88 off along the line, their centres being the ones placed). The line goes through the left middle of the one picked and a content holds the middle of its first line level with its landing. Parallel turns of the leader lines to one landing the one that lies most nearly along the dogleg's axis (arrowheads at 150, 170 and 210 degrees from the landing of a dogleg along x: the one at 170), in the one picked and in the others, where it took the first; the others only follow the landing. A leader of several lines whose arrowheads stand on both sides of the middle of the box keeps on its side the lines whose arrowheads are there and sends the others to a new leader on the other side, the words held as they were (arrowheads at -30 and 40, the box's middle at 17: the line of -30 keeps the leader on the left, the line of 40 goes to a new leader on the right, its landing a gap and a dogleg past the ink), and with every arrowhead on the other side the leader is turned whole, where the leaders of several lines were left as they were. `MLeaderAlignGapsTests` (8: the clearances of blocks 16 by 2.5, 4 by 1 and 10 by 5 at 45 and 135 degrees, level, and under Spacing at two slopes, from AutoCAD's numbers; the split, the whole turn, Parallel of the straightest of two lines). Left: words of several lines in a TrueType font with a descender in the last line are held by the middle of the whole ink here and by half of the last line's in AutoCAD (0.37 on 2.5 high for "gjp" under two lines, 0.02 for the round capitals of one line); a block multileader of an MLEADERSCALE other than 1 whose block has its left edge on its origin is held by the middle of its unscaled height in AutoCAD (1.25 for a block 2.5 high at 0.5), and its landing is laid again from unscaled extents after the move.
**CHANGED.** A DWG is made into its DXF, and that DXF is read, in less time and with less garbage: a DWG of 300 000 entities with fractional coordinates (9.1 MB, 54 MB as the DXF it is turned into) opened the first time in a process takes 1.26 s where 1.63 under .NET 8 and 1.53 s where 2.18 under .NET Framework 4.8, and the next time 0.74 s where 1.12 (.NET 8) and 1.42 s where 2.05 (.NET Framework), medians of 7 runs with the older build alternated (.NET 10, 5 runs: 1.29 s where 1.73 and 0.58 s where 0.96); it makes 596 MB of garbage where 794 (.NET 8) and 617 where 924 (.NET Framework); 20 000 lines and circles are made into their DXF in 1 519 bytes an entity where 2 742 and 31 ms where 95 (.NET Framework). Of the objects of the DWG: the DXF is written into one array, made at once for seven times the bytes of the file (a DXF of 182 drawings was 1.2 to 11.9 times its DWG) and doubled only where that was short, where it went through a `MemoryStream` a byte at a time with a string made for each group code, whole number, handle and double and each double's text tried back through `double.Parse`; that array is the one `DwgReader.Open` gives the reader of the DXF, with its length, and is cut to its length first only where a quarter of it or more is unused, where a copy of 54 MB was made. A group that holds a double or an int keeps it in the group and not as a boxed object of its own (a LINE keeps six of its seven groups so), what only some objects carry (the owned entities and ends of a polyline, the name and entries of a table record, the groups of a block and the rest) is kept in an object of its own made when the first is set, the lists an object has none in are not made, and an entity is given room for the groups it adds: an object of the DWG is 120 bytes where it was 392, a LINE or a CIRCLE kept 731 bytes with the lists and the table of handles that hold it and keeps 432. The bits of a DWG are taken from the bytes they lie in at once where all of them are there, one at a time only where the end of the data is in the way, so that a broken object is refused with the same message at the same bit. Under .NET Core a double that is neither whole nor very large or small (0.0001 up to 1E14) is formatted once, as the shortest text that brings it back, where the older code formatted it with 15 digits and tried that back: the text is the same to the byte for the 60 000 000 doubles tried (nine kinds of them, from random bits to degrees of a whole number), and any number outside those bounds, and every number under .NET Framework, is formatted as before. The DXF made of each of 182 DWGs (95 of AutoCAD's own samples, 71 of the test files and 16 written by AutoCAD) and of two drawings of 300 000 entities is byte for byte what it was (SHA-256), under .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8. The count of a block (`DxfBlockTableRecord.Count`) makes no copy of its entities (7.8 MB at 1 000 000 where it took 9.7 ms, 7.1 ms now), and the copy that a walk of a block makes (`GetEnumerator`, `AllItems`, `AllEntities`, `EntityByHandle`, which has to be a copy, for the block may change while it is walked) is made once for walks that follow one another with no entity added or erased between, and held only until the collector wants it: the lookup by handle that a hatch, a leader and a viewport make took 7.8 MB of garbage at 1 000 000 entities and takes none. Measured and left as they were: the box of a `DisplayArc2` made when asked for (32 bytes of 104 for each arc, 2 per cent of the heap, at 50 to 68 ms for a million boxes where reading one kept takes 5.5 ms, on each pass of the canvas over the items); the contexts a TEXT keeps, which the display of a plain TEXT does not reach (taking them out changed none of its bytes); and the walk over the records for linked columns (6 ms in a display of 1 000 000 entities), which cannot be kept between displays since an edit of an MTEXT's extended data does not change the list. `DxfSpeed27Tests` (16, of which the 3 that run on the older code were red there: 2 742 bytes an entity, 3.2 MB for 20 counts of 20 000 entities, and two walks given two lists) and `DisplaySpeed27Tests` (2).

**NEW.** REVCLOUDGRIPS works in the presenter: a revision cloud shows the few grips of the shape it goes round while it is ON (it was ON and did nothing), as AutoCAD 2021's `GetGripPoints` gives them (run in its console through a plugin, with `MoveGripPointsAt` for the drags). The cloud round the rectangle (0, 0) to (60, 40) with arcs 10 long has 8 grips, (0, 0), (0, 20), (0, 40), (30, 40), (60, 40), (60, 20), (60, 0) and (30, 0), a vertex grip at each corner from its first vertex and a middle grip at each side; the cloud round the polygon (100, 0), (160, 0), (160, 40), (130, 60), (100, 40) has 10, (130, 60) among them though it is no vertex of the cloud (the two lines of the sides meet there); a cloud whose vertices lie on one circle has the five grips of the circle. An open cloud, one of fewer than six vertices, a polyline with no cloud data and every cloud with REVCLOUDGRIPS 0 keep the grip at each vertex and each arc. A grip dragged draws the cloud again along the new shape, in place, one undo step: a corner goes to the point, a side moves by as much as its middle grip did, the centre of a circle moves it, a quadrant sets its radius, and the arcs are 1.1 times the mean chord of the cloud before, laid from the first vertex with the last arc taking what is left (the rectangle 60 by 40 with arcs 10 long, its top middle dragged up 5, is 19 vertices 11 apart; arcs 40 long round a rectangle 120 by 100 give 41.657 and 11 vertices), as in 15 AutoCAD runs the vertices of which the new tests hold to 6 decimals. A cloud too small for two arcs is refused. The grips of a cloud with few grips have no grip menu. `CadGrips.Shown(document, entity)` gives the grips a document shows (`CadGrips.Of(entity)` is still the grip of every vertex), `CadDocument.RevCloudGrips` is the variable, ON to begin with and kept as long as the document is open. Left: AutoCAD takes any polyline of 110 degree arcs for a cloud whatever its data, and fits an ellipse to some clouds, roughly. `RevcloudGripsTests` (24).

**FIXED.** REVCLOUD Modify ends at once, nothing said and nothing changed, when its first point is nearer the start than 1.1825 arcs (AutoCAD 2021 through standard input: at arcs of 20 a point 23.6 from the start ended it and 23.7 went on; at 100, 118 and 118.5; at 50, 59 and 59.5; at 7, 8.2 and 8.3), where the presenter went on to ask for more points and a side to erase. With the arcs varying it is the first arc's length (random in AutoCAD). The points after the first go on whatever their distance. `RevcloudModifyTinyPathTests` (12).

**CHANGED.** TEXTALIGN along a line of two points and DIMBREAK Auto were compared with AutoCAD 2021's console again, each object made in a short probe of its own (the console hangs on MLEADER after its landing point, so multileaders were left): 144 runs of TEXTALIGN (12 alignments, Current Vertical, Current Horizontal, Set spacing 3 and Distribute, four lines, four TEXT with their boxes set to the console's font) and 96 of DIMBREAK Auto (DIMLINEAR and DIMALIGNED, two lines and a circle across each), every text and every piece of the picture the same to 1E-4 (the pieces beside the dimension's own words differ by the font alone). The console moves every typed point at TEXTALIGN's Pick first point by the place of the first text it picks, the last made, and picks no text by a typed point (its TEXTALIGN pick needs the window). Nothing changed in the code; `TextAlignLineRowsTests` (16) and `DimBreakAutoRowsTests` (8) keep rows of them.
**FIXED.** Arc length dimensions (DIMARC) bring their words and arrowheads between the rays at the distances AutoCAD 2021's console does where the last round left them one or two hundredths out. Aligned words past a half circle (arcs of 1 from 0 degrees through 181 to 230, the distance put out by 0.01, DIMJUST 0, text 0.18 and 0.36 high, DIMASZ 0.18 and 0.36, DIMGAP 0.09 and 0.18, 4 880 pictures; DIMARCSYM 0 and 2) fit what they take against the room by the width of the words and DIMGAP, and with the symbol DIMASZ: the arc of 1 through 200 degrees with the symbol before the words keeps both arrowheads between the rays from 0.65 out (the room asked for 0.046 to 0.071 more than it has there, and they came in from 0.67), and without the symbol it takes the words in from 0.47 and the arrowheads from 0.50 (the words from 0.45 before). The words by a ray (DIMJUST 1 and 2) on arcs of 90 to 140 degrees take their arrowheads in a step of the put distance sooner too: on the arc of 1 from 10 through 130 degrees aligned words from 0.93 out and level ones (DIMJUST 1) from 0.95, where they came at 0.94 and 0.96, which is the one arrowhead state tar37's row of 0.95 left wrong. Sets (differing from AutoCAD's pictures, before then after): aligned words and DIMJUST 1 and 2 past a half circle by 0.01 (5 508) 228, now 111; the same with DIMJUST 0 only, a second probe by sizes (4 880) 209, now 55; aligned words and DIMJUST 1 and 2 by 0.3, 0.45 and 0.8 (432) 36, now 0; DIMJUST words by 0.01 on arcs of 1 and 3 (1 848) 58, now 34; DIMJUST words on arcs of 1, 3 and 10 (216) 1, now 0; of the 129 older sets of probes the other 126 are the same pictures byte for byte as before, none is worse. In the sets that changed 349 pictures that were wrong came right and 17 that were right came wrong (9 and 7 a step of 0.01 off in the two probes past a half circle, 1 in the DIMJUST one). Not changed, a few thousandths off or a step late: the arrowheads that stand outside with level words outside past a half circle (the lower edge of the window the arc's middle direction opens, 1 100 of 4 656 pictures of a probe by one degree of the direction, 48 of the 1 969 of the older ones: a refit of the edge by the box, the gap and the arrowhead brought the probe to 1 070, mended 23 and broke 14 pictures of the older ones, so it stays as it was), the words by a ray on arcs of 181 to 250 degrees (70 of the 111 left of the first probe), and level words coming in by the room on arcs of 90 to 140 degrees, a step late.

**FIXED.** The corner of a window and the point of a fence or a polygon are snapped by an object snap override, typed or clicked, as AutoCAD 2021's console snaps them (probed through the standard input of accoreconsole over a line from (0, 0) to (100, 0), its aperture 1.31): `ERASE`, `W`, `END`, then 60,1 makes (100, 0) the first corner, and the same at the opposite corner, in a crossing and a BOX, at the points of `F`, `WP` and `CP`, and at the opposite corner of the implied window (`Select objects: 69,40` then `END` and 60,1). Where the snap finds nothing the line is `No Endpoint found for specified point.` and then `Invalid window specification.` (the first corner asked again; the opposite corner of the implied window asked as it was) or `Invalid response.` (the same prompt asked again), the override spent. The canvas took no snap for the implied window at all: a click that starts or ends it now takes the override the menu or `END` chose, and a click at a fence or polygon inside `Select objects:` too; the snaps that are on still do not touch the window's corners, as in AutoCAD. A number alone at a corner of a window, a point of a fence or `Select objects:` (`W 1` is `W` then `1`) is a point that far from the last point along the rubber band, as at any prompt for a point, where it was `Invalid window specification.` or `*Invalid selection*`. The prompts of the first point of a fence and a polygon read `Specify first fence point or pick/drag cursor:` and `First polygon point or pick/drag cursor:`. `TypedSnapCornerTests` (21), `TypedSnapCornerInterfaceTests` (21 with the 14 words of the next entry: 4 on the command line, 3 on the canvas).

**NEW.** INTersection and APParent typed after the override: over two objects they give their crossing (the one nearest the point where there are several), over one the command line asks ` and` for a second, answered by a point on it, typed or clicked, and gives the crossing of the two (a line over a circle that cross at (180, 0) and (220, 0), the first point on the line and the second at (219, 6): (220, 0)). With no crossing: `No Intersection found for specified point.` (`No found for specified point.` for APParent) and the words of the prompt, the last point left as it was; text at ` and` is refused as that prompt refuses it, and Enter is answered by it. EXTension and PARallel, which need the cursor to rest on an object, always say `No found for specified point.` to a point typed, and GCEnter finds the centroid of a closed polyline the point lies on (the rectangle from (300, 0) to (340, 30): (320, 15)) and `No found for specified point.` elsewhere; the typed snaps no longer leave the point as typed. The command line writes `_per to`, `_nea to`, `_tan to` and `_par to` for PERpendicular, NEArest, TANgent and PARallel, and `of` after the others (`_end of`), as AutoCAD does. `TypedIntersectionTests` (19).

**FIXED.** BREAK says `No object found` to a point on nothing, and LAYOFF, LAYFRZ, LAYLCK and LAYULK `Nothing Selected.`, each asking again. LAYOFF and LAYFRZ write `Current settings: Viewports=Vpfreeze, Block nesting level=Block` first and offer `[Settings/Undo]`; Settings asks `Enter setting type for [Viewports/Block selection]:`, then `In paper space viewport use [Vpfreeze/Off] <Vpfreeze>:` (`[Freeze/Vpfreeze]` at LAYFRZ) or `Enter Block Selection nesting level [Block/Entity/None] <Block>:`, and each command keeps its own settings for the session (the settings are shown; they do not change a pick inside a block or a viewport yet). U says nothing while it turns a layer back and `Everything has been undone.` with none left, where it said `Nothing to undo.`; Enter at LAYLCK and LAYULK says `Nothing selected.` and asks again, where it ended the command. `LayerPromptWordingTests` (16).

**FIXED.** ARRAYRECT and ARRAYPOLAR ask for the levels as for the rows: after the number, `Specify the distance between levels or [Total/Expression] <1.0000>:`, with Total asking `Enter total distance between start and end levels <2.0000>:`; Total of columns and rows asks `Enter total distance between start and end columns` and `... rows` where it said `Specify the distance between first and last column`, takes no Expression, and says `Requires numeric distance or two points.` to text; a distance of nought at any of them is `Value must be nonzero.` and the same prompt is asked again. `ArrayRowsAndLevelsTests` (7).
**FIXED.** A DWG opened with a token (`CadDocument.Open(path, progress, cancellationToken)`, which Esc and Stop of the window stop) is given up where it is stopped, and not at the end of its reading. The token was looked at once, before the file was read, so a DWG of 300 000 entities (6 MB, 1.6 s to read) stopped 100 ms in answered 1 351 ms late, one stopped 400 ms in 1 180 ms late and one stopped at 1 000 ms 545 ms late (the end of the reading, where the walk of its handles saw it): the window held, and the command line said nothing, until the file was read. The token is now looked at before each page of a section of the file is unpacked (of a file of R2004 to R2018 or of R2007; the sections of one of R2000 lie in the file as they are), before each object is read, before each entity and object is written as DXF, and every 4 096 records as that DXF is walked, so that the same stops are answered 1 ms late (31 ms at the very end, in the passes that come after the walk). A file opened with a token not stopped is the document it was: the DXF the DWG is made into and the display of it are the same, and the DXF is read from the bytes it was written in, where a copy of it was made to be read. `DwgReader.ToDxf` told a stop as a broken file (`FormatException`); it lets the `OperationCanceledException` through. `DisplaySpeed26Tests` (14, of which the 5 of a DWG stopped at 0, 20, 50, 62 and 80 per cent of its reading were red on the older code, where it ran on to 100) and `DxfSpeed26Tests` (10).



**CHANGED.** The display of a drawing of a million entities (`d1m.dxf` of `BigDrawing`: lines, circles, arcs, polylines, texts and INSERTs) keeps 358 MB of objects where it kept 391 and makes 363 MB of garbage where it made 404 (.NET 8; 366 and 371 where 399 and 412 under .NET Framework 4.8), by four changes that leave every display list, pixel and saved byte as it was. A chain (`DisplayPolyline2`) is an object of 72 bytes where it was 80, 6 MB at 780 000 chains: its four flags (closed, sampled and which corner of its box each end of a chain of two is at) were four bools, which an object makes room for as one word, so that one byte in their place would have left it at 80 (measured: 80 bytes with four bools, 80 with one byte, 72 with none); they are kept in the look the chain already shares with the others of its style and layer, which is now one look for each of the flags a chain of that style and layer has (at most 16), shared by all of them. The extended data of an object in no file, which only a table record made in code has, is kept outside the object (`DxfDBObject`), so that an object of a record is 8 bytes smaller (a LINE's 24 bytes where it was 32, 8 MB at a million). A LINE, an ARC, a CIRCLE and an LWPOLYLINE that the display draws have no object made for them to keep, 20 MB: the display reads them through one object of each class aimed at each record in turn (`DxfEntity.Glance`), held by no record, so that the object a reader that keeps one is given later is the only one anything else has, one for one record as it was; a reader that asks for it (`FindEntity`, a walk of the block, an edit) is given it made then, as before. An object made for each record and let go of was tried first and kept as an alternative to this: it made a REGEN of a million entities 7 to 10 per cent slower, where one aimed at each makes none; a TEXT, whose object keeps the contexts it read, was tried the same way and left as it was (a REGEN 6 per cent slower for 8 MB). The walk of the records for a display (`DxfBlockTableRecord.WalkedItems`) gives the list of the space itself where the block has no linked columns, where it gave a copy of it, 8 MB on each display and REGEN at a million entities. Cold display of the million entities 1.25 s where 1.29, REGEN 0.57 s where 0.58 (medians of 9 runs alternated with the older build, .NET 8; .NET Framework 4.8 2.27 s where 2.33 and 1.00 s where 1.01 in 7; .NET 10 1.30 s where 1.28 and 0.55 s as before in 10, within its noise of 1.23 to 1.58). The 953 drawings of AutoCAD kept beside the checks (812 DXF and 141 DWG: every space's display list item for item and field for field, a REGEN of the first, the bytes saved and the pixels of two views, plain and with everything selected, under .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8) and the drawings of 100 000 and 1 000 000 entities are identical to the older build's. `DisplaySpeed26Tests` (3 more of them red on the older code by bytes allocated: 80 bytes a chain, 417 a line, 449 a circle) and `DxfSpeed26Tests` (10).
