**FIXED.** A point typed after an object snap override (`END`, `MID`, `CEN`, `QUA`, `NOD`, `INS`, `NEA`, `PER`, `TAN`, typed or chosen from the Shift+right-click menu) is snapped as AutoCAD 2021's console snaps it (probed through the standard input of accoreconsole over a line from (0, 0) to (100, 0) at 0.131 to the pixel, its aperture 1.31): the objects within the aperture of the point are looked at and the snap point of any of them nearest the point is the answer, wherever it lies on the object (`END` then 50,1.3 gives (0, 0) or (100, 0); between two lines (0, 0) to (100, 0) and (0, 1) to (90, 1), 50,0.3 gives (90, 1), the end nearest); where none lies within the aperture it says `No Endpoint found for specified point.` (`Midpoint`, `Center`, `Quadrant`, `Node`, `Insert`, `Perpendicular`; `No found for specified point.` for NEArest and TANgent) and then the words of the prompt, `Invalid point.` at a point, `Point or option keyword required.` at a prompt with options, `*Invalid selection*` with the options listed at `Select objects:` (and no window started) and at a prompt for one object, and asks again with the override spent. The window took the snap for the next click alone and left a typed point as typed, so 50,1.4 was a point on nothing. `CadCommandSession.SnapOverride` and `SnapAperture` (the window sets the aperture, 10 pixels over the zoom, with the cursor). INTersection, EXTension, PARallel, APParent and GCEnter leave the point as typed (INT asks `and` for a second object in AutoCAD); the corner of a window and the point of a fence are not snapped by a typed point yet. `TypedSnapTests` (13), `TypedSnapInterfaceTests` (4).

**FIXED.** A prompt for one object answered with text says AutoCAD 2021's second line, which was missing: `*Invalid selection*` and then `Expects a single object.` for DIVIDE, MEASURE, DIMRADIUS, DIMDIAMETER, DIMLINEAR's Select object, DIMANGULAR, CENTERMARK and the rest, or `Expects a point or` with the options of that prompt for BREAK (`Window/Last/Crossing/BOX/ALL/Fence/WPolygon/CPolygon`), OFFSET (`Exit`), FILLET and CHAMFER (`Window/Last/Crossing/BOX/Fence/WPolygon/CPolygon/Undo/Polyline/Radius/Trim`, `.../Distance/Angle/Trim/mEthod`), LENGTHEN (`Last/Fence/DElta/Percent/Total`), TRIM (`Fence/cuTting edges/Crossing/mOde/Project/Edge`), EXTEND (`Fence/Boundary edges/Crossing/mOde/Project`), PEDIT, SPLINEDIT, HATCHEDIT, TEXTEDIT, LAYOFF, LAYFRZ and LAYULK, each as probed in the console. The corner of a window, a crossing or a BOX that is no point, or Enter there, says `Invalid window specification.` and asks the first corner again (the opposite corner of the implied window asks itself again), where the presenter said `Point or option keyword required.` or ended the box; a point of a fence or a polygon that is no point says `Invalid response.`. `ObjectRefusalWordingTests` (34, with the cases of the next entry).

**FIXED.** CIRCLE's radius says `Requires numeric radius, point on circumference, or "D".` to text and its diameter `Requires numeric distance or second point.`, and a radius or a diameter of nought or below says `Value must be positive and nonzero.` and is asked again, where CIRCLE ended with that line. DONUT's inside diameter takes nought and says `Value must be positive.` below it (it took the absolute value), its outside diameter says `Value must be positive and nonzero.` at nought and below, each asked again (they took the absolute value and went on). UNDO asks `Enter the number of operations to undo or [Auto/Control/BEgin/End/Mark/Back] <1>:` after `Current settings: Auto = On, Control = All, Combine = Yes, Layer = Yes`, and says `Requires an integer between 1 and 32767, or option keyword.` to text, 1.5, nought, a negative number and 32768 or more, asking again, where nought ended with `Requires a positive integer.`; Mark and Back are built (Back takes the steps down to the mark, `Mark encountered`, or asks `This will undo everything. OK? <Y>` with none), Auto, Control, BEgin and End say they are not built.

**CHANGED.** ARRAYRECT and ARRAYPOLAR ask `Enter the number of columns or [Expression] <4>:` and `Enter the number of rows or [Expression] <3>:`, where they said `Enter number of columns` and `Enter number of rows`, and `Select grip to edit array or [...]<eXit>:` with the default straight after the brackets as AutoCAD writes it. SCALE asks `Specify scale factor or [Copy/Reference]:` with no default shown, as AutoCAD 2021 does, and Enter takes the factor used last, 1 at first, as it did. The line `Type = Rectangular  Associative = No` stays: the arrays are made as separate objects (ARRAYASSOCIATIVITY 0), where AutoCAD says Yes.

**NEW.** The point modifiers FROM, M2P, TT, TK and the point filters, and the object snaps, are taken at `Select objects:` and at a prompt for one object, and at the corner of a window and the point of a fence, as AutoCAD 2021 takes them (probed through the standard input of accoreconsole: TT, FROM, M2P, TK, `.X`, `_end`, `_per`, typed with and without the underscore). The point a modifier gives picks as a click does, with no line of its own: ERASE, `Select objects: FROM`, `Base point: 0,-10`, `<Offset>: @50,10` and then `1 found` for the line from (0, 0) to (100, 0); M2P from (0, 0) and (100, 0) and TK from (50, -30) to (50, 0) ended by Enter do the same. A point on no object is the first corner of the window, `Select objects: FROM`, `Base point: 0,0`, `<Offset>: @-10,-10`, then `Specify opposite corner:`, where FROM with `@110,60` ends a window over two lines, `2 found`; at a prompt for one object a point on none asks again. TT gives no point (`Specify temporary OTRACK point:`, then `Select objects:` asked again). Text no modifier takes is refused as AutoCAD refuses it there: `*Invalid selection*` with `Expects a point or` and the options, FROM, M2P and TK's `Next point` asking their own prompt again, and the rest handing the text to `Select objects:`; Enter at FROM's, TT's or a filter's prompt ends the selection. The Shift+right-click menu is shown at these prompts too (it was shown at a point alone, and a modifier chosen from it at `Select objects:` was answered as text, `*Invalid selection*`), its Command menu's Osnap Overrides is enabled there, and a snap chosen or typed (`END`) takes the click to the point it finds near it, where the object is picked. A modifier chosen at a corner of a window or a point of a fence was answered as the next answer of the command waiting; it gives the corner or the point. `SelectObjectsModifierTests` (22 cases), `SelectObjectsMenuInterfaceTests` (9).

**CHANGED.** A point typed at `Select objects:` that lies on no object starts the implied window, `Select objects: 150,150` and then `Specify opposite corner:`, where the presenter wrote `0 found` and asked `Select objects:` again, as AutoCAD 2021 does at its console (probed through a script and through the standard input, with 150,150 on screen and -50,-50 off it, and with a typed pick through a modifier); a click on an object, and a typed point on one, still pick it.

**FIXED.** A prompt for a number refuses what it cannot take in the words AutoCAD 2021 gives that prompt, and asks again (probed in its console with text, 2.5, nought, a negative number and one past the most). POLYGON's sides said `Requires an integer value or option keyword.` to text and 2.5, and say `Requires an integer between 3 and 1024.` as they do to 2, 0 and 1025. -ARRAY's rows, columns and items took 0 and went on, or ended the command with `Value must be positive and nonzero.`, and now say `Requires an integer between 1 and 32767.` to everything else and ask again. The counts of ARRAYRECT and ARRAYPOLAR and its levels took up to 100000 and went on to the next prompt after a refusal; they say `Requires a positive nonzero integer or option keyword.` to text and 2.5, `Value must be positive and nonzero.` to nought and below and `Requires an integer between 1 and 32767, or option keyword.` to 32768 and more, asking again. DIVIDE's segments say `Requires an integer between 2 and 32767, or option keyword.` to text and 2.5 (and without `, or option keyword` after Block); MEASURE's length says `Requires numeric distance, two points, or option keyword.` to text, where it said `second point`, and `Value must be positive and nonzero.` where it said `Requires a nonzero positive distance.`. A chamfer's two distances and its length on the first line, and a fillet's radius, below nought said `Value must be positive.` and left the command's options; they ask again as AutoCAD does. OFFSET's words were the same already. `PromptRefusalWordingTests` (38 cases).

**FIXED.** A DWG saved as R2000 or R2004 held its texts as UTF-8 bytes, which AutoCAD 2021 reads in the drawing's code page: its DXF of the R2000 file written from `text` read "Tiáº¿ng Viá»‡t cafÃ© æ—¥æœ¬èªž Ã˜ Â±" for "Tiếng Việt café 日本語 Ø ±". The texts of those versions are now written as AutoCAD writes them, in the bytes of the drawing's code page (`$DWGCODEPAGE`, ANSI_1252 where it names none) with a letter beyond the page as `\U+1EDB` ("é" is the byte 0xE9, "ế" is `\U+1EBF`; a drawing of ANSI_1251 holds "Привет" as six bytes), in every text of an object, of extended data, of an XRECORD and of a header: AutoCAD's DXF of the new file has the lines of letters of its DXF of its own file byte for byte. Of the 167 drawings of AutoCAD 2021's samples and of the tests written as R2000 and as R2004, the 143 whose texts are all ASCII were the same bytes as before this change alone and the 24 with a letter beyond it differed in their texts alone; R2007 and later are UTF-16 and unchanged.
**FIXED.** The associative network of a dynamic block that AutoCAD makes through its API ended with a second list of soft pointers (`90 1`, `330 82`) that the reader dropped, so that its DXF held 24 groups where AutoCAD's holds 25, and the writer left out of the handle stream. The reader gives the list and the writer writes it; the network of each of four drawings made through the API is AutoCAD's own bytes, and the networks of the Dynamic Blocks samples (a list of 0) are as before.
**FIXED.** A DWG saved as R2000 gives each viewport AutoCAD has numbered its viewport entity header, in a table of them (type 0x46 under the handle B, named by the header variable of the viewport entities, and a header of type 0x47 for each viewport, one that names none first, as AutoCAD lists them), and writes the viewport's frozen layers as hard pointers (handle code 5; R2004 and later keep code 4). The five viewports of the drawing `vports` are AutoCAD's own bits and handle codes but for the numbers of the headers they name. The headers take the handles past every handle of the drawing, those of the records left out too: taken from the last handle written they met the visual styles' handles, and AUDIT found `eNotThatKindOfClass` in 13 drawings of the samples. A drawing with no numbered viewport is as before.
**CHANGED.** A DWG saved as R2000, R2004 or R2007 keeps its materials and its table styles, which it left out below R2007 and R2010 (the dictionaries that named them came out empty): a material of R2000 or R2004 is a material of R2007 without its last six values, a table style its description, flow, margins, rows and colours in the form of R2004 with the CELLSTYLEMAP and its dictionary under it. The three materials, the table style, its cell styles and their dictionaries of AutoCAD's own R2000 files (`text`, `tables`) and of its R2004 file (`props`) are its bytes (the table style of `table` lacks one reactor, its tables not being written before R2010). The visual styles (before R2013), the detail and section view styles (before R2018) and the tables (before R2010) are still left out. The 167 drawings of the corpus written as R2010, R2013 and R2018 are the same bytes as before (501 of 501).
**CHANGED.** `SetDataLink`, `RemoveDataLink()` and `RemoveDataLink(row, column)` of a table read from a file read the links from the cells the table keeps of its TABLECONTENT and write the cell they change, as the merges, rows and columns do, where each read the groups of the whole record three or four times (the links of every cell, the place of the cell, the tail of the record from it) and wrote them all again to put one 92 right. The links the TABLECONTENT names are found in the groups of the cells it holds, in the same places `GroupsOf` gives them (so that `IsLinked`, `GetDataLink` and `GetDataLinkRange` read what they read), the state, the 92 and the run of the link of a cell are changed in the groups of that cell, and the record is written by copying the bytes of every other cell. In a table of 300 rows by 6 columns (1 800 cells, 90 000 groups in its TABLECONTENT, a drawing of 2.1 MB) read from a file, medians of 15 on .NET Framework 4.8 (.NET 10 in brackets): a link put in takes 2.8 ms (2.9) where it took 43.9 (31.3), a link taken away 5.0 ms (3.0) where 54.8 (44.7), and every link taken away 7.7 ms (2.9) where 59.0 (42.3); the first of them, which reads the record to keep its cells, 28.6 ms (21.9) where 56.6 (38.3). Ten links put in and taken away again allocate 147 MB where 1 551 MB. A TABLECONTENT whose groups do not stand as the file writes them (a comment among them, carriage returns where the file has line feeds, a code not padded as the others are), or that holds extended data, is read and written whole, as before. The saved bytes are the same: the hashes of 60 runs of 120 edits (links put in and taken away among rows and columns put in and taken out, merges, texts and heights, with what the table says of its links asked between them) on tables as the library writes them and on tables whose TABLECONTENT holds a comment, extended data, carriage returns, codes not padded, an escape and a letter beyond ASCII, and those of 720 further runs of 100 edits on tables of 8 by 6 and of 30 by 9 cells, are those of the library before, as is each run on a table read anew before every edit (`DxfSpeed25Tests`).
**CHANGED.** The first edit of the TABLECONTENT of a table read from a file (a merge, a row put in, a link) found where each row and cell stand in the record's bytes by making a string of every group of it, 90 000 for 1 800 cells, and writing every group out again to see that the record stands as the file writes it. It finds them from the codes of the groups and the bytes of the markers, compares each group with the bytes the file writes it as (its code padded as the file pads one, its value a text of ASCII with no escape in it; any other group is written and compared as before), and makes the strings of a cell's groups only when an edit asks for them (a merge that empties the cell, a link, a field): a row or a column put in or taken out looks at the 92 of each cell in the bytes, and asks for the groups of those that name a link alone. In the table of 1 800 cells the first merge takes 13.5 ms where it took 29.6 on .NET Framework 4.8 (8.4 ms where 13.3 on .NET 10) and allocates 24 MB where 46, and the first row put in 14.9 ms where it took 32.7 (8.2 where 24.7). The saved bytes are the same, in the runs of the entry before and on a TABLECONTENT of each of the forms that does not stand as the file writes it.
**CHANGED.** The groups of a table's own record that an edit changes are copied once, the copy the edit changes, and what they are compared with to find that the edit changed nothing is the list of the layout the copy was made from, not a second copy of it: twenty heights of rows set in the table of 1 800 cells allocate 41.6 MB where 60.4 on .NET Framework 4.8 (33.4 MB where 43.3 on .NET 10). The handle of a table, asked for after an edit wrote its record anew, is read from the first groups of the record where it took the walk that reads a look, over every group of it: 0.01 ms where it took 0.26 on .NET 10 (0.23 ms on .NET Framework 4.8), a hundred heights set, each followed by the handle, taking 53.3 ms where 104.7 on .NET Framework 4.8 (28.8 where 60.6 on .NET 10). The owner of a record, which what the links let go of asks for (of the TABLECONTENT, which owns the fields), is found from the first groups too, where it was found after a list of every group of the megabytes of the record was made. The saved bytes are the same, in the runs of the first entry.

**CHANGED.** The links a table read from a file reads of its TABLECONTENT (`IsLinked`, `GetDataLink`, `GetDataLinkRange`, and what `SetDataLink` and `RemoveDataLink` look at first) are found without making the strings of the groups of the cells the table has not read, and kept for as long as the TABLECONTENT stands. The table kept its cells and made a string of every group of them, 150 000 for 1 800 cells, to find the 1 800 markers, states and links among them; the groups are now looked at in the bytes of the record where they stand (a search for the next group of a code, a comparison of a group's text with the bytes of it, as the first merge already did for the groups of its cells), and a string is made only for a marker, a state or the run of a link that is asked for. What was read is kept for the record it was read of, the same bytes in the same place, so that a height, a text, a column's width or a style set in the table's own record, which leaves the TABLECONTENT as it is, does not make `IsLinked` read it all again: after an edit of the TABLECONTENT (a merge, a row, a link) it is read again, as it was after each edit. In a table of 300 rows by 6 columns (1 800 cells, a drawing of 2.1 MB) read from a file, medians of 25 on .NET Framework 4.8 (.NET 10 in brackets, a full collection before each timing): the first link put in takes 15.0 ms (8.4) where it took 28.8 (11.7) and allocates 18.3 MB (18.0) where 31.0 (27.9); `IsLinked` after a height set takes 0.14 ms (0.07) where it took 14.5 (5.6) in a table not linked yet and 1.6 (0.95) in one that keeps its cells; every link taken away takes 4.7 ms (2.5) where it took 14.6 (3.4); twenty heights set, each followed by two questions of the table's links, allocate 59.6 MB where 336.3 (.NET Framework 4.8). The kinds of the rows, which a row put in or taken out at the title or the header asks for after each writing of the TABLECONTENT, are counted from the style of each row the table keeps of it, where the bytes of the record were looked through for each `TABLEROW_BEGIN`; the kinds that come out are the same, since the rows are read for their styles whenever the count is above what the table shows, and a count of the rows is never above the count of the bytes. A row put in and taken out among 300 rows takes 4.1 ms where it took 4.4 on .NET Framework 4.8 (2.4 ms where 2.9 on .NET 10), medians of ten runs of 80 edits. A table that keeps no cells (extended data after its TABLECONTENT, groups not as the file writes them) reads as before. The saved bytes, and what the table says of its links and of the kinds of its rows, are the same: the hashes of 42 runs of 100 edits (links put in and taken away among rows put in and taken out at the title, the header and further down, heights, texts, widths, merges, formulas and rows that inherit, with the links and kinds asked after each) are those of the library before, as are those of 756 further runs of 80 edits on tables of 5 by 4, 9 by 6 and 30 by 9 cells of each of the seven forms of the TABLECONTENT of `DxfSpeed25Tests`, and what the table says after each edit of 252 runs of 40 edits is what a table read anew from the drawing's text says (`DxfSpeed29Tests`). A handle of one or two digits still makes the search the file is made for what points at a field or a link read every record: no search of the bytes tells a pointer of two digits from the code lines of every record, and an index of the pointers to fields would be read again after each edit, so that it would spare no record between two edits.

**FIXED.** A DWG saved as R2000, R2004, R2007 or R2010 left its visual styles out, so that the dictionary that names them came out empty, and one saved as R2013 gave them no stamp of the version they were saved by, which every style of AutoCAD's own files before R2018 carries (`AcDbSavedByObjectVersion` of 0 in its extended data). They are written as AutoCAD writes them: of R2000, R2004 and R2007 the 28 properties each in a place of its own (R2007 with one real more), of R2010 the type, the version and the use, then the 28 properties each with how it is applied, with the stamp and the extension dictionary that holds the 30 properties R2013 added. The 24 visual styles of AutoCAD's own R2000 file `text` and the 25 of its R2004, R2007, R2010 and R2013 files of one drawing, each written again from the DXF the reader makes of the file, are AutoCAD's own bytes (124 of 124, handle references included); the same drawing's R2018 file written as R2004, R2007, R2010 and R2013 gives AutoCAD's own styles group for group, but for the lighting model of one style, which AutoCAD's R2004 and R2007 files hold as 2 and a DXF of R2018 cannot say.
**FIXED.** A DWG saved as R2000 to R2013 left its detail and section view styles out (the dictionaries that name them came out empty). They are written as AutoCAD writes them, as the style of R2018 less its display name and its flags, which a file before R2018 keeps as `DISPLAYNAME` and `FLAGS` in the `ACAD_XREC_ROUNDTRIP` record of the style's extension dictionary: a style of R2018 going down (in `DwgWriter`, and in `DxfDatabase.Save` to a DXF of R2013 or before) is given that dictionary and record, a style of an older file written as R2018 takes them back into its own groups, and the dictionary and the record are not written then. The default styles of AutoCAD's own files `text` and `matvis` in R2000, R2004, R2007, R2010 and R2013 and the two styles of its own of `views_AC1018` are written again as AutoCAD's bytes (12 of 12), and the styles of its R2004, R2007 and R2010 files written as R2018 are the bytes of its own R2018 file (6 of 6). The colours of a view style are not in a DXF of R2000, so the two styles of its own of `views_AC1015` differ from AutoCAD's bytes in their colours alone.
**FIXED.** A DWG saved as R2000 had no table of viewport entity headers where the drawing has no numbered viewport, though every file of R2000 AutoCAD writes has it, empty (the object B of 22 bits, and the header variable of the viewport entities naming it, `HB`, where the writer wrote 0). The four files of R2000 AutoCAD wrote of the test drawings (`text`, `tables`, `curves`, `polys`) give AutoCAD's own object and header variable when written again.
**FIXED.** A table style of a DWG saved as R2000, R2004 or R2007 that came from a drawing of R2010 or later had no map of cell styles, which AutoCAD writes for each style it saves so (a DWG of R2018 holds none), and AutoCAD's DXFOUT of the file then made one itself with six borders in each cell style (`94 6`) where its own file of the same drawing has none (`94 0`). The CELLSTYLEMAP is made now, in the style's extension dictionary or in one made for it, from the style's three rows. Compared through AutoCAD 2021's DXFOUT of the file written as R2007 and of its own R2007 file of the same drawing, the 11 table styles and maps of eight drawings are the same group for group but for the reactor of a table (not written before R2010), a style with no name whose rows name no text style (written with Standard, which AUDIT cannot repair without) and the style Standard of `tcustom`, whose R2018 object holds a margin and borders of its own equal to the defaults that a DXF cannot carry; the map written for the style Standard of `ttable` is AutoCAD's own bytes but for the handles. In R2000 and R2004 the same DXFOUT listed six borders in each cell style even of the maps that were AutoCAD's own bytes, because the file header named the version of the format (23 and 15, 25 and 104) where AutoCAD 2021 names itself (33 and 174) in the bytes 0x11 and 0x12 of every file it writes before R2018 (and at 0x16 and 0x17 in R2004), and recomposes the cell styles of a file that names another; the header names it now, and the DXFOUT of the files written from six drawings is that of AutoCAD's own files in R2000 and R2004 as in R2007, but for the style Standard of `tcustom`.
**NEW.** A DWG saved as R2000, R2004 or R2007 holds its tables, which it left out below R2010 (the table style then lacked the reactor that names each table, and a drawing of R2018 written so was counted as having left its tables out). An ACAD_TABLE before R2010 is written as AutoCAD 2021 writes it: its block reference, its flags, columns and rows with their sizes, its style, each cell (kind, edges, merging, size, turn, the field or block it holds or, before R2007, its words, the values the cell's flags name, and from R2007 its value) and the overrides of the whole table, with the round trip under its extension dictionary that AutoCAD keeps (the TABLECONTENT and the TABLEGEOMETRY, and in R2000 and R2004 a DATATABLE, ACDBDATATABLE in R2000, with the checksum of each cell's words and the XRECORD that holds its value). The DXF of R2000 and R2004 holds the flags of a cell in a signed 16 bits and the file holds more, the bit four places up beside each of the flags 0x400 to 0x2000 and 0x40000 in a cell with words: AutoCAD refused the file (ErrorStatus 53) in 6 of the 21 files written from the seven table drawings (`ttable`, `tstyles`, `tclean`, `tcustom`, `table`, `tall`, `tcell`) until the writer added them. The ACAD_TABLE, TABLECONTENT, TABLEGEOMETRY and DATATABLE of AutoCAD's own R2000, R2004 and R2007 files of `table` (two tables), written again from the DXF the reader makes of them, are its bytes, handle references included; the 21 files of the seven drawings written as R2000, R2004 and R2007 open with AUDIT 0 (21 of 21), and AutoCAD's DXFOUT of the tables, their content, geometry and data tables is that of its own file of the drawing, but for the proxy graphics of R2000 (AutoCAD draws them anew, 2 544 bytes where 2 880), the flag 4 of an empty value in R2007 and the masks of the data table (`DxfVersionConverter` gives AutoCAD's for `table` and not for `ttable`, `tstyles`, `tall` and `tcell`, where AutoCAD writes 0 in the second column of two). A table with a number or a field in a cell, or a general value with nothing in it (`tclean`, `tcustom`), is still written as the block it is drawn with in R2000 and R2004, as `DxfVersionConverter` makes it; R2007 writes them as tables. `DwgObjectReader` gives the overrides of the whole table of a DWG before R2007 before the sizes of the rows, as AutoCAD's DXF has them, and names the text style a cell or the table overrides, where it gave them after the cells and by handle, so that a table of AutoCAD's own R2000 file keeps them going to R2010 and later too.
**CHANGED.** The file header of a DWG saved as R2010 or R2013 names AutoCAD 2021 as the application that saved it (33 and the maintenance release 174 at 0x11, 0x12, 0x16 and 0x17), as the header of every file AutoCAD 2021 writes of those versions does, where the writer named the version of the format (29 and 226, 31 and 125). Whether AutoCAD then recomposes the tables and the maps of cell styles, as it does of a file of R2000 and R2004 that names another, was probed: its DXFOUT of the files written from the seven table drawings as R2010 and R2013 (14 files with the old header, 14 with the new one) lists the same tables, table styles and maps with either, differing from its own files of the drawings in the same records, so the header is matched and nothing else changes. The 150 drawings of the 167 of the corpus that hold no table style with a margin or a border of its own are the same bytes as before but for those four bytes.
**FIXED.** The colours of a detail or section view style of a drawing of R2018 written as a DWG of R2000 were lost: AutoCAD's own R2000 file holds each as its index in the object (the true colour of the first style of `views`, 706590, is lost, its index 102 kept; AutoCAD keeps no record of them, and its DXF of R2000 has none), and the DXF of R2000 `DxfVersionConverter` makes has no group 62 for it, so the writer gave every part the colour by layer. The converter keeps the group in the text it makes for a DWG (not in a DXF of R2000, where AutoCAD has none), and the section view style of its own of `views` is AutoCAD's bytes in its data, colours included. A true colour (420) of a view style no longer stays in a DXF of R2000 either, where AutoCAD's DXF has none.
**FIXED.** The face lighting model of the visual style Realistic of a drawing of R2018 or R2010 written as R2000, R2004 or R2007 (a DWG, or a DXF of those versions) was 3, which those versions lack; AutoCAD saves it as 2, as its own files of the drawing in R2004 and R2007 hold it (the 25 styles of `matvis` written from its R2018 file are now AutoCAD's group for group in R2004 and R2007, and in R2010 and R2013 as before).
**NEW.** XCLIP Clipdepth cuts a circle, an arc and a polyline that cross a plane, as it cuts a line, as AutoCAD 2021 draws them (PNGOUT of accoreconsole, front view and
plan): a circle standing on its edge (radius 30, about (50, 20, 0), in the plane of X and Z) with front 10 and back -10 is left as the two arcs at the ends of its width, x 20 to 21.72
and 78.28 to 80; the zigzag (10, 0), (30, 30), (50, -30), (90, 20) in X and Z is left as three pieces, x 10 to 16.67, 36.67 to 43.33 and 66 to 82. A lightweight polyline is cut in each
of its line and arc segments (the arc segment's wave of heights is solved, not sampled) and at a vertex that stands on a plane, a closed one included, and its pieces keep its widths and
look. What an INSERT inside the clipped block holds is cut by the same planes carried through the INSERT's placing: the block of the five lines nested in another, scaled by 2 and lifted 5,
with front 20 and back -10, shows its rising line from x 0 to 15 (AutoCAD 2021 left 15), and a nested block tilted 45 degrees about X shows the first 20 of its line in plan, as AutoCAD does. An
external reference is cut by the planes measured from its base point, which stands at the insertion point: the drawing whose base point is (0, 0, 10) stands 10 lower and its rising line is
left for 30 of x where one at (0, 0, 0) leaves 20 (AutoCAD 2021's PNGOUT of both). A hatch and text that cross a plane are still drawn whole.
**NEW.** A clip made in a system tilted out of the plan shows each entity of the block where the boundary's prism meets the plane at the entity's own height, not only at the block's plane:
a grid at height 50 under the boundary that shows a grid at height 0 from y 73.09 to 130.83 shows from y 44.23 to 101.96, as AutoCAD 2021's PNGOUT draws it. An entity that does not lie flat
and is none of the lines and curves of the entry after this one keeps the ring of the block's plane. A clip whose plane is parallel to the block's, which is every clip the presenter makes, is drawn as before.
**NEW.** XCLIP Clipdepth cuts an ellipse, a spline, a heavy 2D polyline and a 3D polyline that cross a plane, as AutoCAD 2021 draws them (PNGOUT of accoreconsole, front view): an ellipse of semi-axes 30 along x and 15
along z about (50, 0), with front 10 and back -10, is left as the two arcs x 20 to 27.64 and 72.36 to 80 (50 -+ 30 cos(asin(10 / 15))); a spline through the points (150, 0), (170, 30), (190, -30), (220, 20) is left as three pieces, x 150 to 154.94, 178.91 to 183.26 and 207.53 to
216.07; the zigzag (300, 0), (330, 30), (350, -30), (390, 20) as a heavy polyline, and (450, 0), (480, 30), (500, -30), (540, 20) as a 3D polyline, as three pieces each, as the lightweight one is. A spline is cut where its height meets a plane, found by halving a step of its parameter, and a heavy
polyline in each line segment, each arc segment (its wave of heights solved) and at each vertex on a plane. The lines and curves of a dimension's picture and of a table's are cut by the planes of the block the dimension or the table stands in, as the entities of a block are:
AutoCAD cuts a hatch, text, a dimension's text and a solid at the plane too, glyph by glyph and pixel by pixel (probed, front view, planes 10 and -10: a hatch, text of height 40, an MTEXT, a dimension and a solid are all left from z -10 to 10), which the display, that keeps no height to cut them by, still draws whole.
**NEW.** A line or a curve of a block that does not lie flat is cut by the prism of a clip made in a system tilted out of the plan, where its path leaves the boundary seen along the clip's normal, in no ring: a line from (50, -100, 0) to (50, 100, 60) under a boundary tilted 30 degrees about X, y from -40 to 40, shows from y -54.13
to 24.61 (AutoCAD 2021's PNGOUT: -54.2 to 24.5), where the ring of the plane at height 0 gave -46.19 to 46.19; a circle of radius 30 standing about (50, 0, 40) in the plane of Y and Z loses the arc from -18.19 to 78.19 degrees and is left from y -30 to 28.50.
**NEW.** A line or a curve of a dashed linetype that Clipdepth, or the prism of a tilted clip, cuts goes on with the pattern of the whole, as AutoCAD 2021 draws it (PNGOUT of a DASHED line and of two polylines, PLINEGEN on and off, across the planes 10 and -10: every dash of every piece falls on a dash of the whole): the dashes of the pieces of
a zigzag start where those of the whole stood, 20 + 6.67 along the plan for the second, and none restarts at the cut. `DisplayStyle` has an internal `DashPhase` (drawing units) that the canvas gives its dashes.
**FIXED.** The cells of a MINSERT of a plane tilted out of the plan stood a spacing apart in the plan, where AutoCAD 2021 shows them a spacing times the cosine of the tilt apart, and each higher by the spacing times its sine: an array of 1 column by 3 rows, the rows 40 apart, of a plane tilted 45 degrees about X, has its lines at y 0, 28.28 and 56.57 (AutoCAD 2021: 0.2, 28.1 and 56.5, to a pixel), not 0, 40 and 80, and under the planes
front 20 and back -10 only the first is left, the others standing at 28.28 and 56.57 high. The planes of Clipdepth carried into an array go through the height of the cell as well as its place.
**FIXED.** XCLIP generate Polyline draws the polyline where the boundary stands, not on the plane of the world: a boundary made in a system lifted 15 gives a polyline of elevation 15, and one
made in a system at (100, 50, 20) turned 30 degrees about X (AutoCAD 2021 wrote both) the polyline of the normal (0, -0.5, 0.866), elevation -7.679 and vertices (110, 63.30), (190, 63.30),
(190, 113.30), (110, 113.30) in its own system, where it was flat at elevation 0 whatever the boundary's plane.
**FIXED.** A DXF of R2010 or R2007 saved as R2013 or R2018 (`Save(path, "AC1027")`, `"AC1032"`) kept the associative network of a dynamic block in the layout of the older version, which AutoCAD 2021 does not read
there: it discarded the drawing at the first constraint group (`ACDBASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP ... Premature end of object`, `ErrorStatus` 53), as it refused 4 of 4 files of its own R2010 DXF of the sample drawings so saved. The converter brings it up as AutoCAD does when it
saves such a drawing: each action (network, variable, group) at version 2 with four numbers of 0 after its three, and a group of constraints in the second layout, two numbers and a flag of 0 past its next identifier, then the count of
its nodes, a directory of every node as class and identifier, and the nodes by identifier without their class, a circle and an arc with a fourth real of 0 after their three. The 13 DXF files of R2010 that AutoCAD writes of the 13 `Dynamic Blocks` samples, saved as R2018 and R2013,
and the 13 of R2007 saved as R2018 (39 files), open in AutoCAD with `AUDIT` finding the errors of its own DWG of R2010 of each (0, 2, 10 and 0 in Architectural - Metric, Civil - Imperial, Mechanical - Metric and Structural - Imperial), and 3 196 of
the 3 204 dynamic objects of the 13 drawings equal AutoCAD's DXF of R2018 of its own DWG of R2010 of each, group for group and in order (the other 8 are stretch actions of Mechanical - Imperial whose entities AutoCAD's two DXF files list in another order, the converter keeping the order
it is given). A text goes up where an action says version 1, whatever its header says; an action at version 2 and a drawing saved in its own version are as they were. A DWG read from a file of R2010 or R2007 names that version in its header and holds the first layout
(`DwgReader.ToDxf`; the text matches its header), so it is taken up when it is saved as R2013 or R2018 and is the text it was when it is saved in its own version (a test pins both).

**FIXED.** A group of constraints that holds an ellipse (`AcConstrainedEllipse`), an ellipse with end points (`AcConstrainedBoundedEllipse`) or a concentric constraint (`AcConcentricConstraint`), made in AutoCAD by constraining an ellipse or an elliptical arc
or two concentric curves, was left out of a DWG read as a broken object (`A constraint group holds a node of a class the reader does not know`), left in the layout it had by a DXF save to another version (which AutoCAD refused in R2010 and R2007), and left out of a DWG written. The three classes are known: a concentric
constraint holds what a tangent one does, an ellipse its pointer, a number, its centre, major axis and ratio, and a bounded one its two end points after them, in the first layout and the second alike (no fourth real). In two drawings made through AutoCAD's API (seven circles and arcs
with tangent, concentric and equal radius constraints, and one with an ellipse, an elliptical arc and a line) the group of the DWG of R2018, R2010 and R2007 reads as AutoCAD's own DXF, group for group; written again, the group of R2018 and of R2010 is AutoCAD's own bytes, and the DXF saves in each direction equal AutoCAD's DXF of each
version. AutoCAD opens the 18 files made with `AUDIT` finding the errors of its own file (4 in the first drawing, from the constraints set, none in the second) and refused the two R2010 DXF files the converter gave before.
**FIXED.** A point modifier chosen from the Shift+right-click menu where AutoCAD 2021 does not take it is refused on the command line as typing it is: `Base point: _tt` and then `Point or option keyword required.` (`Invalid point.` where the prompt it was typed at has no options, `Invalid 2D point.` inside TK), and the prompt asks again, where the menu did nothing and said nothing. The pairs are those of AutoCAD 2021's console, probed one inside another: TT and TK are taken at a command's own prompt and inside M2P and nowhere else, inside TT and TK only M2P is taken, FROM and the point filters are taken inside FROM, M2P and a filter, and M2P is not taken inside M2P at any depth. TT and TK inside M2P were refused and are taken; FROM and a filter inside TT or TK (FROM, not a filter, was refused inside TK) are refused; M2P inside M2P was taken and is refused (`Point or option keyword required.`, `First point of mid:` asked again). What TT or a filter refuses goes to the prompt it was typed at as text, and no longer starts a modifier there: `_tt` typed at TT's own prompt asked for a second temporary track point, where AutoCAD says `Invalid point.` and asks `Specify first point:` again. A modifier chosen where no point is asked (`MainViewModel.ModifyPoint` called at the integer prompt of POLYGON) is answered by the prompt waiting as the word typed there is. `PointModifierNestingTests` (39 cases) and `PointModifierRefusalInterfaceTests` (4).

**CHANGED.** An open chain of arcs in space (`GeoPolylineArc3`, which an open polyline with a bulge in a tilted plane is read as) whose arcs share one normal, and whose last vertex is given no bulge and no normal, keeps no array of normals, as a closed loop does since the work of speed16: an edge reads its normal from the one the chain holds, `Normals` makes the array when it is asked for and keeps it (the same one for every call and every thread), and `GetNormalAt`, `GetEdgeAt`, `Equals`, `Clone`, `Translate` and the display read the normal of an edge without making it. The constructor also reads the lists it is given where they stand, and keeps its vertices and bulges in arrays, where it grew three lists a vertex at a time: a chain of five vertices with one arc is built with 272 bytes where it took 1 648 (.NET Framework 4.8) and in 85 ms for 300 000 where it took 137, and 20 000 open polylines with a bulge in a tilted plane are displayed with 812 bytes a polyline where they took 1 636 (cold display 72 ms where 76, within the noise). The last vertex, which no edge leaves, keeps the bulge and the normal it is given as it was given, so a chain given either keeps its array, as does one with arcs of two normals (a bulge about (0, 0, 1) and one about (0, 0, -1)), one with two vertices on each other, and a chain made of edges; every number the chain holds is the bit it was: 3 600 chains at random (vertices on each other, a bulge or a normal on the last vertex, normals of two directions, of lengths 1, 2 and 1.0000000000000002 and of none, lists short or missing) are read by the constructor as it was before and as it is, or refused by both (`DxfSpeed24Tests`, 14, 1 red on the older code by bytes allocated; `DisplaySpeed24Tests`, 4, 1 red).

**CHANGED.** The search of the file for what else points at a field a cell lets go of (`DxfField.Erase`, behind a merge across a field, a text set or a reset over one, and `SetFormula` over another
formula) passes over the records that cannot point at a handle of digits alone, as it did for a handle with a letter in it. A pointer's value is the handle's digits with nothing but zeros, spaces and
tabs before them and spaces, tabs and the end of the line after them, so only a record whose bytes hold the digits as the whole of a value line is read group by group; a number that holds the same
digits (`190.5`, `1190`) is not one. Up to four such handles of three digits or more are looked for in one search; a handle of one or two digits, or more than four of digits alone, have every record read,
as before. In a table of 49 rows by 19 columns (931 cells) read from a file, ten merges across a cell holding a field numbered from 700000 read 10 records group by group where they read 1 375, each
taking 1.3 ms on .NET Framework 4.8 (1.8 ms on .NET 10) where it took 3.4 ms (3.6), and a field numbered 190 takes 1.9 ms (1.6) where it took 4.7 (2.8); a field with a letter in its handle takes what it took
(1.5 ms, 1.0 on .NET 10), and a text set over a cell holding a field, whose handles run from digits alone to a letter among them, takes 1.7 ms (1.4) where it took 3.0 (2.5) (medians of three runs on a machine other work
shared). The cell that a row or a column put in is made of, 49 groups of a TABLECONTENT, is copied from one made once, not written out group by group with a number formatted for each, the layout kept for the record
a row or a column put in made is the list the edit built, not a copy of it, and the table's extension dictionary is read from the record the cells a merge wrote were counted from, not from the record put together
with them, a copy of its 1.1 MB: twenty rows put in and twenty taken out of the 931 cells allocate 186.8 MB where they allocated 199.6, eight columns put in and eight taken out 94.8 MB where 100.2, and twenty merges
each followed by an unmerge 61.9 MB where 66.9. The saved bytes are the same: the hashes of 48 runs of 120 edits among fields numbered from 9000 and from 70000, those of the 64 runs of `DxfSpeed21Tests`, and of 21 000
searches among records made at random (the handles looked for of digits alone, of digits and letters, and of one or two digits; pointers with zeros, spaces and tabs before and after, in either case, and numbers that
only look like them) are those of the library before (`DxfSpeed22Tests`).
**FIXED.** A DXF saved as R2010 or R2007 (`Save(path, "AC1024")`, `"AC1021"`) held the associative network of a dynamic block in the layout of R2018, which AutoCAD 2021 does not read
there: it discarded the drawing at the first constraint group (`ACDBASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP ... Premature end of object`, `ErrorStatus` 53), as it did the 8 `Dynamic Blocks` samples that hold groups
(34 in all). The converter takes it down as AutoCAD does when it saves such a drawing: the network, the variables and the groups at version 1 without their four numbers more, and the nodes of
a group by identifier with their class, their group, identifier and byte, the identifiers they name and what their class holds, a circle and an arc with three reals where the version 2 has four (the
fourth is 0 in every sample, and in 21 curves made through the API as circles, arcs turned the other way, an arc through the zero angle and a circle with a thickness, fixed, tangent, concentric,
of equal radius and solved; an ellipse keeps its ratio in a place of its own). The DWG writer reads the converter's text for R2010 and R2007 (it kept its own conversion for a drawing it is given as it
is): the 1 080 files the 167 drawings of the corpus and the 13 R2018 saves give as the six versions are the same bytes as before. The 8 samples saved as DXF of R2010 and R2007 open with `AUDIT` at the 0, 2, 10 and 0 errors of
Architectural - Metric, Civil - Imperial, Mechanical - Metric and Structural - Imperial that AutoCAD's own DXF of each gives, and 3 204 dynamic objects of the 13 drawings in R2007 and 3 203
in R2010 equal AutoCAD's own DXF group for group and in order (the other is a group whose actions AutoCAD lists in another order in its DXF of R2010 than in that of R2018). A group with a
node of a class the library does not know (`AcConcentricConstraint`, `AcConstrainedEllipse`, `AcConstrainedBoundedEllipse`) is left in the layout it has, as before.

**CHANGED.** The entities a stretch action binds are read from a DWG in the order the file keeps them, and the actions a group of constraints owns are written in the order the groups give, where the
reader sorted the entities by handle and the writer the actions. AutoCAD keeps both in an order of its own, which is no order of their handles (a turn of the handle order, `4FB8 4FB9 4FBB 4FAA 4FB0
4FB7` for the handles `4FAA` to `4FBB`), and gives its own DXF a third order that turns the file's into another each time a drawing is saved and read again. Read in the file's order, AutoCAD's
DXF of the 13 `Dynamic Blocks` originals lists the entities of its stretch actions as the file does in all but 4 of the 115 (7 by handle), that of the R2010 files it saves from them in all (5 by
handle) and that of the R2018 files in all but 10 (13 by handle); the 102 stretch actions and the 34 groups of its R2018 files, and the 34 groups of its R2010 files, written again from the DXF the
reader makes of them are AutoCAD's own bytes (the handle order wrote all 34 groups' handle streams differently). The 13 R2018 saves written as R2010 and R2007 and saved by AutoCAD as DXF differ from its
own DXF in 5 and 6 objects where 8 and 14 did. Of the 1 080 files of the corpus run, the 56 of R2007 to R2018 of the 14 drawings that hold groups or stretch actions change, and their `AUDIT`
verdict is that of the file before (32 files at 0 errors, 16 at 2, 8 at 10); the 1 024 others are the same bytes.
**CHANGED.** The cold display of a drawing of 1 000 000 entities makes 404 MB of objects where it made 454, and a REGEN of it 244 MB where it made 276
(.NET 8; 412 MB where 462 under .NET Framework 4.8, collected 61 times where 69). Under .NET Framework 4.8 the cold display takes 2.36 s where it took 2.51
and a REGEN 0.97 s where 1.08 (best of six runs alternated with the older build, medians 2.48 s where 2.64 and 0.99 s where 1.12); under .NET 8 the cold
display takes 1.22 s where 1.27 (best of ten, medians 1.33 s where 1.36) and a REGEN 0.40 s as before, under .NET 10 1.20 s where 1.22 and 0.38 s where
0.39, within the noise of a machine that other work shares. What changed, each measured alone first:
- A chain of two vertices, which is its box and two flags and keeps no array, is made of its four numbers: a LINE, and the run of two vertices a closed
  polyline with an arc leaves before its arc, were each given an array of 56 bytes for the constructor to drop (31 MB of the cold display of 1 000 000
  entities). 200 000 lines are displayed with 50.0 MB of garbage where 60.7 (262 bytes a line where 318), 200 000 closed polylines with an arc with 142 MB where
  171, and 20 000 INSERTs of a block of 20 entities with 49 MB where 61 (.NET 8).
- A closed loop of arcs in space (`GeoPolygonArc3`, which a closed polyline with a bulge is read as) whose arcs share one normal keeps no array of normals:
  its edges read the normal from one the loop holds, a loop of four edges with one arc is built with 264 bytes where it took 360 (under .NET Framework 4.8),
  and the 200 000 of the drawing hold 18 MB less. `Normals` makes the list when it is asked for and keeps it, the same one for every call and every thread, and
  `GetNormalAt`, `GetEdgeAt`, `Equals`, `Clone` and `Translate` read the normal of an edge without making it. A loop whose arcs have normals of their own (a
  bulge about (0, 0, 1) and one about (0, 0, -1)), one with two corners on each other, and one whose arcs are given normals that differ in the last bit, keep the array as before.
  The display draws a loop through `GetNormalAt`.
- The style of a TEXT and the block of an INSERT are read as the one string the records before them spelled the same, among the last four the thread read, where
  each made a string of its own: 200 000 texts in the style Standard are displayed with 67 MB where 75 (a REGEN with 50 where 57). Only a name of printable ASCII of
  64 letters or fewer is shared; any other is read as it was.

The display lists, their boxes, runs and insertion points, the bytes a drawing saves and the pixels are the same: 167 samples of AutoCAD and six generated drawings
(200 000 loops, 200 000 texts in the style Standard, 20 000 INSERTs, 100 000 entities, a drawing of plates, the drawing of the viewer's samples) give the same list item for item
and field for field in every space, the same pixels in three views (plain, selected, highlighted, hovered), and the same bytes saved; the 1 000 000 mixed entities give the same list (.NET 8).
Not changed, with the reason: the 36 MB of entity objects (`DxfLine`, `DxfArc`, `DxfCircle`, `DxfPolyline`, `DxfDBText`) the display makes, because an entity object binds
itself to its record as it is made, so that dropping those the display made could drop one that another thread was given meanwhile, and one record would give two entities;
the shapes of the entities, which a display that does not keep them makes the heap 92 MB lighter (300 MB where 392) at the price of a REGEN of 0.83 to 1.0 s where it takes
0.43 to 0.55 (.NET 8), their numbers being read again each time; the box of an arc (25 MB) and the string of each handle (32 MB, shared by the record, the items and the run).
`DxfSpeed23Tests` (15) and `DisplaySpeed23Tests` (7).

**FIXED.** The arc point of an angular dimension whose words are put by DIMTEDIT (or by Properties) is written as AutoCAD 2021 writes it. It stood where the dimension was
made, a third of the way round from the first ray; AutoCAD writes two thirds where the point stands nearer the first ray than the second (as seen from the vertex, the short
way round) and a third where it stands nearer the second, on the arc it was on under DIMTMOVE 1 and 2 and through the point itself under 0, for an angle of three points
(group 10) and of two lines (group 16), the rays given either way round and for an angle past a half turn. An angle of 60 degrees from 0 with its words put at 215 degrees or at
22.7 degrees has it at 40 degrees, put at 100 or 35 at 20; exactly between the rays (30 and 210 degrees) AutoCAD's own rounding decides. AutoCAD's pictures differing from ours:
648 of three points and two lines under DIMTMOVE 0, 1 and 2 (p1) 326 before, 4 now; 576 with the rays the other way round and a reflex angle (p2) 151 and 17; the 558 pictures of
the jump of the band at the height of an arc's middle (d1, SHX) 70 and 11, and in Arial (td1) 64 and 2; the 13 968 pictures of a ring of words round an arc of 240 out (e3) 3 479 and
40 (26 of them at 210 degrees, between the rays).
**CHANGED.** The leader of an angle's words put by DIMTEDIT under DIMTMOVE 1 is read on every arc from 1.3 landings out (a landing is half the words, a gap and an arrowhead), and
by the band of AutoCAD 2021's pictures for each first ray. It was read by the rule from 2.5 landings out and by the fit before, and the table of the rule was fitted to an angle from 0
degrees: a first ray at 30 to 330 degrees has AutoCAD draw the leader up to 2.5 sooner or later on some directions (709 of 36 278 probes wrong, "60°" put every 0.25 at 36
directions round the angle at 30 out; 27 now) and an arc between 1.4 and 3.4 landings out is read by the table of the rule with a second one (1 238 wrong of 17 612 by the rule,
1 060 by the fit, 415 now); the correction falls off as one over the radius beyond 16 landings out, where the 240 out arcs had too much of it. Leader presence differing from
AutoCAD's pictures (the five exact directions left out): at 240 out e3 6 to 4 of 6 499 (Arial te3 7 to 4), e5 10 to 6 of 6 984 (te5 14 to 10); at 30 out e8 63 to 48 (te8 57 to
50), aq 93 to 75 and taq 75 to 63 of 6 860, ta8 1 to 0 of 165; worse: e1 1 to 2 of 3 492 (a probe at 0.016 of the edge) and te11 24 to 26 of 6 984. The first rays at 15 degrees'
steps (OrientedCorrections, 23 tables of 36 directions) were fitted to 79 000 probes: read from the 30 degrees' steps only, the 15 between them had 731 of 39 576 wrong and have
275; at 60 out 161 of 13 192 and 81. Angles of other sizes were not probed. 76 of the 111 sets of AutoCAD pictures (the radius, diameter, arc length, linear and redraw sets, tar1 to 26, t1 to
t11, d2 to d5, tw1 to 17, m2 to m6) are byte for byte what they were, the 35 that changed all hold an angle's words put by DIMTEDIT, and the pictures differing of those with an AutoCAD picture are the same or fewer (a5 18 to 17 of 2 938).
**FIXED.** The leader band of an angle's words put by DIMTEDIT is read by the direction of the angle's middle, not by its first ray, so that angles of other sizes than 60 degrees have the
band AutoCAD 2021 draws: the table for a first ray is read at the middle's direction less 30 degrees (the first ray itself for an angle of 60). "30°", "90°", "120°" and "150°" put every 0.25
at 36 directions round angles of those sizes from 0, 45, 90, ... 315 degrees, the arc 30 out (26 384 probes of each size) had 188, 208, 722 and 848 probes with the leader wrong and have 13, 25,
345 and 373 (Arial, 9 894 probes of 30 and 90 degrees from 45, 180 and 270: 102 and 105 before, 47 and 60); the two other indexes, the first and the second ray, leave 192 to 838. The 1.4
per cent left at 120 and 150 degrees is the words' width: "120°" put round an angle of 60 degrees has 371 of 25 481 wrong, where "60°" has 27 of 36 278, so words of other widths still have the
band of the narrow words. The pictures differing from AutoCAD's of angles given the other way round and reflex (p2) are 17 of 576 before and 6 now.
**CHANGED.** The correction of the leader band on arcs under 5.1 landings out is fitted across landings, where it was fitted to one (SHX's 5.83 for "60°"): rings of an angle of 60 degrees from 0
with DIMASZ 4, DIMTXT 4 and 1.8 and DIMSCALE 2 (SHX) and with Arial 2.5 and 4 high and at DIMSCALE 2, 1.5 to 4.5 landings out (114 000 probes of AutoCAD 2021's pictures), with the arcs of 30 and 45
out and the rings of 8 to 20 out. Leader presence differing from AutoCAD's pictures, before and now: e8 48 to 37 of 6 984 (Arial te8 50 to 38), e11 18 to 14 (te11 26 to 22, the loss of the last
round undone), taq 63 to 61 of 6 860; the rings of SHX's landings other than 5.83 1 590 to 1 486, of Arial 1 029 to 951; worse: aq 75 to 78 of 6 860 and the rings of 8 to 20 out (SHX 5.83) 413 to
432 of 17 612 (r8 153 to 160). The pictures differing of the other sets with an AutoCAD picture: e8 455 to 444, e11 57 to 53, te8 320 to 308, te11 108 to 104, taq 66 to 64, p2 17 to 6, aq 78 to 81; a3g (no
AutoCAD picture) changed in its near-threshold leaders; the other 103 sets of the harness are byte for byte what they were. Not fitted: the rings of DIMTXT 4 (words 4 high with arrowheads of 2.5) which no table of this form follows (a fit without them
leaves them at 1 128 where the old table had 1 050), and the jump of the band at the height of an arc's middle, whose 11 of 558 pictures (SHX; Arial 2) stay: a narrowing in the rise to that height
by a profile of nodes, by a power, by the distance in landings and by landing-scaled units each moved them by trading against aq and taq, and no rule was found.
**CHANGED.** The ACAD_TABLE of a table is written from its own bytes by `InsertRows`, `InsertRowsAndInherit`, `InsertColumns`, `InsertColumnsAndInherit`, `DeleteRows`,
`DeleteColumns`, `SetRowHeight` and `SetColumnWidth`, where each wrote and then read again all of its 56 000 groups (931 cells) when the library had written the record
whole before: each cell that comes out as it was is copied as it stands, the head and the cells made or changed are written, and the places of the cells are kept for the next
edit. The layout the table reads takes the cells written one by one since into it (`Own`), so that an edit that still writes the record whole does not read its groups again
after a text is set; a height or a width set left the table to read the record anew at its next edit, which a merge, a text set or a row put in paid for with 3 to 7 ms. The
search a merge makes in the file for what else points at a field the merge lets go of (`DxfField.Erase`) reads each record's groups one at a time, none kept, and passes over a
record whose bytes hold the digits of none of the handles looked for, in either case or with zeros before them; a handle of digits alone is searched for in every record, as before.
In a table of 49 rows by 19 columns (931 cells) read from a file, medians of 20 edits on .NET Framework 4.8 (.NET 10 in brackets): a row put in takes 2.0 ms (1.35) where it
took 3.5 ms (2.3), a row put in taking the look of another 2.3 ms (1.4) where 3.7 (2.3), a row taken out 1.9 ms (1.0) where 3.4 (2.2), a column put in 2.3 ms (1.3) where 3.8 (2.5), a
column taken out 1.65 ms (1.0) where 3.25 (2.0), `SetRowHeight` 0.28 ms (0.19) where 1.4 (0.9) and `SetColumnWidth` 0.33 ms (0.25) where 1.4 (0.8); after a height or a width set, a
merge takes 0.6 ms (0.8) where 5.7 (3.8), a text set 0.01 ms where 2.5 (1.5), a row put in 1.4 ms (1.6) where 6.7 (4.5); a merge across a cell holding a field 0.9 ms (0.5) where 3.0 (1.8)
when the handles of its fields hold a letter, and what it took (2.9 ms) where one is of digits alone. Ten rounds of a height set, a merge, a width set, a row
put in, a text set and the row taken out allocate 151 MB where they allocated 341, 20 rows put in and 20 taken out 199 MB where 293, and 20 merges across a field 49 MB where 175. The saved bytes
are the same: the hashes of 64 runs of 120 edits with heights and widths set among rows and columns put in and taken out, merges across a field, resets and text set (`DxfSpeed21Tests`), and of
480 further runs of 150 edits on tables of 6 to 35 rows and 4 to 15 columns, are those of the library before, as is what a field a record points at in any case does to a merge.
**NEW.** `DwgWriter` writes a 3DSOLID, a REGION and a BODY into a DWG of R2000, which left them out. The entity holds the SAT text of ACIS 4.00
itself, as AutoCAD 2000's file keeps it: the flag of not empty, a bit AutoCAD 2000 sets to 1 where later versions leave it at 0, the version
1, the text in blocks of at most 4 096 bytes each with its size ahead of it and a 0 after the last, and the wireframe of a new solid (no
count of materials, no history handle). The lines are the groups of the DXF with a caret held alone and a line that starts with a space
starting with a tab, each ended by a carriage return and a line feed. AutoCAD's own DWG of R2000 of a box 30 by 20 by 10, a region and two
spline solids (the second of 9 836 bytes of text in blocks of 4 096, 4 096 and 1 644) are read and written again to the very bytes of each
entity (4 of 4). The solids of the box, sphere, cylinder and region of the DXF of R2004, R2010, R2013 and R2018, of a box with a region,
and of a plate 400 by 400 with 400 holes, written to R2000, open in AutoCAD 2021 with `AUDIT` at 0 errors and `MASSPROP` gives them what it
gives the original and its own SaveAs to R2000 (9 087.1384 for the three solids, area 153.9380 and perimeter 43.9823 for the region; 6 000
and 314.1593; 1 398 938.0702). A solid whose ACIS cannot be put as 4.00 (the 2 spline solids of the DXF of R2004, R2007 and R2010) is left
out of R2000 as before. Of 1 080 files (the 167 drawings of the corpus and 13 saved by AutoCAD as R2018, each written as the six versions)
1 056 are the same bytes as before; the 24 others are the 8 of R2000 that hold bodies and the 16 of R2007 and R2010 of the next entry.

**FIXED.** The constraint groups of a dynamic block of the second layout (ACDBASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP of a drawing AutoCAD 2018 saved) were left
out of a DWG of R2010 and R2007, with the network that listed them, the evaluation graph and the dependencies of the block. They are
written in the first layout, as AutoCAD 2021 does when it saves such a drawing in those versions: the action at version 1 without its four
numbers more, the two numbers and the flag after the next identifier left out, and the nodes by identifier, each with its class as a text,
its identifier, its byte and what its class holds (a circle and an arc with three reals, where the second layout has a fourth, 0 in every
sample). The 34 groups of the 8 `Dynamic Blocks` samples that hold some, saved by AutoCAD as R2018 and written as R2010 and R2007, open with
`AUDIT` at the errors of AutoCAD's own R2010 file of each (0, 2 in each Civil, 10 in Mechanical - Metric), AutoCAD's DXF of the files holds
every group of the R2018 file group for group, and the data of each group equals the data of the group in AutoCAD's own DWG of R2010, bit for
bit (the handles of the actions a group owns come in AutoCAD's own order there). A test that expected the groups to be left out changed.

**CHANGED.** The edits of a table that go into its TABLECONTENT are written into the bytes of the cells and rows they change, as `MergeCells` is, where each read
and wrote its 100 000 groups (a table read from a file holds one, from R2007 on): `ResetValue` of a block cell, which takes the block's content out of it,
`InsertRows`, `InsertRowsAndInherit`, `InsertColumns`, `InsertColumnsAndInherit`, `DeleteRows`, `DeleteColumns`, `SetSize`, and a `MergeCells` that empties a cell holding
a field (the fields it lets go of are taken out of the list after the rows and erased, as the whole writing did). The TABLECONTENT is read once and kept, each of its rows
and cells with where it stands in the record's bytes; an edit copies the rows it does not touch as they stand, writes the cells and rows it makes or changes, and puts the
list of merged ranges and the rest after the rows in their places. The layout of the ACAD_TABLE is kept after rows or columns are put in or taken out (it was read again
from the bytes just written), which spares the next edit of the table the reading of its 56 000 groups. In a table of 49 rows by 19 columns (931 cells) read from a file,
on .NET Framework 4.8 (.NET 10 in brackets): a reset of each of its 456 block cells takes 0.1 to 0.3 s and 0.5 GB (0.13 s) where it took 12.1 s and 12.7 GB (7.0 s);
twenty rows put in take 2.4 ms each (3.3 ms) where they took 25.7 ms (15.2 ms), twenty taken out 3.3 ms (3.7 ms) where they took 29.7 ms (18.1 ms), twenty put in
that take the look of another 4.4 ms (4.8 ms) where they took 39.5 ms (23.8 ms), eight columns put in 4.0 ms (5.7 ms) where they took 40.4 ms (17.4 ms) and eight taken out
4.0 ms (3.6 ms) where they took 36.2 ms (17.8 ms); a merge across a cell whose field the ACAD_TABLE holds, 3.0 ms (2.8 ms) where it took 4.9 ms (3.4 ms), the fields it lets go of looked
for among the bytes of the cells and not in a layout read anew. The same rows and columns put in and taken out of the table a program built (no TABLECONTENT) take 2.5 to
4.1 ms each (2.4 to 5.1 ms) where they took 5.5 to 11.3 ms (4.1 to 9.6 ms). `MergeCells`, `UnmergeCells`, `SetFormula`, `SetTextString` and `ResetValue` of a text cell take
what they took, within the noise of a machine that other work shares, but for the unmerges of a file with its TABLECONTENT, which cost the copy of its rows now and take 0.075 s for 192 where they took 0.062 s (192 merges of two cells in a file take 0.13 s, as before). The saved bytes are the same: the hashes
of 64 runs of 120 edits (rows and columns put in and taken out, with and without taking the look of another, merges, merges across a field, resets of a block cell, the setters
of a cell; text cells and block cells, with and without a TABLECONTENT, four versions, four seeds) and of 32 runs of 60 edits of the table AutoCAD 2021 wrote linked to data,
with and without a field in its linked cell, equal those of the library before; and the text of runs of the same edits made in place equals that of the same runs
made on a record read anew before each edit (16 sets, 40 to 60 edits). A TABLECONTENT whose groups do not stand as the file writes them (a comment among them, found once, or
one after the last group) is read and written whole, as before.
**CHANGED.** The cold display of a drawing of 1 000 000 entities makes 452 MB of objects where it made 533 and takes 0.86 s where it took 1.04 (best
of 15 runs alternated with the older build in three passes, .NET 8; median 0.88 s where 1.09), and a REGEN of it takes 0.39 s where 0.45 and makes 276 MB where 306.
Under .NET 10 the cold display takes 0.75 s where 0.90 (452 MB where 516) and a REGEN 0.36 s where 0.41; under .NET Framework 4.8 the cold display takes
2.48 s where 2.65 (460 MB where 541) and a REGEN 1.08 s where 1.24. What changed, each measured alone first:
- A closed polyline with a bulge, which is read as a loop of arcs in space (`GeoPolygonArc3`), is built with 360 bytes where it took 448, and its `Area` makes no
  garbage where it made 176. The vertices are walked by place where they stand in a list or an array (a walk of them as a sequence made an enumerator),
  `GeoPlane3.ContainsAll` tests the points of an array or a list the same way, and the area is measured in two arrays of the thread's own, 64 edges and
  fewer, where a polygon of the plane and two arrays were made for each call; a loop of more edges, or one that has two corners on one point once laid out
  (as a point tolerance finer than the planar one allows), is laid out whole as before. A cold display of 200 000 polylines of four vertices with
  a bulge takes 0.26 s where it took 0.34 and makes 169 MB where 219 (.NET 8).
- The layer of an entity is found among the eight the builder drew last, by the string its record gave for it, which the entities of one look share. Three
  tables were asked for its name before (the shared spelling, the layer, its bit in the list) and the last hit of each missed whenever layers took
  turns: 200 000 lines on three layers in turn are redrawn in 18 ms where they took 25 (on one layer 17 ms where 20), and the cold display of
  1 000 000 entities is 80 to 100 ms quicker (.NET 8).
- A LINE, an ARC, a CIRCLE and a LWPOLYLINE go to their shapes at once, where the cases of `Draw` tested each against seventeen classes, four of them
  unsealed: 10 ns an entity, 2 ms of the 20 of a REGEN of 200 000 lines, and within the noise at 1 000 000 entities.
- The words of a TEXT are cleaned and trimmed with no builder, no buffer and no array for each `Trim`: they are made again only where they hold a carriage
  return or the code of a degree, a plus-minus or a diameter sign. 200 000 texts are displayed with 65 MB of garbage where 95 (150 bytes a text) and redrawn
  with 50 MB where 80, in 0.10 s where 0.11 and 0.085 s where 0.10 (.NET 8).

The display lists, their boxes, runs and insertion points, the bytes a drawing saves and the pixels are the same: 167 AutoCAD samples and three generated
drawings (60 000 entities on twelve layers, one off, with INSERTs of blocks on layer 0 and texts with codes; 100 000 and 1 000 000 mixed entities) give
the same list item for item and field for field (cold, after a REGEN, the layouts, three layers off and on) under .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8 (the
1 000 000 under .NET 8), the same bytes saved and the same pixels in two views, plain and selected, and 540 000 loops of arcs built three ways (a list,
an array and a sequence) have every vertex, bulge, normal, area and the words of every exception the same to the bit. Not kept: a one-pass read of the code
line of each group in the walk of a record, for the REGEN of the texts (it takes 87 ms for 200 000 texts with it and without, the read of their groups being 28 per cent of
it): the walk is not made again but by keeping the places of the groups of each text, 144 bytes of each. `DxfSpeed20Tests` (11) and `DisplaySpeed20Tests` (11).

**CHANGED.** `MergeCells` and `UnmergeCells` are written into the bytes of the cells they change and into those of the table's TABLECONTENT, as the setters
of one cell are, where each call read every cell, rebuilt the whole record and read and wrote every group of the TABLECONTENT (a table read from a file
holds one, from R2007 on). The blocks of merged cells are kept from one call to the next, for as long as every cell is as a whole writing leaves it (its
merging by the blocks, its link by the links of the table; a table that has a cell otherwise is written whole once, which sets it right, and the next
merge is in place), and are read again once a cell is edited in its kind, merging or link. A merge reads and writes the cells of the range and those
along its edges, a handful of cells; the TABLECONTENT is read once, the bytes of the cells a merge empties and of its list of merged ranges then
put in their places and the rest of the record copied. 192 merges of two cells in a table of 49 rows by 19 columns (931 cells), on .NET Framework 4.8 (.NET 10 in
brackets): 68 ms and 53 MB (57 ms) where they took 1.57 s and 1.8 GB (1.15 s); their 192 unmerges 62 ms and 29 MB (44 ms) where they took 1.57 s and
1.8 GB (1.17 s); on the table of a file with its TABLECONTENT, 94 ms and 235 MB (86 ms), 130 MB of them the one reading of the TABLECONTENT, where they took
5.7 s and 6.8 GB (4.2 s), and 55 ms and 196 MB (42 ms) for the unmerges where they took 6.0 s and 7.0 GB (4.3 s). The saved bytes are the same: the hashes of 48
runs of 120 edits (text cells, text cells of a file with its TABLECONTENT, block cells; four versions, four seeds; merges and unmerges
among the setters of a cell, formulas, rows and columns put in and taken out) equal those of the library before, and so do 570 runs of 150 to 160 edits
of the same kind made by a probe on tables of 7 by 5 to 20 by 7 cells (merges and unmerges in the greater part, with and without a TABLECONTENT), and the text
of runs made in place equals that of the same runs made on a record read anew before each edit, which reads it whole (about 400 runs in 8 sets). A TABLECONTENT whose groups do not
stand as the file writes them (a comment among them, found once, for the table) is written whole as before. The first call on a table whose record the library did not write whole yet writes it whole, and leaves it so that
the next is in place.
**FIXED.** The presenter measured every text after one failed read of a font file by the estimate it falls back on, for as long as the process lived: `CadTextInk` (the ink of
a face) and `CadFontMetrics` (the metrics WMFIN takes) kept the failure of a read of a font file, a TrueType file held open by another program or read while the
disk was busy among them, as they keep a file that is no font. A read that fails with an `IOException` or a refused access is no longer kept: the next measure reads
the file again (the face's measure is made anew for the next call, not kept with the failure), while a file that is no font is still kept as none.
**FIXED.** Arc length dimensions (DIMARC) in the presenter put the arc point where AutoCAD 2021 does for words outside an arc of more than
half a circle, and lay the words next to a ray (DIMJUST 1 and 2) on a small arc by the chords AutoCAD lays them by (measured on its console;
the counts are differing pictures, before and after). Past a half turn the words stand in the half turn left over, and the arc point is two
thirds of the way round where their middle is nearer the first end than the second (the short way round about the vertex), a third where it
is nearer the second, whichever end they hang on to: the arc of 1 from 0 through 181 degrees, aligned words, put 0.31 out has it at 60.3
degrees, at 0.32 out at 120.7 (DIMJUST 1 the other way round), through 200 degrees the change comes between 0.36 and 0.37. It was two thirds
for aligned words (a third for DIMJUST 1) and a third for level ones whatever the distance. It holds in all 1 969 pictures of the probes with
the words outside, the level words whose box has a hair inside the arc (two thirds) among them. Words standing on the arc next to a ray lay the
arrowhead, the gap after it, the half of their box with its gap and the gap besides it by a chord each, not by the cube of two of them over
24 radii squared, which fell 4 degrees short round an arc of 0.3 radius: the arc of 1 from 0 through 225 degrees put 0.3 out, DIMJUST 1, words
"3.9270" 0.75 wide, stand 170.5 degrees from the second ray and are turned 324.49 degrees (the cube 166.5 and 328.47), at 0.45 out 108.0 and
27.0, as AutoCAD draws them. Sets (differing, before then after): aligned words and DIMJUST 1 and 2 past a half circle (432) 204, now 36; the
same to 0.01 in the distance (5 508) 2 691, now 228; level words, the distance finely (4 284) 208, now 199; where the words stop going outside
(1 488) 126, now 116; the direction by 5 degrees (1 296) 192, now 185; the sizes of the box and gap (456) 112, now 104; DIMJUST words on arcs
of 1, 3 and 10 (216) 4, now 1. Of the 115 sets of probes with AutoCAD's pictures 7 are nearer, none is worse, 108 have the same count, and of
the 2 668 pictures that came right none that was right came wrong (13 sets differ in their numbers by less than 0.001, from the chords). Not
changed: the arrowheads that stand out with level words outside (the lower edge: 48 of the 1 969 pictures differ, 13 of them where DIMGAP 0.18
without the arc symbol wants the edge 2.3 degrees higher while DIMGAP 0.18 with it wants none, 16 where the box is near an arrowhead and the
arrowheads stay in at a middle direction of 125 to 150 degrees), and where the words come in on arcs of 181 to 200 degrees (AutoCAD brings
them in one or two hundredths of the distance later than the room asks, by 0.015 to 0.04 of room at 181 degrees, 0.001 to 0.025 at 190 and
0.04 to 0.066 at 200, not one amount; and both arrowheads in, which want 0.04 to 0.07 less room than the fit gives with the arc symbol
and from 0.026 less to 0.04 more without it as the sweep goes from 181 to 225 degrees: the 228 left of the 5 508).

**CHANGED.** `SetValueFromText`, `SetAutoScale`, `SetBlockScale`, `SetBlockRotation`, `SetBlockAttributeValue` and `SetFormula` are written
into the place of the cell's own bytes, as `ResetValue`, `SetCellType` and the lines of a cell are, where each call read and wrote every group
of the table's record (`SetBlockScale` and `SetBlockRotation` also read the layout of the table to learn the value the cell had; they read
it from the cell now). On a table of 49 rows by 19 columns, half its cells block cells of a block with one attribute definition, on .NET
Framework 4.8 (the tests run there; .NET 10 not timed): a text typed into each of the 466 text cells takes 26 ms and 9 MB in place of 4 014 ms
and 3 688 MB, the fit of each of the 465 block cells 11 ms and 9 MB in place of 4 565 ms and 3 809 MB, their scale 4 ms and 9 MB in place
of 5 599 ms and 4 791 MB, their turn 3 ms and 9 MB in place of 6 998 ms and 4 792 MB, the value of their attribute 45 ms and 9 MB in place of
6 010 ms and 3 807 MB, and a formula in each text cell 159 ms and 86 MB in place of 8 230 ms and 6 625 MB (the field of each is written into the
drawing too). The saved bytes are the same: the hashes of 24 runs of 120 edits (four versions, six seeds, every one of these setters among them
with `MergeCells`, `UnmergeCells`, `SetValue`, `ResetValue`, `SetCellType` and the lines of a cell) equal those of the library before, and 240 random
runs of 60 edits equal the same runs made on a record read anew before each edit, which reads it whole. (Those runs leave the first row alone:
a table read anew merges across a row whose cells hold no value, as AutoCAD does on load, which a table edited in place does not do again.)
**CHANGED.** `DxfTable.Value` of a cell that holds a date or a time is the `DateTime` AutoCAD 2021's console gave (probed, en-US and a zone seven
hours ahead of Greenwich: 1/1/2020 the 1st of January 2020, 12:30 the 30th of December 1899 at 12:30, 1/1/2020 12:30 and 2/29/2020 23:59 as
typed, to the second), where it gave the words the cell shows. A date a table cannot read (16 bytes that are no date) still gives its words.
**CHANGED.** `Fill` with `GenerateSeries` goes on with dates and times as AutoCAD 2021's console went on with them (probed over 48 sources,
zone seven hours ahead of Greenwich), where it copied them: each is counted in seconds as the C library's `mktime` counts them, the date as
shown read in the machine's zone and taken to the epoch (1 January 1970), the series goes on from the last date by the step between the last
two (a day for one), or in reverse back from the first by the step between the first two, and each date is put back with no zone, the cell of
the format of the source it repeats. So 1/1/2020 filled into three cells has the values 1/1/2020 17:00, 1/2/2020 17:00 and 1/3/2020 17:00 (shown
1/1/2020, 1/2/2020 and 1/3/2020) in that zone and 1/2/2020, 1/3/2020 and 1/4/2020 in Greenwich; 1/1/2020, 1/2/2020 and 1/4/2020 go on by 2
days, the last step, where numbers go on by the step from first to last; 1/1/2020 and 1/2/2020 12:30 by 36 hours 30 minutes, the cells in turn of
the formats %x and %c. A date before the epoch counts as -1 (mktime fails): 12:30 alone, on the 30th of December 1899, goes on from -1 by a
day to 1/1/1970 23:59:59 in any zone, and two such times by nought to 12/31/1969 23:59:59; 1/1/1970 (-25 200 s in that zone) and 1/2/1970
go on by 61 201 s. A count of seconds before 12 hours before the epoch makes no date: the cell holds 16 bytes of nought and no words, as AutoCAD's
did (-25 200 s gave 12/31/1969 17:00 and -111 600 s none). Dates mixed with other values are copied as before, and so are dates under
`CopyContent`. The zone comes from the machine (`TimeZoneInfo.Local`) as AutoCAD's does, its daylight saving of the date shown included; a
machine in another zone gives other times of day in the same rule, which the tests work out from the machine's own zone.
**CHANGED.** The endless 1.8 % growth of a fitted block cell's column under repeated `GenerateLayout` and `RecomputeTableBlock` (said above, in
the entry on the attribute of a block cell) was probed again and not reproduced: both calls made 12 to 14 times in the console, through the .NET API, over
a fitted block cell of seven tables (three new ones, four read from a file; the column left alone, set to 40, to 20, and started from the widened
