40.69607 with the scale 1.41401 and with 1) left the column and the scale where the first pass put them, to the last digit. The presenter, which
settles after one pass, stays as it is; the guide says what was and was not seen.
**NEW.** `DwgWriter` writes AutoCAD 2007 (AC1021): `DwgWriter.Write(database, path, "AC1021")`. The file is the container AutoCAD 2007 has and the
later versions do not: a file header, a header proper of 0x400 bytes and pages, all coded by Reed-Solomon, with CRCs of 64 bits and a
compression of their own. The two codes were found by taking the blocks of AutoCAD 2021's own files of R2007 and testing which field and
which roots make them codewords (the header and the maps: 255 bytes of which 239 are data, the field of `x^8 + x^6 + x^5 + x^3 + 1` and
the roots 2^239 to 2^254; the data pages: 251 of 255, `x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1`, 2^251 to 2^254), and the 2 746 headers, maps and data
pages of 171 of its files are coded again to the byte. The compression is the variant of LZ77 that the reader already knew
(`DwgLz21`), now also written: by a search of the longest copy of 3 bytes or more from up to 65 535 bytes back, read back before it is
used, a page that does not get shorter stored as it is. A drawing of a later version is made into the DXF of R2007 first, as for R2004.
The presenter's Save As lists "AutoCAD 2007/LT2007 Drawing (*.dwg)" between 2010 and 2004 (`CadExportJob.DwgSaveTypes`), `SAVEAS` with
FILEDIA 0 takes `2007`, `LT2007` and `2007(LT2007)` (only R14 is refused now: "... is not written: a DWG is saved as AutoCAD 2018, 2013,
2010, 2007, 2004 or 2000 (2018, 2013, 2010, 2007, 2004, 2000)."), and Save (QSAVE) writes the DWG of the version last chosen again.
AutoCAD 2021 refused the first files with `ErrorStatus` 434 before it read a page. Putting its own pages into the writer's container, one
section and one change at a time, found what it wants that the format does not say: the header proper only with its data compressed (the
stored form is refused), the section map only compressed, the size a page names in the section map equal to the size of its data, and,
of the pages it keeps unpacked (the application information, its history and the summary information), parity made from the bytes its own
memory held, which no other program can write; the application information is written coded 4 (compressed, in blocks of the code of 251, as
the header is), which AutoCAD reads as well and opens with `AUDIT` at 0 errors, the history and the summary information are left out, and
the preview is written only where the drawing has a picture. The
free-space section is the 53 bytes AutoCAD writes into R2007 and the auxiliary header names the version of the file (27, 50) between two of
the application, and the classes carry the release it gives them there (33 and 174, the table cell styles 27 and 1), as its own files do. The 167 drawings of AutoCAD 2021's samples and of the tests, each written as AC1021 and opened in
AutoCAD 2021 with `AUDIT`: all 167 open, 160 at 0 errors, the other 7 with the errors of their originals (24, 24, 2, 2, 32, 32, 10 = 126
of the 150 the originals have in all), and the 4 table drawings that had 6 each have none; none refused, none beyond 4 GB or 120 s. They
come to 19.2 MB (the bodies, the dynamic blocks and the application information are in), where AutoCAD's own SaveAs of the same drawings to R2007 come to 19.7 MB. The same 167 written as R2000, R2004, R2010,
R2013 and R2018 are the same bytes as before (835 of 835 compared). The 3DSOLID, REGION and BODY and the constraint groups of a dynamic
block are written into R2007 as the next two entries say. Left: the preview of a drawing with a picture holds parity the writer makes from
zeros, which AutoCAD 2021's console does not check, and its application window was not tried.

**CHANGED.** The cold display of a drawing of 1 000 000 entities makes 532 MB of objects where it made 837 and is collected 31 times where 47,
and takes 1.52 s where 1.82 (best of 15 runs alternated with the older build in three passes, .NET 8; median 1.74 s where 2.15); under .NET
Framework 4.8 540 MB where 860, 82 collections of the youngest generation where 123, 2.80 s where 3.10, and under .NET 10 1.52 s where 2.43. A REGEN takes 0.58 s where 0.80
(1.27 s where 1.37 under .NET Framework 4.8), a layer switched off 22 ms where 35 (42 where 63), a layer switched on 314 ms where 342, and
a MOVE of one line 16 ms as before. An entity of one shape keeps the shape itself where it kept a list of it (24 bytes of each of 780 000
entities, and an enumerator of 48 for every walk of it): `Shapes` gives the list as before, made when asked for and kept, and the drawing
takes the shape bare. The width of a LWPOLYLINE and the groups of a TEXT are found in the walk of the record that finds its look, by the same
code, where each was a walk of its own over the same bytes; a polyline found to have no width is marked so, and a REGEN no longer walks each
of 200 000 polylines to be told it again (a tenth of a REGEN). The box of a text is found with no array made, the lists a polyline of four
vertices is read and drawn through are a thread's and a builder's own, emptied for each, and the room the runs, items and insertion points
of a list need is made once after the first 4 096 entities where it was made over by doubling twenty times. A layer switched off is patched in
pieces on up to eight threads where more than 131 072 runs are taken, the insertion points of the runs dropped taken out by another at the
same time; those points were 12.5 of its 33 ms once the rest was in pieces, where they had been 2.5 of 36. Not
kept: the shapes of a LWPOLYLINE, whose drop takes 68 MB off the heap (526 MB where 594) and a REGEN 0.84 s where 0.60. The display lists, their
boxes, runs and insertion points, the bytes saved and the pixels are the same: 167 AutoCAD samples (cold, after a MOVE, an ERASE, three layers
off and on, a REGEN and the layouts) item for item under both runtimes, the saved bytes but for the one sample with an ACIS body, and the
pixels in two views, plain, selected and hovered; drawings of 200 000 and 1 000 000 entities the same way. `DxfSpeed19Tests` (13) and `DisplaySpeed16Tests` (7).

**NEW.** `DwgWriter` writes a 3DSOLID, a REGION and a BODY into a DWG of R2004, R2007 and R2010, which left them out (only R2013 and later wrote
them). The entity holds its ACIS data itself in those versions, as SAB: the flag that says it is not empty and another of 0, the version 2,
the bytes, the wireframe of a new solid, from R2007 the count of materials 0 and, of a solid, the handle of its history, and the file has no
data store. The SAB is that of the version (head 20800, 21200 or 21500, ending in `End-of-ACIS-data`), made of the SAT the DXF of the version
gives, which the entity keeps as it is. A box 30 by 20 by 10, a sphere, a cylinder and a region as AutoCAD 2021's own DWG of R2004, R2007 and
R2010 hold them are encoded again to the bit, entity by entity, but for the date of the SAB (24 bytes in AutoCAD's, empty in the writer's, as
in R2018). The 167 drawings of AutoCAD's samples and of the tests, written to R2004, R2007 and R2010: the 11 that hold bodies (5 of the acis
drawings, 2 of solids and 4 of splines) come out with them, but for the solids whose spline records the grammars do not place (the 2 of
the ACIS 4.00 splines of R2000, and one of two in some others), and the 33 files open with `AUDIT` at 0 errors, and `MASSPROP` gives the three solids of the box, sphere and cylinder the volume 9 087.1384 and the region the area 153.9380 and
perimeter 43.9823 in R2004, R2007, R2010 and R2013, as of the original; the spline solids have the volumes of their originals (1 654.1254
and 1 654.1366). The 157 other drawings written to R2004 and to R2010 and all 501 files of R2000, R2013 and R2018 are the same bytes as before. Two faults of the
SAT turned into SAB came to light and are fixed: the end of the data of R2004 to R2010 names ACIS, not ASM, and the parametric curve of a
lofted solid of R2007 ends with the flag of its surface alone, where R2010 and later hold a flag more (the flag is put in or taken out as the
form crosses R2007 and R2010, and written alone AutoCAD 2021 refused such a solid with a modeling error, 75004).

**FIXED.** A drawing with a dynamic block saved as R2007 from a later version keeps its constraint groups (ACDBASSOC2DCONSTRAINTGROUP with the
network, the variables and the dependencies that go with them, and the evaluation graph of the block), which it lost because R2007 has no
place for the vertex identifiers of a polyline nor for the mark of a dimension of a constraint, and AUDIT found 34 errors in each
Architectural drawing of the samples, 22 more than the original in each Civil and 24 in each Structural where the groups were kept without
them. The 8 dynamic-block drawings of the samples lost their groups, the 2 Mechanical ones, which hold no polyline with ids, their whole block as
well (60 and 20 dependencies, 56 and 12 dimensions of constraints, the evaluation graph). `DxfVersionConverter` gives the DXF of R2007 the two records AutoCAD 2021 keeps for what R2007 has no place for, in
the extension dictionary of the entity under `ACAD_XREC_ROUNDTRIP`: `VERTEXIDENTIFIER` on each LWPOLYLINE whose vertices have ids (the count
of the whole numbers that follow, itself one, then the ids as bytes, in groups of 127) and `ISDYNAMIC` with a 1 on each dimension of the
constraints (the layer `*ADSK_CONSTRAINTS` with an association among its reactors), which is also made invisible and loses its text, as
AutoCAD does; the writer keeps the groups where the drawing holds either. The 8 polylines and 25 dimensions of Architectural - Metric come
out each equal to AutoCAD's own R2007 file (33 records of 33), and the 8 drawings written as R2007 keep their groups and open with `AUDIT`
finding the errors of their originals (2 in each Civil, 10 in Mechanical - Metric, none in the others). The DXF saved as R2007 holds the
records too.

**NEW.** `DwgWriter` writes AutoCAD 2000 (AC1015): `DwgWriter.Write(database, path, "AC1015")`. The file is the one AutoCAD 2000 has and not the pages of
the later versions: a header of 0x61 bytes with six locators, the auxiliary header, the preview, the header variables, the classes, the objects, the
object map with the places of the objects as places in the file, and the template, with the maintenance release 15 and no free-space section. A
drawing of a later version is made into the DXF of R2000 first, as the later versions are, so that what R2000 cannot hold is left out or replaced as
`DxfDatabase.Save(path, "AC1015")` does. The presenter's Save As lists "AutoCAD 2000/LT2000 Drawing (*.dwg)" after the 2004 type
(`CadExportJob.DwgSaveTypes`), `SAVEAS` with FILEDIA 0 takes 2000 (`2000`, `LT2000`, `2000(LT2000)`; R14 is refused, "... is not written: a
DWG is saved as AutoCAD 2018, 2013, 2010, 2007, 2004 or 2000 (2018, 2013, 2010, 2007, 2004, 2000)."), and Save (QSAVE) writes the DWG of the version last chosen again.
Its objects are laid out as AutoCAD 2000's own, found by writing the DXF the reader makes of AutoCAD's files of R2000 and comparing object by object with
AutoCAD's bytes: an entity holds the links to the entity before and after it in its owner's list (left out where they are the handles one before and one
after), the vertices of a polyline are linked to each other and its SEQEND to none, a table record holds the bit that says it is referenced, a dimension style
the bit after its lineweights, a layout the handles of its base and named UCS, and an MTEXT the bit after its line spacing factor. The table records,
dimension styles, layouts, vertices, SEQEND, lines, circles, ellipses and splines of the test drawings come out as AutoCAD's own bytes. The 167 drawings of
AutoCAD 2021's samples and of the tests, each written as AC1015 and opened in AutoCAD 2021 with `AUDIT`: all 167 open, 160 at 0 errors, the other 7
with the errors of their originals (126 of the 150 the originals have in all), and the 4 tables that had 6 each have none. Left: a text beyond the code
page is written as its UTF-8 bytes in R2000 as it is in R2004, where AutoCAD keeps `\U+1EBF`.
**FIXED.** REVCLOUD in the presenter draws the shapes shorter than its arcs as AutoCAD 2021's console does (run through standard
input, 15 November). A path shorter than the longest arc is a cloud of two vertices, its start and the point halfway along it,
bulging the positive way: a line 15 long at arcs of 20 is (0, 0) and (7.5, 0), a rectangle 10 by 10 (0, 0) and (10, 10), a circle of
radius 3 (3, 0) and (-3, 0); a line 20 long still (0, 0) and (20, 0). Two vertices were refused as too small, and Object, which asks
for another object after `Unable to convert object, object is too small for the cloud's arcs.`, ended there. Rectangular draws a
cloud of two to five vertices and says `Invalid shape to create revision cloud.` all the same (25 by 25 at arcs of 20: five
vertices and the message; 5 by 5, one vertex: the message and no cloud), and Polygonal draws nothing below six vertices (the square
of 25 none, of 28 six), where the presenter drew from three. The first cloud drawn while REVCLOUDAPPROXARCLEN is nought sets it to
the length it was drawn with, so that the next clouds keep it whatever the view shows. Modify erases the cloud picked and makes a
new one, of a new handle, on the same layer and with the same `RevcloudProps`, as AutoCAD does; it changed the cloud in place. At
REVCLOUDARCVARIANCE 1 AutoCAD's arcs vary at random from cloud to cloud (each between two thirds and four thirds of the length, evenly
spread: 300 arcs of a line 6 000 long had a mean of 20.0000), where the presenter's are one fixed sequence of that kind; that
cannot be matched and is left.
**NEW.** REVCLOUDARCSTYLE, REVCLOUDGRIPS, REVCLOUDMINARCLENGTH and REVCLOUDMAXARCLENGTH in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's:
REVCLOUDARCSTYLE a text, "Normal" or "Calligraphy" as the Style option sets it, which SETVAR takes whatever it says (only exactly
"Calligraphy" draws calligraphy); REVCLOUDGRIPS a switch, ON to begin with; REVCLOUDMINARCLENGTH and REVCLOUDMAXARCLENGTH 0.5 to
begin with and written by Arc length and by REVCLOUDPROPERTIES (30 gives 20 and 40, or 30 and 30 with REVCLOUDARCVARIANCE 0; 12 gives
8 and 16), and by nothing else.
**FIXED.** `-VPORTS ?` and Delete in the presenter treat `*Multiple`, the configuration Toggle writes and writes over, as AutoCAD 2021's
console does: ? lists it in the order of the names, ahead of the named ones, and says `No matching viewport configurations found.`
where none matches; `Delete` with `*` deletes it with the rest (`Deleted 3 viewport configurations.`); Restore of `*Multiple` or
`*Active` ends with nothing said and nothing changed; Save refuses a name that begins with an asterisk with `Invalid viewport
configuration name.` and asks again. Three tiles toggled, split into two and toggled again leave the two as `*Multiple`, as in
AutoCAD. `CadTiledViewports.Delete` and `CadTiledViewports.List` now take `*Multiple` in; `CadTiledViewports.Names` still leaves it out.
**CHANGED.** The count of vertices PEDIT makes of a spline within a precision was probed again, on 14 splines at 17 precisions (238
counts, 186 right, 52 with 1 to 22 vertices more, one with one fewer): the fault is not that of fit points. AutoCAD gives the same
counts for a spline of control points of the same knots and points, and PEDIT's equal `ToPolylineWithPrecision`'s in all 238. Its
halving tolerance is c over (precision + 1) squared (the pieces halved and kept are separated to 0.03 per cent by one c for each
spline), c one over the largest second derivative M where that stands at an end of the spline and 0.06 to 3.9 per cent above it
where it stands at a knot inside; what AutoCAD takes M at there is not found (no grid of the parameter or the length, no second
difference of the polyline, no point a fixed distance from the knot fitted all of 26 cases), so the library's counts stay.

**FIXED.** A drawing saved as a DXF of R2000, R2004 or R2007 (`DxfDatabase.Save(path, version)`) lacked three things AutoCAD 2021 writes
there, which the DWG writer had learned first. The 3 multileaders and the 2 multileader styles of a sample drawing of AutoCAD's, saved from
R2018, carried no extended data, where AutoCAD's own DXF of the drawing in each of the three versions has `ACAD_MLEADERVER` (version 2) on
each of the 5 and the application at the end of its table of applications (a count of 3); they hold it now, the application with the handle
after the highest the drawing has (AutoCAD's own number is whatever its session had reached), the seed moved past it where it lagged
behind. A drawing that holds the data already is not given it twice, one with no table of applications is left as it is, and R2010 and
later have none. The vertex ids of a polyline (group 91
of an LWPOLYLINE, which AutoCAD writes where the constraints of a dynamic block name its edges) are of R2010 and later: the 3 dynamic-block
samples with ids (8, 12 and 8 polylines, 36, 32 and 32 ids) saved as R2004 or R2007 had them all (AutoCAD's DXF has none), and have none now,
with R2010 and R2013 keeping every one. A letter beyond the code page of a drawing of R2004 or before (`\U+1EDB`, and `\M+182A0` of a
multibyte page) stays an escape in R2000 and R2004, where AutoCAD writes it so, and is the letter when the drawing is saved as R2007 or
later, as AutoCAD writes it: the layer `L\U+1EDBp \U+1EA9n` is `Lớp ẩn` in R2007, R2010 and R2018 (AutoCAD's own DXF of the drawing has none
of the 2 escapes the file had), where an escape typed in a text of R2007 or later is the text and stays. The saved bytes of a drawing of R2000
or R2004 that holds such a letter, saved as R2007 or later, change for it alone: in the 90 drawings of `DxfSpeed11Tests` and `DxfSpeed12Tests`
12 saves to R2013 changed, each by the one text `café \U+0110 A\PB` that is `café Đ A\PB` now, the 78 others equal to the bit.
**CHANGED.** The DWG writer saves a drawing of a later version through the same converter and no longer does the first and third of those by
itself (the extended data of a multileader and the letters in place of the escapes, which it put in after the converter or before the
DWG's file was laid out): the 167 drawings of AutoCAD's samples and of the tests, each read from its DWG and written again as R2004, R2010
and R2013, are the same 501 files to the bit as before.
**FIXED.** The extension dictionary `CreateExtensionDictionary()` makes named its object as a reactor (`{ACAD_REACTORS`) as well as its owner. AutoCAD 2021 names the owner alone (330), and puts the object's group `{ACAD_XDICTIONARY` straight after its handle, before its reactors where it has some: probed in its console on 28 objects given a dictionary by the API (a LINE, CIRCLE, TEXT, MTEXT, INSERT, HATCH, polyline, dimension, layer, block, the paper space block, a text style, dimension style, linetype, view, UCS and registered application, their tables and the viewport table, a dictionary and an XRECORD of the named object dictionary) and the 10 dictionaries the drawing had (layer 0, the layer table, model space, a layout, three materials, a table style, a detail view style and a section view style), written by DxfOut: not one of the 38 carries a reactor, and the circle that is the boundary of an associative hatch, an XRECORD and a dictionary, each with a reactor of its own, have `{ACAD_XDICTIONARY` before `{ACAD_REACTORS`. The dictionary is made as `DxfTable` already made one for a table. The 25 callers (layers, blocks, tables, views, fields, dynamic blocks, dimension breaks and the rest) read the dictionary through the object's `ExtensionDictionary` and none read its reactor; the Dxf suite (4 327 tests) and the Viewer suite stay green, the one test of the old form (`DxfDBObjectTests`) changed, and `DxfExtensionDictionaryFormTests` (3, red before) checks a LINE, a layer, a block, two tables and a dictionary of the drawing.
**FIXED.** COPY, MIRROR, ROTATE and SCALE with Copy, ARRAY and the other copies of the presenter dropped the data a plain entity keeps in its extension dictionary; AutoCAD 2021 copies it with its entries (a LINE and a CIRCLE copied and mirrored in its console, written by DxfOut). The copy now gets a dictionary of its own, owned by it, holding a new XRECORD for each XRECORD of the original's and a new dictionary for each dictionary of XRECORDs (to any depth), under the same names and in the same order, each owned by the dictionary above it, with the reactor AutoCAD gives it; a LINE with the entries GH_PLAIN (an XRECORD), GH_POINTERS and GH_SUB (a dictionary of two XRECORDs) is copied with all three, and an entity with an empty dictionary with an empty one, as AutoCAD does. What a copied XRECORD points at (330, 340, 350 and 360 among its data) among the objects copied, the entity itself and the other entries of its dictionary, it points at the copies of, as AutoCAD's map of ids has it: GH_POINTERS naming the line names the copy, and one naming another entry names that entry's copy; a pointer at any other object stays (soft and hard pointers at an object outside stayed as they were in AutoCAD, 330 and 340). Entries of another kind (the contexts of an annotative object, a clip, a dynamic block's representation, fields) are left to the code that copies those. The object a 350 or a 360 names outside the copied set is cloned too (see the entry on ownership pointers below). `CopyKeepsExtensionDictionaryTests` (5, 4 red before; the fifth, an entity with no dictionary, stays with none).
**FIXED.** The copy of an annotative HATCH made by COPY, MIRROR, ROTATE or SCALE lacked the view context AutoCAD 2021 writes (probed in its console on hatches of ANSI31, HONEY, SOLID, AR-B816 and ANSI37, one scale and two, at angles 0 and 30 and scale 1 and 2): the dictionary ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALE_VIEW_COLLECTION of AcDbContextDataManager, before ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALES, with one ACDB_HATCHVIEWCONTEXTDATA_CLASS under the name of the default context (`*A1`), a second scale of the hatch having none. It is the default context as the original held it, the origin of each of its pattern lines (43, 44) and the direction of the pattern (10, 20, 30) nought, and then AcDbHatchViewContextData (330 of 0, the normal 0, 0, 1, 51 and 290 of 0); the class is listed in CLASSES. A hatch of 1:1 copied 100 along x has 43 of 100 in its own context and 0 in the view's, and a copy of a copy has the same. The files of the library, opened in AutoCAD 2021 with AUDIT, found 0 errors and wrote the same dictionaries back (a LINE copied and mirrored with three entries and an empty one, a hatch of two scales copied and mirrored). `HatchCopyViewContextTests` (3, red before). The hatch moved by MOVE itself gets the same view context, and the contexts move with the copy (see the entries on the contexts of a moved hatch below).
**CHANGED.** The tolerance that reads a multileader mirrored across a line at 45 degrees as not turned back (`DxfMLeader.FinishMirror`, 1E-9 on the dot product of the old and mirrored x axes) stays: it was written for a dot product a hair below nought, which a mirror at 45 degrees now has at nought exactly when the line is picked at whole numbers (the matrix of `GeoTransform3.Mirror` is exact there), but a line picked at (1.1, 2.2) and (3.3, 4.4), or (12.5, -3.7) and (40.2, 24), is 45 degrees within a last digit and meets the old axis at -2.2E-16 or 1.1E-16, and without the tolerance the first is read as turned back (the plane's x axis written as -1 where AutoCAD writes 1). Pinned by `MLeaderMirror45Tests`; the comment says so. No behaviour changes.
**FIXED.** An annotative HATCH moved, turned, scaled or copied (MOVE, ROTATE, SCALE, COPY, ARRAY, `TransformBy`) kept the contexts of its scales where they were; AutoCAD 2021 carries them with it. Probed in its console on hatches of ANSI31 (angle 0, scale 1 and angle 30, scale 2), HONEY, ANSI37, AR-B816 and a user pattern, each at one scale and two, moved by (100, 50), turned 30 and 90 degrees about (0, 0) and -45 about (20, 10), scaled 2 and 0.5 about (0, 0) and 3 about (20, 10), copied 100 along x, written by DxfOut: the 84 cases of the first seven of those operations (12 hatches each) come out the same here in every context and its direction. The base point of each pattern line (43, 44) moves with the hatch (43 of 100 for a copy 100 along x, (-40, -20) for (0, 0) scaled 3 about (20, 10)), its angle (53) turns, and its offset (45, 46) and dashes (49) turn and scale as the lines of the record do: a user pattern at 30 degrees with the offset (-1, 1.732) turned 30 holds 53 of 60 and (-1.732, 1), turned 90 holds 53 of 120 and (-1.732, -1), the sign of the second flipped, scaled 2 holds (-2, 3.464); the 1:2 context's offset (-2, 3.464) turned 30 is (-3.464, 2). The direction of the pattern (10, 20) turns and is made of unit length: (0.866, 0.5) turned 30 is (0.5, 0.866). The mirror and the turn of -45 degrees, which these first probes left open, are in the entries below. `HatchContextMoveTests` (15, 14 red before).
**FIXED.** A hatch moved in place did not get the view context AutoCAD 2021 writes, and the copy of one took the base of the pattern lines of its view as nought whatever it was. AutoCAD writes ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALE_VIEW_COLLECTION on an annotative hatch each time it is transformed, by MOVE, ROTATE, SCALE, MIRROR or the API's `TransformBy`, a move by nought too (hatches of one scale and of two, ANSI31, SOLID and a user pattern): the default context as it stood before the move, its pattern lines as they were (a hatch moved by (100, 0) and then by (0, 50) holds the base (100, 0) in it, not (0, 0)) and the direction of the pattern (10, 20, 30) nought, replacing the view it had. The library does so, and the copy of a hatch that holds a view context is given a clone of it, as AutoCAD clones it: a hatch moved by (100, 0) and copied by (0, 50) has the base (0, 0), the place its original first stood at, in its copy's view. A copy of a hatch with none still gets its original's default context. A hatch that is not annotative gains no dictionary. `HatchContextMoveTests`.
**FIXED.** An ownership pointer (350, 360) among the data of a copied XRECORD, at an XRECORD or a dictionary of them outside the objects copied, kept naming the original; AutoCAD 2021's COPY clones it. Probed with a LINE whose XRECORD holds 330 at the line, 340 at a circle, 350 at an XRECORD of the named object dictionary, 360 at another and 350 at a dictionary with an entry, copied, written by DxfOut: the 350 and 360 name new objects, each owned by the copied XRECORD and in no dictionary, with the data of the original and the reactor it had; the dictionary is cloned with its entry, owned by the clone; the pointers 330 and 340 and one at an entity stay. Done the same here, two pointers at one object naming one clone (the drawings opened in AutoCAD 2021 with AUDIT: 0 errors, and it writes the clones back). Another kind of object a 350 or 360 names keeps being named. `CopyExtensionDictionaryOrderTests` (4, 3 red before).
**FIXED.** The entries of the extension dictionary of a copy, and those of the context manager inside it, stood in the order they were added; AutoCAD 2021 keeps a dictionary ordered by name, the names compared as lower-case letters. Probed on an extension dictionary of 18 names and on a dictionary below it (written by DxfOut: "10", "9", "[br", "]rb", "^caret", "_under", "a_b", "A_c", "aB", "AcDbThing", "alpha", "Beta", "GH_PLAIN", "Zeta", "ZSUB", "zz", "~tilde" in both), and on the copy of an annotative hatch holding GH_PLAIN, AA_FIRST, AcDbX and zz_last, which has AA_FIRST, AcDbContextDataManager, AcDbX, GH_PLAIN, zz_last, and in the manager ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALE_VIEW_COLLECTION before ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALES. The copies of COPY, MIRROR, ROTATE, SCALE with Copy and ARRAY, and the dictionaries below them, put each entry where its name falls; the original's order is left as it was, and so is every other dictionary (the list of scales is in the order the user gives it). `CopyExtensionDictionaryOrderTests`.
**FIXED.** A HATCH mirrored was turned over in its plane (its normal (0, 0, -1), its x axis the drawing's -x), where AutoCAD 2021 keeps the normal and reflects what lies in the plane. Probed in its console on some 540 mirrors (hatches of ANSI31, HONEY, ANSI37, AR-B816, DASH, ANGLE, a user pattern, SOLID and a gradient, with one scale and two, loops of polylines, bulges, lines and arcs, circles, ellipses, elliptical arcs and splines, mirrored across five lines, with MIRRHATCH 0 and 1, by MIRROR and by `TransformBy`), the library and the presenter now write what AutoCAD writes in every one, to 1E-9 in every number: the normal is the image of the old normal, so that a mirror across a plane that holds it leaves it (0, 0, 1) and one across the plane of the hatch turns it over (the loop at (42, 50) of a hatch at z = 0 across z = 5 is written at (-42, 50), its elevation -10); the loops and the seed points are reflected in the plane (a rectangle over (42, 50) to (58, 58) across the line through (0, 0) and (10, 10) lies over (50, 42) to (58, 58)); a bulge changes its sign (0, 0.5, 0, -0.3 across x = 0 is 0, -0.5, 0, 0.3, a bulge of nought still 0, not -0); an arc and a circle run the other way round, flag 73 turned and the angles as the file holds them moved on by the angle the mirror gives the x axis (a counter-clockwise arc of 0 to 180 across a vertical line is written clockwise, -180 to 0, and back to 0 to 180 counter-clockwise across a second; a circle across a line at 56.31 degrees is -112.62 to 247.38); an ellipse's major axis is reflected and its angles stay with the flag turned; control points and tangents of a spline are reflected. A mirror that scales unlike along the axes, which AutoCAD's commands do not make, is the plane reflected across its own x axis first, the normal kept, and what is left of the transformation after it, so that its arcs become ellipse edges as before and its area and corners are those of the transformation. `DxfHatchReflectionTests` (9, red before), `HatchMirrorCommandTests` (11 of 11, red before).
**NEW.** MIRRHATCH, the system variable of AutoCAD 2021 that says whether MIRROR mirrors the pattern of a hatch, kept by the session, 0 or 1, 0 as AutoCAD's default. MIRROR with 0 leaves the lines of the pattern as they were, in the record (base 43 and 44, angle 53, offset 45 and 46, dashes, and the pattern angle 52) and in the contexts of its scales, and reflects the direction of the pattern of each context all the same ((0.866, 0.5) across a line at 56.31 degrees is (0.1285, 0.9917)); with 1 the lines are reflected with the rest: the line at 30 degrees through (0, 0) with the offset (-1, 1.732) across the line through (20, 5) and (30, 20) is at 82.6198649480404 (twice the angle of the line less 30) with the base (23.0769, -15.3846) and the offset reflected. AutoCAD's own `TransformBy` follows MIRRHATCH too; the library's reflects the pattern, as MIRRHATCH 1 does, and the presenter's MIRROR puts the pattern back where it is 0. The view context of the copy is that of the original's place, its direction nought, as before.
**FIXED.** The direction of the pattern of a hatch's context (10, 20, 30) was carried as a direction of the hatch's plane (its z left alone); AutoCAD 2021 keeps it as a vector of the world and carries it by the transformation, so that a pattern line at 30 degrees of a hatch of normal (0, 1, 0), which holds (-0.866, 0, 0.5), turned -33 degrees about z holds (-0.7263, 0.4717, 0.5). A hatch in the plane of the drawing is as it was. What stays open: a hatch turned about an axis that is not the drawing's z by `TransformBy` (not by a command), where AutoCAD leaves the direction of an annotative hatch's context as it was in 21 of 90 cases, with no rule found (a hatch of the plane of the drawing turned 40 degrees about x, or of normal (0, 1, 0) turned about z).
**FIXED.** ROTATE took its angle as typed (-45 degrees as -45); AutoCAD 2021 takes it from nought up to a whole turn first (-45 is 315, 360 is nought, -0.0001 is 359.9999), so that a turn of 360 degrees touches nothing and the pattern of a hatch turned -45 degrees holds 53 of 360 where its line stood at 45 degrees (0 here, before): the angle of a pattern line, in the record and in the contexts, is that of the image of its direction from nought up to a whole turn, a hair below nought written 360. 378 turns of nine patterns about (0, 0) by 21 angles, with one scale and none, are the same as AutoCAD's in every group (38 differed before). The pattern angle (52) of a hatch turned -180 degrees is 180, not -180. `HatchMirrorCommandTests` (red before).
**FIXED.** The angles of a circular arc edge of a hatch, turned, were written each by its own `Atan2` (a counter-clockwise arc of 0 to 180 turned 30 degrees was 30 to -150); AutoCAD 2021 adds the angle the transformation gives the x axis to each, as the file holds it (30 to 210; a clockwise arc of 0 to 180 turned 30 is -30 to 150). 56 turns of seven kinds of boundary are the same as AutoCAD's now (11 differed).
**FIXED.** A hatch's gradient angle (460) was turned with the hatch by `TransformBy`, ROTATE and MIRROR, and a SOLID fill, which holds none, was given one; AutoCAD 2021 leaves it as it is under every turn, mirror and scale (probed on gradients at 0, 30 and 90 degrees, and on SOLID, by ROTATE, MIRROR, `TransformBy` and the scale). `TheAngleOfAGradient_IsLeftAsItIs_ByATurnAndByAMirror`, `TheAngleOfAGradient_IsLeftAsItIs_ByRotateAndByMirror`.
**FIXED.** -OBJECTSCALE Add (and `AddContext`) on an annotative hatch did not write its view context; AutoCAD 2021 writes it, as a move does, from the default context as it stands, replacing the one it has: ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALE_VIEW_COLLECTION before ACDB_ANNOTATIONSCALES, a view of the place the hatch stands at (a hatch moved by (100, 50) and given 1:2 holds 43 of 100 and 44 of 50 in its view, and the context of 1:2 200 and 100, twice that, as it did). 65 sequences of MOVE, ROTATE, SCALE, MIRROR and -OBJECTSCALE Add on five patterns are the same as AutoCAD's in every group (30 differed before). `HatchMirrorCommandTests` (red before).
**CHANGED.** A layer switched off in a drawing of 1 000 000 entities is shown in 36 ms where it took 96 (.NET 8) and in 78 ms where it took 177
(.NET Framework 4.8; best of eight, alternated with the older build, three rounds): the entities of a third of the drawing, 333 000, were each made of their
record, drawn and found to have nothing to draw. The display patch now takes the run of an entity that read the layer switched off and no
other, which draws nothing now, as an empty run of the same layer, in the one pass that copies the runs between those drawn again (the handle of
a run is not read, nor the insertion points of one that has none), and draws again only the runs that read another layer besides, those an
edit names and those that read what these drew. A bit of the layers of the runs that the layers beyond the 63rd share hides a run only where
every layer of the bit is off. The box of the list, found again from every item where more than 64 runs were dropped, is found in pieces on
several threads for a list of more than 131 072 items, the fold of boxes giving the same box in any order. The lists, their boxes, the
insertion points and the pixels are the same: 167 AutoCAD samples (cold, after a MOVE, an ERASE, a layer off and on, a REGEN and the
layouts), item for item and field for field under both runtimes, and the pixels of the samples in two views, plain, selected and
highlighted. The layer switched on, which draws a third of the entities again, the cold display and a REGEN are as they were.
**CHANGED.** The objects of a drawing of 1 000 000 entities take 17 MB less: an entity as the file was read (`DxfItem`) is 96 bytes where it was 104,
its three flags (removed, hidden, in paper space) sharing the word of its count of records, and a polyline holds one reference to what it was read by,
its vertices, its normal and its places, where its eight fields took 56 bytes of every one (200 000 of them in this drawing: 8 MB of the 17);
the heap of the displayed drawing is 610 MB where 627 (.NET 8; 618 where 635 under .NET Framework 4.8). The index of handles of a drawing read
ahead for an undo holds the record of each entity and no object made for it (a million of them, of the 520 MB a drawing read and indexed
held, some 45 MB of them): after a MOVE of one line, with the drawings of the undo and the redo read ahead, the heap is 1 235 MB where 1 357, and three moves with
their undos and redos allocate 6.1 GB where 6.5; an entity is made of its record when one is asked for by its handle, as before. Open, cold
display and REGEN are as they were (best of three alternated runs: open 473 ms where 484, cold display 2.1 s both, .NET 8). No public signature changed.
**CHANGED.** The reader makes a closed polyline of four vertices from its bytes through fewer lists: the vertices it read are kept as they are
where none lies on the one before, not copied twice, and the normals of the edges are made by a loop where a closure and a converted list were
(1 040 bytes allocated a read where 1 408 on .NET Framework 4.8; 839 MB where 915 for the cold display of 1 000 000 entities, .NET 8). The shape
is the same to the bit.
**FIXED.** A text set in the last cell of a table could be written into the table's own groups. The last cell of a table ends where the
table's own groups begin, which the flags it holds decide (an override its flags give it is its own, the same override of the table's is
not), and the library kept that place from the first reading of the record; an edit of the cell that changed its flags left the place
behind, so that the next edit read the groups of the table as the cell's. On a table of 2 rows and 2 columns, `SetGridColor(1, 1,
HorizontalBottom, ...)`, `SetOverrides(1, 1, 0, 0x3F)` and `SetTextString(1, 1, "zzz")` left `TextString(1, 1)` empty on .NET Framework 4.8
and .NET 10, the text having gone into the value that follows the cell, the table's own; it reads "zzz" now. The end of the last cell is found
again from the record after each write of the cell, as a reading of the record places it, the last cell still written by its own bytes (1 000
calls on the last cell of a table of 1 000 cells stay within 4 s, as before). Found by making the same random edits on a record read anew
before each of them, which reads it whole: 60 of 4 000 random drawings (109 of their 99 000 saved lines) differed, on both runtimes, in the
bytes of a last cell; the saved bytes now equal those of the whole reading in 14 000 random drawings (49 870 saves on .NET 10) and in 316
saves of the 30 drawings with tables among AutoCAD's 167 sample drawings; on .NET Framework 4.8 the same 60 drawings differ from before. Nine runs of 60
edits of every setter that writes a cell, the last cell among them, in `DxfSpeed13Tests`, 7 of them differing before, and the three versions of the table of 2 rows and 2 columns above.
**CHANGED.** `ResetValue`, `SetCellType` and the lines of a cell (`SetGridColor`, `SetGridLineWeight`, `SetGridVisibility` and
`SetGridProperty` of a cell) are written into the place of the cell's own bytes, as `SetTextString`, `SetFormat` and the other setters of a
cell are: the bytes of the cells they change are kept apart from the record and put in once when it is next read, where each call read and
wrote every group of the record or copied its bytes, its groups and the places of its groups. The reset of each of the 931 cells of a table of
49 rows by 19 columns takes 4 ms and 6 MB in place of 4.0 s and 6.3 GB on .NET Framework 4.8 (9 ms and 5 MB in place of 3.3 s and 6.2 GB on
.NET 10), the lines (the bottom and right of each) 16 ms and 19 MB in place of 206 ms and 673 MB (24 ms and 16 MB in place of 146 ms and 415
MB), their showing 24 ms and 49 MB in place of 295 ms and 814 MB (50 ms and 40 MB in place of 180 ms and 499 MB); 10 000 cells, 50 rows by 200 columns, take 33 ms and 62 MB for the reset and
82 ms and 204 MB for the lines (98 ms and 57 MB, 0.21 s and 174 MB on .NET 10, where the lines took 11.7 s and 46 GB). The cells a call needs
(the cells beside the one set, the cells of a merged block) are read from their own bytes, each once; a cell whose content's looks are weighed
by `ResetValue` takes the rows of the table from the layout read last. A record written otherwise than whole by the library (a table read
from a file and not yet edited) is read and written as before. The saved bytes are the same: the hashes of the 931 resets and of the lines
and their showing agree with those of the library before, the fuzz above, and the tests of `DxfSpeed12Tests` and `DxfTableCellSetterSpliceTests`.
**CHANGED.** The first save after an edit of a drawing that holds a table written in the session no longer indexes every entity of the
drawing by its handle to ask whether the table needs its content made: the tables written are found among the records by their type, in one
walk that reads the handle of no other entity (`TryGetObject` made the index, 55 ms of the first save for 100 000 lines). A drawing of
100 000 lines (10 MB) with a table, opened, enumerated and saved after one edit, takes 9 ms and 40 MB for the first save in place of 57 ms and 52
MB on .NET Framework 4.8 (9 ms in place of 60 on .NET 10); the file saved is the same to the byte (hash 939605231CB81D...).
**CHANGED.** The lines of the rows of a kind (`SetGridColor(color, borders, rows)`, `SetGridLineWeight(lineWeight, borders, rows)` and
`SetGridVisibility(visible, borders, rows)`) are written into the places of the table's own groups alone, as the lines of a cell are: the
groups of its head and of its own part after its cells are read from their bytes, changed and put back, and the cells between are copied
as they stand, where each call read and wrote every group of the record. 108 calls (the six lines of the three kinds of rows, colour,
lineweight and showing, twice over) on a table of 49 rows by 19 columns (931 cells) take 9 ms and 21 MB in place of 590 ms and 982 MB on
.NET Framework 4.8 (14 ms in place of 420 ms on .NET 10). A table read from a file and not yet edited is read and written whole by the
first call, as before, and noted as written whole, so that the next call is the first kind. The cells kept apart from the record (those
set one after another) are put in it before the lines are written. The saved bytes are the same: the hash of the 108 calls and two cell
edits (D08C3490B8314F1A...), the 20 files of 120 random edits in `DxfSpeed14Tests`, 2 900 random drawings of 80 edits (the cell setters, the
lines of cells and of the rows of a kind, a range of cells, 800 of them with extended data after the table's own groups) saved to the byte
of what the library before gave on both runtimes, and 2 700 such runs equal, on .NET 10, to the same edits made on a record read anew
before each, which reads it whole.
**CHANGED.** The walk over the records of a file, which every opening makes, and the completion of a drawing's tables makes again on the
copy it is made on, finds the word of a record's type again by its bytes among the last it saw, in place of making a string of it and
looking it up for each record, and reads a group code line of the usual shape (spaces, up to nine digits, the line end) in one pass in place
of two; any other line is read, and refused, as before. The walk of a drawing of 100 000 entities (10 MB) takes 23 ms in place of 33 on
.NET Framework 4.8 (17 ms in place of 20 on .NET 10). The first save after an edit of such a drawing in which a table was added after it was
opened takes 33 ms in place of 52 (32 in place of 34), and the first save of a drawing of 100 000 lines made in the session, with a table,
45 ms in place of 66 (71 in place of 78); the files saved are the same to the byte (hashes 48E5F175BF7A8857... and 50371D00CCE4FD35...).
Not changed: that save still opens its copy by a walk over all its records (29 to 33 ms of the 40 that were spent on it before, 22 to 25
after), since the handles the copy gives to the content it makes are those a walk of its bytes finds the greatest of; and a table read from
a file pays 1.5 to 2.2 ms for 931 cells, once, at its second edit, for the places of its cells (1.0 ms to read its 25 000 groups into the
layout, 0.4 to place them), where each later edit costs 5 microseconds.
**FIXED.** The rule behind the leader band of an angle's words reads every arc from 2.5 landings out (it was 5.5), where the fit it
replaced was worse in 11 of the 12 styles probed at 30 out. What the rule had left at 30 out is the landing's sagitta (the landing squared
over the radius) again, by the direction of the point and the side of the circle (a table at every 10 degrees: up to 0.35 of it wider than
the rule near 40 degrees inside, 0.5 narrower near 100 and 260 degrees inside), by the rise of the point from the vertex's level to the
height of the arc's middle (the band narrows 1.6 sagittas on the left inside, 0.7 and 0.9 on the left and right outside, and widens 1.0 on
the right inside) and by the diagonal of the box turning over at that height, the height itself included; they fall away as one over the
radius (0.06 at 240 out). Leader presence differing in AutoCAD 2021's pictures of an angle of 60 degrees, the five exact directions
left out, before and now: 30 out 106 of 6 984 and 63 (12 styles; Arial 103 and 57), 58 of 5 670 and 29 (Arial 82 and 17), 130 of 6 860
and 93 (Arial 108 and 75), 38 out 66 of 6 499 and 19, 45 out 92 and 19 (Arial 75 and 24), 60 out 69 and 21, 90 out 28 and 6 of 6 499,
240 out 8 and 6 (Arial 6 and 7; 12 styles 18 and 10, Arial 10 and 14: probes within 0.03 of the edge) and 2 and 1 of the 3 492 along it,
55 and 54 of 24 056; of the older sets of pictures differing from AutoCAD's: a5 30 of 2 938 to 18, a6 11 of 2 346 to 5, a4 4 of 712 to 3,
a 2 of 96 to 0, a2 1 of 112 to 0 (its SHX probe), ta9 12 of 972 to 5, a7 65 of 5 832 to 36 (Arial 88 to 23), aq 132 of 6 860 to 94 (Arial
111 to 77), the jump at the arc's middle (d1, SHX, and td1, Arial, of 558 each) 66 to 70 and 66 to 64, and ta8 0 to 1 of 165; the other
sets (the angle's words moved, the DIMTEDIT sets, the arc length ones and every radius and diameter set but those below) are what they
were byte for byte (a3 and a3g, which have no pictures of AutoCAD's, changed with it). The unit tests that state a probe of AutoCAD's
each (DimensionFollowUps8Tests, 11 and 15) still hold. The arcs nearer than 2.5 landings keep the fit, and so do the words of an arc
length dimension.
**FIXED.** Level words inside a radius or a diameter keep to their line by a better law: two arrowheads (and 0.3 of an arrowhead more as
the line leans from upright over its first 22 degrees), 1.125 of the words' height on a line that runs down, the width of the words times
(0.3 + 0.65 of the cosine of the line's lean, 0.4 running down) times that cosine and a gap times the cosine and a quarter, in place of
the width and a gap times the cosine. Of AutoCAD 2021's pictures of "R5" to "R55.5555" put at half the radius, those differing from its
own: t9 34 of 1 292 to 19, t10 216 of 6 438 to 80, t11 554 of 9 460 to 140, and t6 1 of 1 584 unchanged; a radius of 8 with "R8" at 50
degrees leaves its line (8.17 asked of it, 8.0 before), and a diameter of 16 with words 3.5 high at 210 degrees keeps it (15.3 asked, 16.7).
**FIXED.** `GeoTransform3.Mirror` and `GeoTransform2.Mirror` across a plane or a line at 45 degrees give whole numbers where the
points were whole: (0, 10) across the line from (0, 0) to (1, 1) is (10, 0), and (0, 10, 0) across the plane y = x - 50 is (60, -50, 0),
where the matrix, built from the unit normal 0.7071067811865476 whose square is not quite a half, gave 9.999999999999998 (and
10.000000000000002 from a normal normalized twice) and 59.999999999999986. The matrix is now built from the normal divided by its greatest
component, over its squared length, which is exact where two components are equal and leaves the planes of the axes as they were to
the bit. Any other plane reflects a point within a last digit of where it did: on 20 000 random planes and points up to 20 000 out the
error against the exact reflection (computed with 300 bits) was 2.0E-12 on average and 1.2E-11 at the worst, where it had been 2.5E-12 and
1.7E-11. The benchmarks do not time a mirror and every signature matched before and after.
**FIXED.** The copy of an annotative TEXT, MTEXT or INSERT made by the presenter's MIRROR (or COPY, or a `Clone()` added to a drawing),
and the extension dictionary of an object made annotative by `Annotative = True`, have no `{ACAD_REACTORS` group: AutoCAD 2021 writes
the extension dictionary with its owner (330) alone (probed in its console, the DXF of a TEXT, an MTEXT, an INSERT and a HATCH mirrored
across y = 100 and written by `DxfOut`: the copy's skeleton of objects and reactors equals the library's for TEXT, MTEXT and INSERT),
and the dictionaries below it, down to the context, keep theirs. The library named the object as a reactor of its dictionary. A HATCH's
copy still differs from AutoCAD's in the view context AutoCAD adds (parked, as before).
**CHANGED.** The display of a large drawing after an edit no longer walks its entities where it can tell where the edit was: a MOVE of one
line at 1 000 000 entities is shown in 18 ms where it took 93 (.NET 8) and 22 where 198 (.NET Framework 4.8), an ERASE of one in 26 ms
where 196 and 25 where 278, a COPY of one in 25 ms where 192 and 30 where 283; at 100 000 entities 1.4 ms where 7.8, 1.9 where 13.8 and
2.3 where 13.7 (.NET 8). A display list keeps the list of entities it was drawn from and its version (the space of a drawing counts up
each entity added or erased; an entity added stands last), and holds its runs, items and box in arrays, so that a patch finds the
entities the edit names by their places, drawn again or dropped, takes the runs between them by one copy of their items and one of
their records, and draws the entities added last; its box is the older list's grown by the items drawn again, to the bit, unless one of
the items drawn again or dropped has a side level with a side of the box, or more than 64 runs were dropped (a layer switched), when it
is found again from every item as before. Where the places cannot be told (an undo or a redo, many entities named, an entity added or
erased that no handle names, no handle, a draw order, the Block Editor, an MTEXT with linked columns) the patch still walks the entities,
but by their records, not by an object made for each, and takes the runs it keeps in stretches (a COPY at 1 000 000 entities 74 ms
where 245 even then). The cold display, a layer switched and a REGEN are as they were within the noise (1 000 000 entities displayed in
2.4 s, regenerated in 0.76 s, .NET 8); the shapes of a LINE, an ARC and a CIRCLE are still kept (not keeping them is 55 MB less heap and
27 per cent more on a REGEN and a layer switched on). Display lists, saved bytes and pixels identical on 167 AutoCAD samples (the four
with an ACIS body save other bytes each run in any build) and generated drawings, under both runtimes. No public signature changed.

**NEW.** `DwgWriter` writes AutoCAD 2013 (AC1027), 2010 (AC1024) and 2004 (AC1018) as well as 2018: `DwgWriter.Write(database, path, "AC1024")`.
A drawing of a later version is made into the DXF of the version first, as `DxfDatabase.Save(path, version)` gives it, and what AutoCAD keeps
in such a file in its own way is put in as AutoCAD puts it (see the fixes below). The presenter's Save As lists "AutoCAD 2013/LT2013 Drawing",
"AutoCAD 2010/LT2010 Drawing" and "AutoCAD 2004/LT2004 Drawing" beside "AutoCAD 2018 Drawing" (`CadExportJob.DwgSaveTypes`), `SAVEAS` with
FILEDIA 0 takes 2013, 2010 and 2004 (R14, 2000 and 2007 are refused, "AutoCAD 2007(LT2007) Drawing (*.dwg) is not written: a DWG is saved
as AutoCAD 2018, 2013, 2010 or 2004 (2018, 2013, 2010, 2004)."), and Save (QSAVE) writes the DWG of the version last chosen again. The 167
drawings of AutoCAD 2021's samples and of the tests, each written as AC1018, AC1024 and AC1027 and opened in AutoCAD 2021 with `AUDIT`: all
167 open in every version; 160 of 167 at 0 errors in each (the originals: 156), the other 7 with the errors of their originals (126 of the
150 the originals have in all), and the 4 tables that had 6 each have none. R2000 (AC1015) is written since (next entry); R2007 (AC1021) is not written yet.
**FIXED.** A DWG of R2010 that held a table, a multileader, a wipeout or an image made AutoCAD 2021's `accoreconsole` take all the memory it
could get (66 GB and 86 GB within 240 s on two of the corpus files, the machine frozen) or refuse the file (`ErrorStatus` 53): the file named
no maintenance release, where AutoCAD's own names 226 for R2010 (104 for R2004, 125 for R2013), and its header and classes lacked the long
of 0 after their size that R2010 and later carry (R2004 has none). With them the 6 files that hung and the 13 that were refused open with
`AUDIT` as their originals do.
**FIXED.** Written as R2004, a drawing of a later version was refused by AutoCAD 2021 (`ErrorStatus` 53 or a hang) for five faults, each
found against AutoCAD's own R2004 file of the same drawing: the proxy graphics of a table or a multileader held their texts in 16 bits
(type 38) where R2004 holds them in 8 (type 11), made now as AutoCAD makes them (688 bytes of graphics for the multileader of the test
drawing, the size AutoCAD writes); a multileader and a multileader style lacked the extended data `ACAD_MLEADERVER` (version 2) and its
application in the APPID table; a field was written as R2007 lays it out (no format apart, a value with flags, unit and texts in 16 bits);
the vertex ids of a polyline were written, which are of R2010 and later; and a string of extended data was written as a length of one byte
and a code page of two, AutoCAD's being a length of two and a code page of one (the 18 INSERTs of `Map2Globe` and the ATTRIBs of
`Electrical - Imperial` that AutoCAD found "XData format Problem" in). A letter beyond the code page of a DXF of R2004 or before
(`\U+1EDB`) written as R2010 or later is the letter, not the escape AutoCAD finds "Un-normalized" in a layer's name.
**NEW.** The INSERT of a block cell in a table's block (`DxfTable.RecomputeTableBlock`, and every redraw of the presenter) is followed by
an ATTRIB for each attribute definition of its block that is not constant, as AutoCAD 2021's console draws them: filled and placed
by the INSERT's transformation as the INSERT command fills one, in the order of the block, an invisible definition's invisible, its words
the value the cell gives the definition (`SetBlockAttributeValue`) or the definition's own, empty where those are. BOLT's SIZE at (22, 0),
2.5 high, in a cell at scale 2 turned 30 degrees is an ATTRIB 5 high turned 30 degrees; a constant definition has none; a table drawn
twice has each ATTRIB once, and the drawing reads back byte for byte. The table's block had the INSERT alone, and the words of the
attribute were never drawn.
**CHANGED.** A block cell's block with an attribute definition that is not constant is laid out by two boxes, as AutoCAD 2021 lays it
out (probed in its console, margins 1.5, some 200 tables; the scale and the column of 6 fitted blocks after one pass of its layout, the
least column of 4 blocks not fitted and the place of the ATTRIB of 4 compared with this library's are equal to the fifth place). The room the block takes (`CadTableEditor.MinimumColumnWidth`, the least
a drag of a column or row goes to, what a block not fitted asks of its column and row) and the box it is aligned in its cell by are
those of the words in Arial, whatever the font of the definition's style (a Times style, or txt.shx, or simplex: AB at 2.5 high 4.66
wide, M12 6.79, DEFAULT 15.91, rotated, oblique and width factor kept; a constant definition is measured in its own font, as was
said, and one that is invisible or of no words counts none); where the drawing, the document and Windows find no arial.ttf the words are
measured in their own fonts, as before. The scale that fits the block to its cell comes from the box of the words in the definition's own
font, in one pass: AB at x 22 beside a block 20 by 10 in a cell 40 wide is fitted at 37 over 26.17, 1.41401, and the column, which
that scale gives 26.66 of Arial to hold, is widened to 40.69607 (a block fitted to a cell 40 by 30 was drawn at 1.38787, 37 over the
26.66 of Arial, and its column was not widened), the scale kept in the cell's 144 as AutoCAD stores it, so that a table drawn again
does not widen it again; a column set to another width is fitted anew. AutoCAD run twice (its `GenerateLayout` then
`RecomputeTableBlock`) gives 1.44061 and 41.40525, and widens the column 1.8 % more with each pass for ever; the presenter does one pass
and settles. `DxfTable.RecomputeTableBlock` alone, with no layout to widen the column, fits the block by the wider of the two boxes, 37
over 26.66, 1.38787, inside the cell. The least a column may be dragged to ignores a fitted block, as AutoCAD's does (9, with a
definition or none).
**CHANGED.** `SetFormat`, `SetDataType`, `SetBackgroundColorNone`, `SetOverrides` and the last cell of a table write the bytes of
their cell alone into the record, as `SetTextString` and the setters of a cell's look did, where each read and wrote every group of
it, and the layout the table reads is kept for the record that makes by noting the cell written and putting it in when it is next
read. Over each of the 1 000 cells of a table of 100 rows by 10 columns on .NET Framework 4.8: `SetFormat` 9.6 s to 70 ms,
`SetDataType` 9.6 s to 71 ms, `SetBackgroundColorNone` 1.2 s to 11 ms, `SetOverrides` 14.6 s to 0.55 s; 300 settings of the last
cell of that table: `SetBackgroundColorNone` 3.6 s to 87 ms, `SetTextString` 5.0 s to 20 ms. The drawing is the same to the byte
(150 steps of random settings, merges and the last cell, each compared with the record written whole); `SetTextString` and the
setters of a cell's look cost what they did.
**FIXED.** Words put out by the fit on a slanting line and kept level by DIMTOH, and turned words put between the extension lines, under
DIMTMOVE 1 in the presenter, follow AutoCAD 2021 where they had no leader or the wrong break (probed on its console, sets tw19, tw27,
tw32 to tw35 of the annotative round, differing pictures before and after). Level words so high that no leader goes with them (the
half of their box across the line reaches twice the leader's rise) are put out to the level of the knee the leader would have had,

line reaches that level 4.117 cot s - l / 2 beyond the nearer end (4.63 for a line of 5 at 30 degrees, 1.62 at 45, 1.35 at 120 degrees,
2.63 for a line of 9 at 30 degrees). Where that is more than nothing the line is run on to it, an arrowhead at least and two where the
arrowheads stand out on a short line of their own (a line of 5 at 30 degrees: no run, the level landing leaves from the end of that
short line; a line of 2 at 30 degrees with 24 digits: a run of 6.13 from where it ends; a line of 12: the run of 1.13 made 2.5), and a
level landing leaves from the bend, an arrowhead and the words and their gaps long under DIMTAD 1 (30.394 for 14 digits) and an

Where the line never reaches that level (9 digits on a line of 5 at 60 degrees, 8 at 75) the words stand where they did, and the line
between the extension lines is now drawn twice where the arrowheads stand out. tw19 64 -> 0 of 1 024 pictures that differed, and 590 -> 0
of the 1 152 of tw32 (lines of 2 to 12 at 20 to 65 degrees and their mirrors, 12, 16 and 24 digits, DIMTAD 1 and 0). Words put out
by the fit and then turned (DIMTEDIT Angle) on a slanting line do the same where their box is as high: the line run on to the knee's

within the leader's reach of the line (3.125 or less over it or under it) break it by their chord (6.63 for "100" turned 20 on a line
at 30 degrees) centred on the middle of what the line takes of their box (half the width and a gap along them, half the height and a

2.25 over it, where the box only grazes it; a box that meets the line past its end leaves it whole, and where the break would take
part of an arrowhead (it starts less than 2.5 from the end) the arrowheads turn out and the line is whole, drawn twice (tw27 20 -> 1
of 738). The run to the level of the point, which was for words past an end alone, is now made for turned words between the extension
lines as well where that level lies beyond the nearer end ("100" turned 20 put 2 along a line of 40 at 30 degrees and 3 under it: the
line run on backwards 3.196 and a landing of 2.735; 1 under it and 1.5 along, 0.116 below the level of the start: the arrowheads turn
out, the run is made two arrowheads and the words move down 2.384 to its level, the line drawn once). Probes of turned words in the
span: tw34 (3 510 pictures, slopes 30 to 135, angles 20, 45 and 90, across -3 to 4) 1 688 -> 288 differing, tw35 (2 028, near both ends)
809 -> 106; what is left are words exactly on an extension line or on the line past an end.
**FIXED.** Arc length dimensions (DIMARC) in the presenter put the arrowheads outside with the words on arcs of more than half a
circle where AutoCAD 2021 does, and follow it on the room the arc symbol takes at wide sweeps and just past 90 degrees (measured on
its console: some 19 600 more dimensions made by both; the counts are differing pictures before and after). Level words outside such
an arc take both arrowheads out with them where the box of the words (the symbol before them counted) stands within 0.9 DIMGAP of an
arrowhead that would stand in, and the arc's middle, to the half turn, points from a direction on: 101.5 degrees for a box (words,
symbol and two gaps) 0.93 wide, 30 degrees less for each unit wider, and 40 more for each unit the radius is past 0.3 (in text
heights, so scaled with the text); not below 100.2 degrees up to 185 degrees of sweep. The arc of 1 through 181 degrees put 0.45 out
has its arrowheads outside from 20 to 30 degrees from the horizontal (with the symbol, from 10 to 30), in at 10 and at 40, and the
same half a turn on; a wider DIMGAP keeps them out further (DIMGAP 0.18, symbol, through 204 degrees from 0: out to 0.68, in from
0.70; DIMGAP 0.09 to 0.42). Their landing is then an arrowhead along the arc from the first ray, not two: from 20 degrees put 0.3
out, no symbol, the words stand at (-0.353, -0.0772). Of the 1 929 pictures with the words outside that fitted this, 669 have the

114, now 87; the distance finely, sweeps 181 to 300 (4 284) 319, now 208; where the words stop going outside (1 488) 147, now 126; the
text, DIMGAP and DIMASZ variants (2 576) 299, now 70; the direction by 5 degrees, sweeps 181, 200 and 215 (1 296, new) 345, now 192;
the sizes of the box and gap at 200 degrees (456, new) 199, now 112; exact half circles (288, 252) 29, now 12 and 30, now 14. The arc

of half the text's height and for less past it, DIMASZ taking no part: the arc of 1 through 120 degrees from 10 keeps its words in

arcs of 1 and 3, text 0.18 and 0.36, 8 440: 140, now 113). The room both arrowheads want beside level words with the symbol on sweeps
from 90 to 115 degrees is 0.55 of what was fitted (0.2475 of the words' height at 100 degrees, not 0.45) within the window of the
arc's middle direction, and the whole of it within 5 degrees of its edges, as probed again with the put distance by 0.01 where the
earlier fit used 0.02: arcs of 1 from 0 to 60 degrees, sweeps 90.01 to 98 (3 315, new) 154, now 115, and from 20 to 30 degrees,
sweeps 98 to 114 (1 836, new) 94, now 56; the old probe of 10 074 270, now 256. Aligned words and DIMJUST 1 and 2 past a half circle
were probed to 0.01 (arcs of 1 from 0, 100 and 250 degrees, sweeps 181 to 250, 5 508 pictures): where the words and arrowheads come in
is AutoCAD's in 5 352, the 156 others standing one or two hundredths in the distance off; not changed. Every other set of
probes, of the 113 older ones, is as it was or nearer (104 of the 113 byte for byte; better: a5 33 to 30, aq 137 to 132, taq 126 to
111, tar24 862 to 858, tar24s 74 to 70, tw17 6 to 0, with the three above; none worse). Not as AutoCAD yet: the lower edge of the middle direction for the
arrowheads outside (it moves with the distance, the box and the sweep; 41 of 1 929), the arc point of aligned words outside such an
arc (a third of the way round near the arc, two thirds a few hundredths further out: from 0.32 at 181 degrees to 0.37 at 200; DIMJUST
1 and 2 have more changes of it), and the words' rotation and place beside a ray, a few thousandths off.
**CHANGED.** WMFIN gives a pen's or brush's colour the index AutoCAD 2021's console gives it, where it gave the nearest index of the
colours the indexes show on screen. AutoCAD's own palette for it, found by probing 72 000 colours through the console (a metafile of
16 000 pens at a time; the header's object count must cover them all), has the 24 hues of ten indexes each at the levels 166, 128, 76
and 38 of 255 (so 12 is (166, 0, 0), where the screen has (204, 0, 0)) and greys at 84, 118, 152, 187, 221 and 255 for 250 to 255,
8 and 9 never chosen; the nearest of it by distance in red, green and blue gives AutoCAD's index for 99.7 per cent of the colours
(the nearest of the screen's colours gave it for 33 per cent of 71 860, the darks and greys worst): dark green (0, 160, 0) is 92 and not 94, mid grey
(128, 128, 128) is 251 and not 8, (1, 1, 1) and (10, 10, 10) are 7, (170, 85, 85) is 13. The 0.3 per cent left are colours within a
unit or two of the line between two indexes.
**FIXED.** WMFIN places a text as AutoCAD 2021 does. The reference point of a text is the top left of its font's cell, and AutoCAD
puts the baseline the font's Windows ascent times the em below it (0.905 of the em for Arial, 0.8325 for Courier New, 1.0 for
Tahoma; the guess was 0.9 for every font) and the height of the TEXT at 0.8 of that (0.724, 0.666 and 0.8 of the em; the guess was
0.72), both in whole units of the file (an Arial of 80 is 72 and 57.6). A text turned a quarter reaches 0.0175 of the em further, one
turned to any other angle by a measure of its face (0.1525 of the em for Arial, 0.205 for Courier New, 0.05 for Tahoma, 0.1 for a face
not measured: Arial at 45 degrees is 0.84 of the em high and not 0.72), and one aligned to the bottom of the cell rests on the
descent times the em times the ascent over the capitals' height. A text aligned to the centre or the right is left justified, as
AutoCAD leaves it, and starts the width of its text (all of it or half) back from the point, the width being the advances of its
letters times that same ascent over the capitals (1.26 for Arial): "Hello" in an Arial of 400 starts 1152 back where it was
justified at the point. The look of a font is told by the face (letters of either case the same), bold at a weight of 700 and not
600, italic, character set and pitch and family, so that a Russian Arial is `WMF-Arial1` beside the Western `WMF-Arial0` with its
own character set kept in the style; the bytes of a text are Windows-1252 whatever the character set (80 is the euro sign and not
a control character). The reader of the metafile now plays SaveDC and RestoreDC (the pen, brush, font, text colour, alignment and
clip come back; RestoreDC of -1 or of a save's number) where it read them past, so a pen selected between the two no longer stays,
and IntersectClipRect, which clips the lines as AutoCAD's console does (a line is cut where it crosses the clip, one across the clip
along one axis and outside along the other is cut across the first only, one that misses the clip is left whole and one that
runs along an axis and misses it is dropped; a polygon or rectangle is never cut). A window of a width or height below nought
(the usual y-up metafile) turns the picture over as AutoCAD does: a window of 1 000 by -1 000 puts (100, 100) at (0.883, 0.883), one of

cut against one clip (769 of 772 as the rule above), 33 font looks, 610 texts in 24 faces and sizes from 1 to 800 units.

the one whose stem segment is farther from the stem's pick, then the nearer along the stem, then the earlier (334 of 356 such tees as
