**NEW.** A table made in code and the table styles of a drawing are saved with what AutoCAD 2021 builds of them when it reads the file
(`Save(path)`, `Save(stream)` and the forms with a version, R2007 to R2018 and going down to R2000 and R2004; `ToText()` and the drawing
itself are left as they are): for each table of a drawing of R2007 or later that has none, the extension dictionary with the XRECORD of
`ACAD_ROUNDTRIP_2008_TABLE_ENTITY`, the TABLECONTENT (each column's width, each row's kind and height, each cell's checksum, value and
content format, its alignment and fill, the lines it sets, the merged blocks) and the TABLEGEOMETRY; for each style that has none the
CELLSTYLEMAP of its title, header and data; the table and style listed in `ACDB_RECOMPOSE_DATA` and the three classes made and counted.
AutoCAD 2021 (DxfIn and DxfOut in its console) was given 6 tables (plain, merged, with borders, in no style named, with the title
left out, with looks of their cells) and 8 table styles (looks, colours and fills, lines, margins, title or header left out, a text
style) made by the library with none of these, and its own TABLECONTENT, TABLEGEOMETRY and CELLSTYLEMAP equal the library's group
for group in R2007, R2010, R2013 and R2018 (the 8 styles' maps in all four, 0 differences in 6 tables of 4 or 5 rows), and after
going down to R2000 and R2004 equal but for the heights of the rows and the geometry AutoCAD lays out; a further table of 48 cells
of 12 looks, 8 tables of lines (a bottom and a top set on one line, a hidden line, a line under a title, on the rim of the table, in
a merged block) and 8 tables of the line between a title, a header and the data are equal in their TABLECONTENT and their records
(but for the hidden line below); `AUDIT` finds 0 errors in the 25 files. The lines of
a table's cells are written as AutoCAD writes them when it has read them: the bottom or right of a cell as the top or left of the
cell below or beside it, a line of defaults none, the title's bottom as the header's top where the header's is a default, a cell that
gives a background colour filled (`283 0`). Left as they are, for AutoCAD to build: a table of a drawing of R2000 or R2004, with a block
cell, a field, a link, or lines of its own for a kind of rows (`SetGridColor(color, borders, rows)`). AutoCAD lays a table with a
TABLECONTENT out anew when it reads it (its TABLEGEOMETRY is zeros here, as it builds it, and the library measures no text): a title
of 6 high in a row of 9 becomes 11, and the cells gain the margins and lines of the format it writes then. A line written hidden stays
0, as AutoCAD reads it, where AutoCAD writes 1. Saving is slower in proportion to what is written, and writes it as bytes, not as
lists of groups: 5 tables of 100 rows by 20 columns (10 000 cells), 1.3 MB before and 11.3 MB now, take 127 ms and 189 MB in place of
1 ms as R2018 (462 ms and 522 MB when the content was built as lists of groups), 295 ms as R2013 and 330 ms as R2000 on .NET Framework 4.8
(83, 179 and 222 ms on .NET 10); 1 000 cells take 11 ms as R2018, 27 as R2013 and 35 as R2000, 100 cells 2, 4 and 4. The completed
copy of a drawing is kept, weakly, while the drawing is not changed, so that saving it again (in another version, say) does not make the
content again: 6 ms in place of 127 ms as R2018 on .NET Framework 4.8, until a garbage collection drops the copy.
**CHANGED.** Saving a drawing in an older version (`Save(path, version)`, `Save(stream, version)`) converts its text faster and with less
memory, the file written the same to the byte: the converter reads a group's code from the text without a string of its own, keeps each
short value once however often it stands, writes the codes it knows ready made and sizes its output to its input, and the records the
library writes go out without an array for each group. A drawing of 100 000 lines and 5 000 objects (10.5 MB) saved as R2013 takes
556 ms and 370 MB in place of 957 ms and 510 MB on .NET Framework 4.8 (368 ms and 363 MB in place of 522 ms and 460 MB on .NET 10);
the 5 tables above, 295 ms in place of 918 ms.
**CHANGED.** Saving a drawing in an older version (`Save(path, version)`, `Save(stream, version)`) writes the converted file as bytes
straight from the groups the converter holds, where it built a text (22 MB for a drawing of 11 MB), encoded it again as UTF-8 and read
the bytes as a file to save them: the file is written the same to the byte, but for the cases below which are still made as before. A
drawing of 100 000 lines and 5 000 objects (11.3 MB) saved as R2013 takes 182 ms and 90 MB in place of 262 ms and 142 MB on .NET
Framework 4.8 (70 ms and 88 MB in place of 115 ms and 139 MB on .NET 10), the 5 tables of 100 rows by 20 columns (10 000 cells)
266 ms and 228 MB as R2013 in place of 358 ms and 304 MB, and 322 ms and 257 MB as R2000 in place of 363 and 335 (best of 7). The file is
still read again, as before, where the drawing has a face of a polyface mesh (whose marker AcDbVertex before its AcDbFaceRecord reading
mends), is saved as R12, or has letters beyond ASCII and goes to R2004 or R2000, whose bytes are in the code page of the header.
**CHANGED.** Building a table cell by cell costs in proportion to the cell. After the first edits of a table, which write its record
whole, `SetTextString`, `SetValue` and the setters of a cell's look (`SetAlignment`, `SetTextHeight`, `SetTextStyle`,
`SetContentColor`, `SetBackgroundColor`, `SetTextRotation`) read the groups of the cell's own bytes and write them back into their
place, the rest of the record copied as it is, where each read and wrote every group of the table; the record's bytes are those of a
writing of every group, to the byte (the last cell of a table, and the cells of a record whose groups stand other than the file
writes them, are still written through the whole record). A table of 1 000 cells, each given its text, takes 36 ms and 195 MB in
place of 5 343 ms and 8.7 GB on .NET Framework 4.8 (64 ms in place of 4 359 ms on .NET 10), 3 000 cells 354 ms in place of 48.5 s
(370 ms in place of 31 s), and 10 000 cells 3.2 s (3.9 s on .NET 10) where the same loop had not ended after 15 minutes; what is left grows with the record,
whose bytes are copied for each cell. Saved bytes equal before and after in 27 168 saves of random drawings with tables edited
between saves, in every version from R2000 to R2018 and for a table read back from text in each line end and padding, on .NET
Framework 4.8 (21 208 of them on .NET 10 too), and in the 1 169 saves of AutoCAD's 167 sample drawings.
**CHANGED.** Adding tables to a drawing, copying them to another, and saving a drawing of many tables cost in proportion to the
tables, not to their number times the drawing: a table is given a block of its own without counting the entities of the drawing that
name it (the block made a moment ago can have no other), the name of the block a table is drawn by is read from the head of its
record, a table style is read from its record once for the 54 looks a table drawn anew asks of it, the entities of a drawing are
looked up by handle without making an object of each, the names under which the named object dictionary holds an object are found
for every object in one walk of its dictionaries where each pointer of a copied table walked them all, and the completion of a drawing
lists its tables in `ACDB_RECOMPOSE_DATA` once at its end, not by reading and writing the list for each. 400 tables of 3 rows and 4
columns, each cell given its text, are added in 311 ms and 347 MB in place of 1 966 ms and 4.4 GB on .NET Framework 4.8 (160 ms in place
of 1 023 ms on .NET 10), 1 600 of them in 1.3 s and 1.5 GB in place of 25 s and 59 GB (0.7 s in place of 13.5 s); saved as R2018 after an
edit they take 90 ms in place of 179 ms (400) and 389 ms in place of 1 690 ms (1 600); copying 400 tables among 5 000 other objects takes
80 ms in place of 981 ms, among 20 000 91 ms in place of 4 828 ms (the same, 54 ms in place of 3 488 ms, on .NET 10), whatever the
objects around them. Saved bytes equal before and after in the same saves as above, and in the copies of 25 tables among 120 objects.
Not changed: the completion of a drawing of 100 000 entities (10 MB) that holds a table still takes 158 ms to save after an edit (169
ms before), nine tenths of it the reading of the copy it is made on.
**CHANGED.** Saving a drawing that holds a table or a table style written in the session no longer makes an object of every entity
of the copy it completes them on, nor a string of the whole file. The copy is opened from the bytes the drawing saves as, not from a
text made of them and encoded again; its tables are found in its records by handle in one pass, each given the model or paper space
it stands in, where finding one by `TryGetObject` made the drawing's entities and read the handle of each (most of the 158 ms above);
and the table style its lines are read against is found among the objects. The file saved is the same to the byte. A drawing of
100 000 lines (15.3 MB) with a table, saved after an edit, takes 52 ms and 116 MB in place of 157 ms and 188 MB on .NET Framework 4.8
(39 ms and 115 MB in place of 89 ms and 187 MB on .NET 10), and 20 000 lines (3 MB) 11 ms in place of 26 (9 ms in place of 24). The
text is still the way where the drawing's text is not its bytes as UTF-8 (a mark at its start, bytes read as the replacement
character, a code page), and a table of a block is still found among the entities. Not changed: the first save of a drawing indexes
the entities of the drawing itself, once, as it does for any `GetObject`.
**CHANGED.** The cells of a table set one after another are written once, when the table's record is next read, and no longer copy
the record each: the bytes of the cells set (by the setters that write a cell's own bytes, the last cell and `SetFormat`,
`SetDataType`, `SetBackgroundColorNone` and `SetOverrides` among them) are kept apart and put in their places by a read of the table
or of its entity, a copy or a save, the record's bytes the same as before to the byte. The cells noted for the layout the table reads
last are noted as before, and the layout is patched with them when the record is put together. A run of 10 000 cells of a table, each
given its text, takes 0.37 s and 477 MB in place of 4.3 s and 13.5 GB on .NET 10 (0.44 s and 491 MB in place of 3.6 s and 13.5 GB on
.NET Framework 4.8), 5 000 cells 0.24 s and 239 MB in place of 0.92 s and 3.5 GB, one cell among 10 000 0.05 ms in place of 0.19, and
the last cell of a table of 10 000, set once, no longer copies its 2.5 MB (0.1 ms in place of 0.2). `ResetValue` and `SetCellType` are
not on this path: written cell by cell they leave the table's record as a writing of every group of it would not, the last cell's end
being decided by the flags it holds (two of the fuzz's seeds differed in the bytes of the last cell), so they still write the whole
record (931 resets take 8.0 s, `SetCellType` 0.65 s). `NormalizeEdges`, which gives a table's cells the lines AutoCAD builds when a
table is completed, shares one list of lines among the cells that have none (400 small tables saved after an edit 44 ms in place of
52 on .NET 10, within the noise of the machine). Saved bytes equal before and after in 71 000 saves of random drawings with tables in
model space, paper space and a block, edited setter by setter and in runs of up to 220 with no read between (29 910 saves of 2 500
drawings on .NET Framework 4.8, 41 734 of 3 500 more on .NET 10, and the 2 500 of the first on .NET 10 again), and in the 501 saves of
AutoCAD's 167 sample drawings on both.
**CHANGED.** A body or a region saved to R2013 or later from ACIS text, or from the binary of another version of the modeler, is
dated with the date of the SAT's own head (AutoCAD writes none there, so none) and not with the clock, and a body whose extended data
gives no GUID is given one made of its handle and its data (the first 16 bytes of their SHA-256, as a GUID made of a name) and not at
random, so that the same drawing saved twice is the same bytes where each save differed in its date and its GUID. AutoCAD 2021 read
the 24 drawings made of 4 AutoCAD samples (with 3DSOLIDs and a REGION) by saving each as R2013, as R2010 and as R2000, those two again as R2013,
and the R2000 one as R2018 too, in its console (`DxfIn`), `AUDIT` finding 0 errors, with the volume of each solid and the area of each region
those of the sample; 1 163 of the 1 169 saves of the 167 samples are the same bytes as before, the 6 others being the R2013 saves of
drawings with bodies.
**CHANGED.** The extension dictionary of a table made in code (and of any record given one) is spliced into its record as bytes, not
written group by group from a list of every group of the record: a table of 2 000 cells no longer allocates some 5 MB for it,
and the greatest handle of a copy of the drawing is read without a list for each record. Saving the 10 000 cells as R2018
allocates 127 MB in place of 157 MB on .NET Framework 4.8 and the time is the same (130 ms); 400 tables of 3 rows and 3 columns among
4 600 objects 208 MB in place of 221 MB. Bytes saved the same in 72 174 saves of random drawings with tables, edited between saves, in
six versions, CRLF and LF, padded and unpadded codes, on each runtime, and in 1 000 saves of the AutoCAD sample drawings to every version
(but six saves to R2013 of drawings with ACIS bodies, which differ from one run to the next, as they did before).
**FIXED.** A table made in code in a drawing of R2000 to R2007 had the version number `280 0` of R2010 and later in its record, which
AutoCAD leaves out of those versions. An empty value in the TABLECONTENT of a table going from R2007 or later to R2004 or R2000 is
written `90 0` and `91 0` as AutoCAD writes it (the `91` was missing), and read going up: a table saved down and up again with an
empty cell stays a table (it was written as its block).
**FIXED.** The Block Editor's save works out the anonymous *U blocks of a dynamic block whose action holds a line that was erased,
as AutoCAD 2021's `UpdateAnonymousBlocks` does (eleven panels of ten kinds of action probed through its console, four INSERTs each,
a circle added, lines moved or erased in nine ways: 90 of the 99 edits alike, the 9 left below): the erased line drops
out of the action, which goes on with the rest, every value of the INSERTs kept, and the line is gone from each *U block. A panel
whose Width moves its right edge and bottom, the bottom erased, and its INSERTs set to Width 150 and 200, has them place *U
blocks with the right edge at x 150 and 200 and no bottom; the library left the old *U blocks as they were, the bottom still in
them, because the action named a handle the block no longer had. A stretch, scale, rotate, flip, polar stretch, lookup and XY move
alike; an action left holding nothing does nothing. Not done: an array that loses a line (AutoCAD 2021 drew no copies of the
rest, and for a panel of that one action reset its Width to 100, where a second parameter's value was kept), and a visibility
state that loses one (AutoCAD hid every line of the states in the INSERTs set to a state, where the library shows them as the
state says): both leave the *U blocks as they were.

**FIXED.** A text that leans (an oblique angle), given by an INSERT or `TransformBy` a scale unlike along its two axes, keeps the
shape the scale makes of it, as AutoCAD 2021 worked it (`SetAttributeFromBlock` and the INSERT command both, in its console): the
attribute T8 3 high, 0.7 wide, leaning 15 degrees, of an INSERT scaled 2 along x, is 3 high, 1.4 wide and leans 28.2 degrees, where
the library made it 2.644 high and 1.588 wide, of the right lean and the wrong size; of an INSERT turned 75 degrees and scaled 2 by
0.5 it is 1.5 high, 2.8 wide, leaning 47 degrees, where it was 1.023 high and 4.104 wide. A text that does not lean, and every
scale alike along both axes, is as it was to the last digit. Of 221 attributes (13 definitions of every justification, 17 INSERTs
moved, turned, scaled, mirrored and given a normal, MIRRTEXT 1) 6 differed, now none; 7 more differ only in the second point
AutoCAD reports for a text aligned left, which has none.

**CHANGED.** ATTSYNC says what AutoCAD 2021's own table of strings (the resources of Battman.arx) says: "The selected entity is not
a block." for a pick that is no block, "The selected block has no attributes." for a block with no definitions (both ask for another
block), "Block table contains no attributed block named PLAIN." for a name that is no attributed block (and asks again),
"Attributed blocks:" over the list of "?", "This drawing contains no attributed blocks." when there is none. They were the words of
the help page, and "Block "PLAIN" not found.". A name typed may be a wildcard, as the usage in the same table has it, "a block
name or wildcard": `ATTSYNC` `Name` `GB*` brings in line every attributed block it matches, as one undo step.
Not probed: ATTSYNC itself cannot run in accoreconsole (its command lives in Battman.arx, which imports ACAD.exe and loads only in
the full program, whether fed from a script or standard input, and nothing like it is in the managed API or in acdb24.dll);
`SetAttributeFromBlock`, which Battman.arx imports, was probed in its place (13 definitions of every justification, 17 INSERTs
moved, turned, scaled, mirrored and given a normal), and the INSERT command's own attributes: with MIRRTEXT 0 an INSERT mirrored
in x gets attributes mirrored with it, as the library gives them, where `SetAttributeFromBlock` of the same transformation gave
them readable, normal (0, 0, 1) and turned back; with MIRRTEXT 1 both mirror. Which of the two ATTSYNC takes is not known.
**CHANGED.** A large drawing displays faster, in its own costs, with the display lists, the saved bytes and the pixels as they were
(167 AutoCAD samples and five generated drawings, item for item and field for field). A profile of the drawing of 100 000 entities
(lines, arcs, circles, polylines with a bulge, texts and an INSERT in fifty) found the time not in the shapes but in what is asked of an
entity first: a polyline asked whether it has a width (`DxfPolyline.HasWidth`) made the typed value of every group it holds, 31 % of the
cold display and 58 % of that of polylines alone; whether an entity is visible (`DxfEntity.Visible`) made the list of all its groups to
read one, and the look of an entity a dictionary for each. Each now walks the bytes of its record where the groups stand (a polyline's
width 0.21 µs and 24 bytes where it took 0.74 and 2.4 KB, visibility 0.07 to 0.09 µs and 24 bytes where it took 0.34 to 0.39 and 0.5 to
1.1 KB), a TEXT is drawn from one pass over its groups where its twelve properties found theirs one by one (an attribute, a text with an
extension dictionary and a copy that carries contexts read as before), and a block with no handle, as in R12, is listed once a build and
not for each INSERT of it. Nothing is kept: a text or a polyline edited after it was drawn is read afresh. Cold display of the drawing of
100 000 entities 255 ms where it took 330 under .NET 8, 431 where 519 under .NET Framework 4.8, a layer switched on 75 ms where 123, with 154
MB of garbage where there were 277; texts alone 245 ms where 360, 100 000 INSERTs of a block of 20 entities 1 175 ms where 1 591, and the
drawing of 1 000 000 entities 2.8 s where 3.4 (.NET 8) and 4.3 where 5.0 (.NET Framework). The shapes an entity keeps stay: the same
objects each time they are asked for. No public signature changed.
**FIXED.** Turned words (DIMTEDIT Angle) put near an end of a slanting line under DIMTMOVE 1 in the presenter go back from the line run
on to the leader from the middle where AutoCAD 2021 does (probed on its console with some 20 000 more probes, the sets tw17 to tw31 of
the round, differing pictures before and after). AutoCAD draws the shorter of two leaders: the line run on from its end to the level of
the words' point and a level landing back from there (the run and the landing together), or the straight leader from the middle of the
line to the point; where the level of the point is not beyond the level of either end of the line, or the leader from the middle is
the shorter, it keeps that. An upright line of 40 with the words 8 past its end is run on up to 45 across and has the leader from the
middle beyond (60 at 5 past the end, 36.67 at 12, 30 at 20); a line of 40 at 60 degrees up to 13.2708 across (30.987 of leader either
way), at 30 degrees 5.5025, at 20 degrees 3.5664, and a line of 100 at 60 degrees 34.28; lines leaning back (120 and 135 degrees) are
run on as long as the level of the point is beyond the end (13 across at 120 degrees for a line of 25, not 14). Neither DIMASZ, DIMTXT,
DIMGAP, DIMEXE, the length of the words, their angle nor the distance of the line from its points change the cut-off, and the distance
past the end hardly does (13.52 across at 5 past, 12.42 at 30, a line of 40 at 60 degrees). Words over the line by less than DIMGAP and
an arrowhead (or half their height and DIMEXE, whichever is more: 3.125 for the style of the probes, 2.8, 3.7, 4.375 and 4.625 as they
are varied) are run on whatever the length: a line of 10 at 20 degrees with the words 1 over it has the line run on 10.747 to their level,
a landing of 2.5 and the words moved in to stand at its end. The run is made an arrowhead long where it would be shorter, the landing
and the words moving with its end: a line of 40 at 140 degrees with the words 8 past and 5 over has 2.04 of run made 2.5 (the words
0.459 further along and 0.295 higher), an upright line of 7.2 with the words 1.44 past its end and 5 over has the run made 2.5 and
the words stand 1.06 higher, and words 4 along from the start of a long line leaning back run its line on backwards. On a line too
short for its arrowheads they stand out on a line of their own and the run starts where that ends (two arrowheads at least), and the
line between the extension lines is drawn twice where the leader goes from its middle and once where the line is run on (72 probes of
lines of 3, 5 and 6 at six slopes). Words put past an end of a level line within the leader's reach are laid on the line, their point
as high as it, and the line run on to a gap and half their width short of them (48 probes). Of the probe sets, the differing pictures
before and after: tw17 6 of 324 now 0, tw18 17 of 1 188 now 2, tw20 112 of 480 now 0, tw22 59 of 154 now 1, tw23 (1 140 probes of
slopes 20 to 80 and lengths 10 to 100 across the cut-off) 615 now 0, tw24 (past the end by 5 to 30) 366 now 0, tw26 (the line 5 to 60
from its points) 336 now 0, tw25 (by style, words and angle, 2 200 probes) 1 422 now 0, tw28 (6 480 probes of the cut-off bisected to 0.0025 over slope, length and distance past)
4 240 now 7 (exact ties of the landing's side), tw29 309 of 672 now 0, tw30 72 of 72 now 0, tw31 48 of 48 now 0; the other 73 sets of probes (tw1 to tw16, tw19, tw21, the m sets, tm3, ts1 and the 51 made by AutoCAD itself) are as they were, to the byte. Not as AutoCAD yet: words on the line a little
inside an end (across 2.25 within 5 of it: AutoCAD turns the arrowheads out, draws the line twice and breaks it round the turned box
off the foot of the point, 20 of 738), the words of an exact tie of the leader's side (a level line of 7.2 with the words below its
middle at 180 degrees), and level words put out by the fit past a leader on a line of 5 or 9 (tw19: 64 of 1 024, where AutoCAD draws
the line run on to the level of the leader's knee and the words on a landing).
**CHANGED.** A large drawing displays faster again, in what the display asks of an INSERT and of a closed polyline with a bulge, with the display
lists, the saved bytes and the pixels as they were (167 AutoCAD samples and nine generated drawings, item for item and field for field under
.NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8, the pixels of 171 of them in three views, plain, selected, highlighted and with a hover). An INSERT read its
block (`BlockTableRecord`), its insertion point (`Position`) and its placing (`BlockTransform`) one property at a time, each looking again
for the normal, the scale factors and the angle among the groups of its record, the placing making two 4 by 4 matrices: 1.7 µs and 2.5 KB an
INSERT, 16 % of a drawing of INSERTs alone. They are read in one pass over the bytes of the record (`DxfBlockReference.TryReadForDisplay`),
0.6 µs and the one string of the name of its block, for an INSERT whose record holds no extension dictionary, so no annotative context and no clip (those, a copy that
carries contexts and an INSERT given its block in code are read property by property as before), with the arithmetic of the properties
step for step, so that the point, the matrix and the block are the same to the bit; an INSERT with no ATTRIB after it no longer makes the
frame its attributes are drawn in; whether an INSERT is an array (a MINSERT, asked of every INSERT when its object is made) is told by a
walk of the bytes and not by the groups made a list; the block a run of INSERTs places, and the layer a run of entities is on, are found
again by the very object asked for last, not by a dictionary each time. The loop a closed polyline with a bulge is made (`GeoPolygonArc3`)
and its area are built with the arrays they keep and the one chain the plane is found from where they were made of lists, a chain and a
copy (0.61 µs and 2.2 KB a loop with its area, 0.37 µs and 0.6 KB now, .NET 8), every vertex, bulge, normal and area the same to the bit,
the same exceptions with the same words (300 000 generated loops, lists, arrays and sequences, vertices doubled, a last one on the first,
bulges out of the plane or not numbers, against the long way, and the 34 results of the benchmark suite match their approved signatures); and
the line end of a record is found by a short loop before the vectorised search is set up for a line of three bytes. Cold display of the
drawing of 100 000 entities (open not counted) 217 ms where it took 247 under .NET 8, 345 where 449 under .NET Framework 4.8, a layer
switched on 45 ms where 52 and 78 where 89, a REGEN 109 where 124 and 173 where 221, 121 MB of garbage where there were 155; 100 000 INSERTs
of a block of 20 entities 858 ms where 1 115 (.NET 8) and 1 494 where 2 057 (.NET Framework), a layer switched on 316 where 441 and 550 where
758, 424 MB of garbage where 640; the drawing of 1 000 000 entities 2.1 s where 2.3 under .NET 8 and 3.8 where 4.4 under .NET Framework,
1 155 MB of garbage where 1 492 (a MOVE and its display, 250 ms, is as it was within the noise). No public signature changed.

**CHANGED.** A large drawing opens and is edited faster again, and one with INSERTs of unlike scale factors displays nine times faster, the
display lists, the saved bytes and the pixels as they were (167 AutoCAD samples and twelve generated drawings, item for item and field for field
under .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8, and the pixels of 179 of them in three views, plain, selected, highlighted and with a hover). The note of
the last round, that a MOVE and its display at 1 000 000 entities was no slower and not told from noise, was wrong: it was 60 ms slower,
296 and 292 ms where 232 and 239 (the display alone, the move itself 10 ms, medians of eight moves with the undo read-aheads let finish
between them). The display after an edit makes the list again from the older one and asked its table of insertion points for the handle
of every one of the million entities it copied (a hash of a string ignoring case and a probe among 220 000 entries, 180 ms of the 300);
a run now says whether its entity kept a point, so that only those are asked for, and the table is the older list's own until a patch has
a point to take out or put in, then a copy of it: the display after a MOVE of one line is 165 ms where it was 295 (.NET 8) and 375 where
540 (.NET Framework), the MOVE with its display 125 ms where 336 and 307 where 399. The look of an entity (layer, linetype, thickness, colour, lineweight,
true colour) and whether it is hidden are found in one walk over its record, not two, and the look from the places of its groups among those
of looks met before (64 are remembered), so that an entity of a look met makes no string of them and no `Look` (a REGEN of 100 000 entities
makes 9 MB less garbage; a layer switched on 48 ms where 60 and a REGEN 153 where 171 at 100 000, 492 ms where 696 and 1.2 s where 2.0
at 1 000 000, .NET 8); a group 102 is told from its bytes, a brace or not, as `Trim` reads it, and no longer made a string; the origin of
a block is read once until the records of its file change, not for every INSERT; the style of the last colour and weight is answered as it
was. The greatest handle of a file, which opening it asks for, is found as the records are walked, not by a pass of its own over every
group of every record (a quarter of an opening): 1 000 000 entities open in 0.50 s where 0.90 under .NET 8, 100 000 in 45 ms where 86, and
1.8 s where 3.1 under .NET Framework (on a loaded machine; 0.87 s where 1.30 on a quiet one); a new handle is the one it was, over
generated files with pointers, seeds, a DIMSTYLE and the header's own 390. An INSERT whose scale factors are not alike draws the arcs and
circles of its block as chains of points, each found by the shape's own arithmetic, 0.16 ms an INSERT of a block of 20 entities; the points
of a shape of a block, before the INSERT's matrix, are now found once for all the INSERTs that place it, and each INSERT puts them through its
own matrix into its array at once: 20 000 INSERTs display in 0.41 s where they took 3.5 s (.NET 8; 0.72 s where 4.5 s under .NET Framework),
a layer switched on in them in 0.19 s where 1.2, with 451 MB of garbage where 1 479, every point the same to the bit. Not changed, with the
reason: the cold display of 100 000 mixed entities (222 ms where 233, within the noise: what it does is the first touch of every
record and its shapes, three walks over each, one of which is now gone) and the table of insertion points of a list made whole (a lookup and
an insert for each entity that has one, 2.7 % of the display). No public signature changed.

**FIXED.** Arc length dimensions (DIMARC) in the presenter follow AutoCAD 2021 where the last round left them (measured on its console,
some 50 000 more dimensions made by both; the sets listed are differing pictures of those probed, before and after).
Words next to a ray (DIMJUST 1 and 2) stand a cube of the arrowhead and of the half of their box over 24 radii squared further along,
as AutoCAD lays them by chords: the arc of 3 through 40 degrees from 10 put 2.4 out, DIMJUST 1, aligned words "2.0944" with the arc
symbol before them, stand 0.00125 further along, the half of their box 0.63 and the arrowhead 0.18 (the arc of 3, DIMJUST 1 and 2, level
and aligned, put 0.5 to 0.95 out: 76 of 216 pictures differed, now 18; of the 384 of both styles, symbols, text sizes and arrowheads
280, now 4; 10 of 108 of the earlier probe, now 1). The arc symbol before words on a sweep of 100 to 165 degrees takes more room as the
sweep widens, by the height of the words and the sine of the direction of the arc's middle (0.09 of the height at 100 degrees, 0.24 at 150,
0.32 at 165): the arc of 1 through 150 degrees from 10 put 0.695 out has "2.6180" outside past its first end and at 0.70 between its
rays, where they came in from 0.68 (arcs of 1 and 3, text 0.18 and 0.36 high: 257 of 8 440 differed, now 161; the arcs of 1 from 10 and
100 degrees, 5 152: 158, now 151). Level words outside stand to the right or the left by where the arc stands a third of the way
round, not where its first end points (the arc of 1 through 179.99 degrees put 0.45 out has them to the left from 170 degrees, where
the end points up, and to the right from 350, where it points down: 94 of 252 differed, now 76, the 36 starts of the sweeps under 180
degrees all as AutoCAD). The room both arrowheads need beside level words with the symbol is a window, not a power of the sine: 0.12
more, 0.85 of their height, where the arc's middle points within 75 to 102 degrees of the horizontal (259 to 288 for the other
half turn) for "1.0472" and its symbol, 64 to 114 for a single digit, and none elsewhere (arcs of 10 put 12 out, DIMASZ 0.36, chord
2.24: both arrowheads between the rays from 66 and from 96 degrees, outside from 70 to 94; 4 598 of 4 598 pictures of the edges, 208
differed, now 21; 1 573 of the other half turn, 31, now 2; DIMASZ 0.27 and 0.36 from 50 to 150 degrees, 7 308: 92, now 10; level words
by DIMASZ 0.09 to 0.5, 8 840: 135, now 62; aligned, DIMASZ 0.09 to 1, 8 424: 46, now 29; the old probe of single digits 181, now 176).
Not as AutoCAD yet: sweeps of 180 degrees and more put the words past the second end (the arc point a third of the way, never two
thirds) and fit them between the rays in more cases, which this does not follow (100 of 5 152 pictures of the arcs from 10 degrees
through 180 differ); level words under DIMJUST 1 on a sweep of 80 degrees have their arrowheads outside, where this keeps them in
(12 of the 18 pictures left of 216); the distance both arrowheads first come in at DIMARCSYM 0 and 100 degrees, 0.05 later. Every
other set of probes (angles of three points, radius, diameter, linear and DIMARC away from these cases: 80 sets) is as it was, to
0.0003 in a text's place for the DIMJUST ones. The text of an arc length at a tie of the fifth decimal (an arc of 10 through 0.048005
radians, 0.48005) is rounded either way by AutoCAD from the angles' last digits; the probes that showed it fed the presenter angles
rounded to six decimals where AutoCAD had ten, so there was nothing to fix there.
**FIXED.** The lines of a table's cells set one cell at a time (`SetGridColor`, `SetGridLineWeight`, `SetGridVisibility` and
`SetGridProperty` of a cell) read and wrote every group of the table for each call, so that a loop over a table took time that grew
with its square. After the first call, which writes the record whole so that its groups stand as the library writes them, each call
copies the bytes of the cells it changes into a record of its own and keeps the layout and the places of the groups for the next.
The four settings of each cell of a table of 200 rows by 10 columns (8 000 calls) took 141 s on .NET 10 (17.7 ms a call, 0.9 ms
now) and take 6.9 s; 100 by 10 (4 000 calls) 40.2 s and 2.2 s; 50 by 10 (2 000 calls) 11.9 s and 0.8 s on .NET Framework 4.8. The
drawing is the same to the byte: the text of 40 drawings of random settings, merges and texts over a plain, a CRLF, an unpadded, a
reloaded and a unicode file, and of the four table sizes, hash equal before and after. `SetGridProperty` over a range was one
writing already and is as fast as it was.
**FIXED.** The least a column may be dragged or set to (`CadTableEditor.MinimumColumnWidth`, the drag of a column's line,
`SetColumnWidths`) ignored the blocks of block cells. As AutoCAD 2021's `MinimumColumnWidth` gave it in its console (margins 1.5, text
of 6 and 4.5), a block cell not fitted to its cell asks the width its block's extents fill at the cell's scale and turn, and the two
margins, where that is more than the 9 of the margins and the title's text: a block 30 wide 33, at scale 2 63, turned 45 degrees
31.28427 and turned 90 13 (for a block 30 by 10); a block 2 wide 9; a fitted block 9; a block merged across two columns asks the column
it starts in alone (33 and 9).
**FIXED.** A block cell in the first column left its row to its block (a block 2 by 2 in rows of 3 made them 5, a fitted one left them
at 3) where AutoCAD 2021 lays every row out by the one line, 4/3 of the text height and the margins, of its first cell, whatever it
holds: 9 in both, and 13 for a block 10 high (9 tables of 4 rows of AutoCAD's console).
**CHANGED.** An attribute definition of a block cell's block is counted in the block's extents, as AutoCAD 2021 counts it (it was left
out): the words the cell gives it, else its own, measured in the fonts of the drawing, or of the document where the drawing names none
(`CadTableEditor` looks in the document's folders and the system's for the length of the measure only); none where the words are empty
or the definition is invisible, and a constant definition its own words whatever the cell gives. A block 20 wide with a definition at x
22 of words 31.7 wide (CONSTANT TEXT at 2.5 high) asks a column 56.67 wide (22 + 31.67 and the margins, as AutoCAD gave), an invisible
one or one of no words 23, a definition inside the block's box none. The column is the width of the words in the drawing's font: AutoCAD
measures the words of a definition that is not constant in a TrueType font (4.66, 6.79 and 15.91 wide for AB, M12 and DEFAULT at 2.5,
where txt.shx makes 4.17, 5.83 and 16.67), a difference of a millimetre or less that is parked, with the width AutoCAD fits a block
with a definition to (a block fitted to a cell 40 by 30 with AB took the scale 1.44061, the column first widened to 41.40525).
**NEW.** The date formats of a table's cell show `%C`, `%h`, `%F`, `%r` (as `%X`), `%u` (1 on a Monday to 7 on a Sunday), `%z` and
`%Z` as AutoCAD 2021 shows them (probed in its console in en-US from a DXF whose dates carry their day of the week): 20, Mar,
2020-03-07, 3:04:05 PM, 6, and the zone of the machine, +0700 and its daylight name, "SE Asia Daylight Time", for every date. `%j`,
`%U`, `%W`, `%V`, `%G` and `%g` still show the date: AutoCAD gives `%j` 001 for every date it reads, `%U` 01 on a Sunday and 00 on any
other day, and `%W` 01 on a Monday and 00 on any other, the day of the year never being worked out for a date it reads, which is
plainly wrong.

**CHANGED.** MLEDIT's tees (CT, OT, MT) work on the pair of segments AutoCAD 2021 takes, as the crosses do, and not on the ones the picks
lie on: the stem is run on past the free end of its first or last segment, the second is met on one of its segments (the end of its
last is not on it), the pair nearest the picks is taken, and the end of the stem kept is the side of the meeting its pick is on. The
stem (30, -60)-(30, -100)-(80, -100) picked on its second segment at (55, -100), onto (0, 0)-(100, 0), has its start moved to
(30, 0) with its elements starting 20 along. Where no pair can be made, the nearest pair of all says whether it is `Invalid operation
on a self intersecting multiline.` (the stem's start caps put off, nothing else changed: the stem (130, -100)-(130, -60)-(180, -60)
onto the same line) or `These multilines do not intersect.` (the stem (130, -60)-(130, -100)-(180, -100)). 80 stems of an L against a
straight multiline at 3 options, a random run of 600 tees (184 differences from AutoCAD before, 79 now) and 503 rows of the new
tests agree; the tees onto a second of three segments are right in about two cases of three (a meeting within the width of a corner
and the stem's other segments are left, parked). A break across the second that reaches the end of its last segment leaves nothing
beyond it, as a cross's does.
**CHANGED.** MLEDIT's crosses break each element on the segment of its own line the crossing is nearest the picks on, one element after
another, as AutoCAD 2021 does, so that within the width of a multiline of a corner the elements of one crossing are broken on different
segments, and a break that runs past the end of an element over a corner is written as AutoCAD writes it: from where it starts to the
end of the segment, the next segment whole and the rest of the break as the start of the one after it, where each of the two lines
of the other multiline meets the element's path once. The staircase (0, 0)-(100, 0)-(100, 100)-(200, 100) crossed by the vertical
(82, -60)-(82, 60) holds `{0, 82}` and `{0, 82, 102}` on its first segment, nothing on its second and `{2}` on its third for the
first element; a line that meets the path twice or not at all (the U, the L at x = 85) is still `Invalid operation on a self
intersecting multiline.`, and the elements are now broken one by one up to the one it is said of, the ones before it left broken as
AutoCAD leaves them. The 25 breaks within 20 of a corner of a staircase that were left out are equal, with 1 674 crosses of a U, a Z and
two staircases (176 differences fewer, none more) and 615 of the staircase (114 fewer); a cross that runs the second multiline on
past its end (OC, MC), and a break that ends exactly on a vertex, are left as they were.
**CHANGED.** MLEDIT with the same multiline picked twice says nothing for a cross or a tee and asks for the first again, as AutoCAD 2021
does (the corner joint still says `These multilines do not intersect.`), and a corner joint picked on the very point the lines meet keeps
the start of that multiline. CS, CA and WA write a cut that runs to the end of an element without the stretch that would start there
(a cut from 35 of an element 50 long is `{0, 35}`, not `{0, 35, 50}`).
**CHANGED.** A grip or STRETCH that moves a vertex of a closed multiline cut across a vertex puts no nought in front of the list of the first
segment or the last, as AutoCAD 2021 does (the triangle (0, 0)-(100, 0)-(50, 80) cut from (75, 40) to (25, 40) across (50, 80), whose
vertex (100, 0) goes to (90, 0), still holds `{47.1699}` at (50, 80)): the 20 moves of the triangle and 6 of the six-sided staircase that
were left out are equal, 56 of the 687 probed moves fixed and none changed for the worse. Left out: 4 moves of the staircase's concave
corner and 30 cuts AutoCAD writes inside out (parked).
**NEW.** A solid or surface made by a sweep along a spline, an extrusion at a slant, a spline turned about an axis, a spline extruded
with its exact surface kept, and a loft through rectangles, saved as another version (`DxfDatabase.Save(path, version)`), was left out
of the file going to R2000, R2004, R2007 and R2010 and, from R2010, going to R2013 and R2018. The data of R2010 holds them now, as the
SAT AutoCAD 2021 writes (probed in its console: 65 bodies of R2018, among them boxes, cylinders, spheres, tori, extrusions, revolutions,
sweeps, lofts, unions, subtractions, fillets, shells and surfaces, read by it and written as R2004, R2007 and R2010, equal its own text
line for line, which is 390 conversions): the oblique extrusion (`sum_spl_sur`, `sumsur` in R2004) and the turned spline (`rot_spl_sur`,
`rotsur`) are written in every version from R2004 on with the numbers and the flag each has, the sweep (`sweep_sur`, the rail with its law and
edges, or no rail and a scale along the path) in R2010, and an exact surface kept by an extruded spline (`cyl_spl_sur` of `full`) in
all. A sweep along a spline goes to R2000, R2004 and R2007 as the text of R2010, as a loft does, and AutoCAD reads it there with the volume
it had (6 by 4 swept along a spline: 2 463.5152, where AutoCAD's own R2004 file holds a spline of its own of 2 463.7445); R2013 and R2018 open
with the volume and `AUDIT` finds 0 errors in all 96 files probed. Going up, the text of R2010 of these surfaces is read into the data of R2013.
**FIXED.** An edge AutoCAD writes as reversed (the edges a fillet, a shell or a thickened surface makes) was refused by the SAT and SAB
converters, and so the body was left out of a file saved as another version: a box with 12 filleted edges, a shell and a thickened
surface now go to every version, and the curve of intersection of two surfaces (`par_int_cur`) with the flag R2013 holds after it.
**CHANGED.** A normal that is a unit but for its last bit (a plane whose normal is 0.9999999999999999 long) is written divided by its
length going from the SAB of R2013 or R2018 to the text of an older version, as AutoCAD writes a body it has read from a file; it
kept the three numbers as they were, which is what AutoCAD writes of a body it made in its own memory and never read (a pyramid,
a taper, a slanted extrusion and a sweep read from R2018: 24 lines of 8 of 65 bodies differed in the last digit).
**CHANGED.** A table going to R2000 or R2004 is saved some 20 percent faster: the data table of its cells takes its handles from the
seed of the drawing at once and shares the groups every cell holds (5 tables of 100 rows by 20 columns saved from R2018 as R2000 in
125 ms before and 98 after, and as R2004 in 126 and 100 ms, the bytes of the file unchanged).
**NEW.** The front and back planes of XCLIP Clipdepth cut what a clipped block shows, as AutoCAD 2021 draws it (PNGOUT of a block
of five lines at several heights, in plan and in an isometric view): the block is shown from the back plane to the front plane,
planes included, in the units of the clip system whatever the reference's scale, and from the plane of the boundary, which goes with
the block (a reference 15 high, clipped in the world's plane with front 20 and back -10, shows a line rising from (0, 0, 0) to
(100, 0, 100) over its first 5 of x, the same block standing at 0 over its first 20). An entity wholly above the front plane or below the back one is
left out, a line that crosses a plane is cut at it, and any other entity that crosses one is drawn whole, since the display keeps
no height to cut it by (parked). A clip that is off shows the whole block, as AutoCAD does. The planes of an external reference are
written and not applied (parked).
**FIXED.** Clipdepth answered by a point took 0 whatever the plane: it is the point's distance from the boundary's plane along the
boundary's normal, the point lying on the plane of the current user coordinate system, so that it is 15 from a boundary made in the
world's plane when the system stands 15 higher and 0 from one made in that system (AutoCAD 2021 writes 15 and 0). A front plane
equal to the back plane, or above it by a millionth or less, was taken; AutoCAD refuses it with the same message (front 10 with back
9.999999 refused, with 9.999998 taken).
**FIXED.** The clip boundary of a block made in a system tilted out of the plan (AutoCAD writes them; the presenter makes none): a
vertex dragged is taken to the level plane through its grip and moves by the parts of the offset along the boundary's own X and Y
axes, as AutoCAD 2021's `MoveGripPointsAt` moves it (corner (10, 10) of a boundary turned 30 degrees about X, dragged by (5, 3, 0),
goes to (15, 10 + 3 cos 30); a reference scaled by 2, turned, lifted and moved gives the same steps), where it took the foot of the
point on the block's plane and put the vertex 12.5 off in the example. The block is shown where the boundary's prism, its lines along
the boundary's normal, cuts the plane of the block, and the frame is drawn where the boundary stands in the plan, as AutoCAD's own
plan view shows them (a grid shows from y 73.09 to 130.83 for a boundary whose frame runs from y 58.66 to 101.96). A clip
parallel to the block's plane draws as before.
**CHANGED.** A LINE, an ARC, a CIRCLE and a LWPOLYLINE of a `DxfFile` (and so of every drawing the presenter opens) are read from the bytes of their
records, where each group was made a string and a reader object made for the entity (3 KB of garbage and 1.1 to 1.6 µs for a LINE, an ARC
or a CIRCLE, 6.6 KB and 4.0 µs for a polyline of four vertices with a bulge, 1.4 KB of each the reader object). The shapes are the same to
the bit: the group order, padded codes, CRLF or LF, `+.5`, `1E-3`, `-0`, a tab round a value, the first group of a code, the checks the
reader makes of every number and whole number of the record, and the extrusion, the elevation, the bulges and the closed flag are as the
reader has them; a number of up to 19 digits is read from its digits and the power of ten (one multiplication or division where the digits
are at most 2^53 and the power is within 1E22; otherwise, as for the 17 digits AutoCAD writes, a 192-bit product of the digits and a 128-bit
power of ten, taken only where both ends of its range give the same double), the number the reader reads from the text, the double
nearest it, on .NET Framework as on .NET 10; any number it cannot settle is read by the reader's own number reader, and any record it is
not sure of (a letter beyond ASCII in a number, no radius, no length, a group code that is no number, an exception) is read the long way.
A LINE, an ARC or a CIRCLE takes 0.2 to 0.5 µs and 64 to 88 bytes of garbage now, a polyline 2.0 µs and 3.0 KB (2.3 KB of it the closed
polyline with an arc that it is), and a number of 17 digits 0.04 to 0.13 µs where it took 0.4 to 0.9. The shapes of the 78 000 of these
in a drawing of 100 000 entities (lines, arcs, circles, polylines with a bulge and texts, one entity in fifty an INSERT) take 86 ms (.NET 8) and 123 (.NET Framework 4.8) where
they took 170 and 270; its display, from the opened file, takes 350 ms where it took 400 (.NET 8; medians of 9 runs, three alternated
rounds) and 550 ms where it took 650 (.NET Framework 4.8), and that of 1 000 000 entities 3.1 to 3.9 s where it took 3.5 to 4.0 and 5.0 to
5.5 s where it took 6.1 to 7.0; opening the file, a layer switched on (1.0 s at 1 000 000) and the heap (650.9 MB, 658.8 MB) are as they
were. The 4 377 LINEs, ARCs and polylines of an AutoCAD sample of 17-digit coordinates (070-PBBASE) are read in 14 ms where they took 37
(.NET 8), 4 where 21 (.NET Framework). The display list of 160 drawings (the 100 000 entities and 159 AutoCAD samples read in place) is
the same bit for bit under both runtimes. Checked against the long read on 200 000 generated records of each of the four types (groups in
any order, omitted, repeated, padded, in 18 number formats, with extrusions, elevations, bulges, closed flags and comments; run under both
runtimes), on the 121 792 LINEs, ARCs, CIRCLEs and LWPOLYLINEs of the 167 AutoCAD sample drawings, and on 27 million numbers against the
reader's number reader (random digits, the shortest text of doubles of any bits, the ties between two doubles, powers of ten). The shapes
are still kept: with the faster read, the polylines' shapes read afresh would still make a layer switched on at 1 000 000 entities take
1.3 to 1.5 s in place of 1.0 s, for 578 MB of heap in place of 651.

**CHANGED.** Every number read from text (the reader's own number reader, `Numbers.TryRead`, which `DxfReader.Read`, the typed values of a
`DxfFile`, the header, the tables and the DWG reader's text numbers all go through) is read from its digits and the power of ten with no
array made, as the fast read of the shapes reads a number from bytes, and the double is the same to the bit: one multiplication or division
where the digits are at most 2^53 and the power is within 1E22, otherwise the 192-bit product of the digits and a 128-bit power of ten, taken
only where both ends of its range give the same double, and the long way (the digits in an array, a guess moved a step at a time in
integers) for any other text, for a number of more than 19 digits or of an exponent of more than three, and for a letter beyond ASCII. A
power of ten up to 1E38 is held whole by the 128 bits, so a tie between two doubles of a whole number of 16 to 19 digits (9007199254740993)
is settled by the product with no second end to the range. A number of 17 digits, as AutoCAD writes them, takes 0.03 µs where it took 0.15
and a value such as 1.4210854715202004E-14 0.03 where it took 0.26 (.NET 8; 0.04 where 0.3 and 0.5 under .NET Framework 4.8), a short one
(`12.5`) 0.011 µs where it took 0.014 (0.014 and 0.025); `DxfReader.Read` of a drawing of 100 000 entities with 17 digits in every
coordinate (15 MB) takes 314 ms where it took 414 (.NET 8) and 390 where it took 639 (.NET Framework 4.8), the same drawing with short
numbers (7 MB) 255 and 350 ms as before, and the 167 AutoCAD sample drawings together 628 ms where they took 685 (.NET 8) and 935 where
1 010 (.NET Framework 4.8). The values are as they were: the 167 AutoCAD sample drawings read by `DxfReader.Read` (shapes, the typed groups
kept and the text `DxfWriter` writes of them) and by the presenter (the display list) are the same bit for bit before and after under both
runtimes, and so are the drawings of 100 000 and 1 000 000 entities; every group value of the samples is read the same by the two ways,
and 27 million texts (random digits, the shortest text of doubles of any bits, the ties between two doubles, powers of ten, texts with
letters beyond ASCII) against the long way, under both runtimes.
**CHANGED.** A TEXT and an MTEXT of a `DxfFile` are read from the bytes of their records, as a LINE, an ARC, a CIRCLE and a LWPOLYLINE are:
the words are cut from the bytes by the file's decoding and go through the reader's own functions for `%%c`, carets, escapes and the
formatting of an MTEXT, an MTEXT's own groups are those before an object embedded in it (the first 101), and the same shapes come out to
the bit, however the groups are ordered, repeated, padded or written (a TEXT in 0.17 µs where it took 1.7, 0.33 where 2.7 under .NET
Framework 4.8). The first INSERT of a `DxfFile` that is asked for the shapes it places learns the layer of every other entity of the
drawing from the first group 8 of its bytes, where it made a reader record of each (0.8 µs of 98 000 entities in a drawing of 100 000): the
shapes of the 98 000 entities that are not INSERTs and then of the first INSERT take 63 ms where they took 126 (.NET 8), 113 where 181
(.NET Framework 4.8). The display of a drawing is not faster for them but for the numbers (the 20 000 TEXTs of the drawing of 100 000
entities display in 41 ms where they took 49 under .NET 8; its whole cold display is within the noise of the machine, about 310 ms under
.NET 8 and 500 under .NET Framework 4.8): a TEXT is drawn from the groups of its entity and an INSERT from the entities of its block. The
entities an INSERT places are not read from bytes: the records of the blocks are read once with their numbers kept, and each placed entity
takes 0.6 µs, a fifth of it its look. Checked against the long read on 200 000 generated records of each of the six types (the words with
signs, carets, escapes, letters beyond ASCII and MTEXT formatting, the alignments, extrusions, embedded objects and bad numbers; run under
both runtimes) and on the 135 987 LINEs, ARCs, CIRCLEs, LWPOLYLINEs, TEXTs and MTEXTs of the 167 AutoCAD sample drawings (135 777 read
from bytes); a drawing's layer spelling, which the INSERTs it places take, is the same.

**NEW.** MLEADERCOLLECT (MLC) in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console runs it (probed through standard input, multileaders made by
MLEADER in a style of a block), and the Collect button of the Annotate tab's Leaders panel. "Select multileaders:" then "Specify
collected multileader location or [Vertical/Horizontal/Wrap] <Horizontal>:": the multileaders stay as they are and each block moves, by
its extents, so that the blocks stand in the order selected side by side, one under another or in rows, their boxes touching, their tops
level in a row and the first one's left at the point, which is the top left of the group (three circles of radius 5 collected at
(150, 150) have their middles at (155, 145), (165, 145) and (175, 145); a box 20 by 10, a square 8 by 8 and such a circle have their
lefts at 150, 170 and 178 and their tops at 150). Wrap asks "Specify wrap width or [Number]: <0.000000>" and breaks the row where the
next block would not stay short of the width (two blocks 10 wide stand in a row at 20.0001 and one to a row at 20), or under Number
"Specify number per row <1>:" after that many; the next row is as far down as the tallest block above is high. Only one leader is kept:
the leader lines of the last multileader selected go to the first block's left, or to the right of the last block of the first row
where the arrowhead is nearer that landing (a circle row ending at 180: an arrowhead at x = 163 keeps the leader at 142, at 167 at 188,
its dogleg turned against x), a column having both ends at its last block; a leader on each side of the last multileader keeps each at
its end, and the leaders of every other multileader are taken away. Multileaders of words, other objects and those on a locked layer
are left out (`2 were filtered out`, `1 was on a locked layer.`, asking again where none is left). The registry is of 264 commands.
The point is the top left as typed; AutoCAD's console reads it shifted by the first multileader's arrowhead, which is taken out here.
**CHANGED.** The styles a hatch or an MTEXT makes of its own, the lines of a pattern, the middle colour of a gradient and the runs of an
MTEXT in a colour, are one object for each colour and weight in a display list, as the style of a LINE is, where each hatch and each MTEXT
made a style of its own with its look (100 bytes). A drawing of 100 000 entities, half of them hatches and half MTEXTs (250 000 texts among
the items), held 75 000 styles and holds three: the display list is 135.0 MB where it was 142.4, and the heap grows by 343.6 MB once the
drawing is opened, displayed and its pick index made, where it grew by 351.0 MB (356.7 MB where it was 364.2 under .NET Framework 4.8). A
drawing of lines, arcs, circles, polylines and texts has none to share, and its 650.9 MB at 1 000 000 entities is the same, as are its
display, frame, layer-on and layer-off times (medians of five, .NET 8 and .NET Framework 4.8, within the noise of a machine other work was
running on). The display list of 19 drawings (4 of our own and 15 AutoCAD samples) and the pixels of each at 5 views, plain, selected,
highlighted and hovered, the saved bytes and the list after a layer off, on and a REGEN are the same bit for bit under both. What else a
displayed drawing keeps was weighed and stays: the shapes an entity has read (128 MB at 1 000 000 entities) take 2 to 10 µs and 3 to 6 KB
of garbage to read again, and a layer switched on at 1 000 000 entities took 2.4 s without them where it takes 1.1 s; the strings of a
hatch's loops, a seventh of the hatch and MTEXT drawing, take 10 µs a hatch to read again, and a layer switched on in it took 20 per cent
longer without them. The handle strings (31 MB) are the one string each entity, its display items and its run share, and an arc's box
(25 MB) is asked for at each arc a frame shows as a dot.

**FIXED.** The DWG writer gave a TEXT, ATTRIB or ATTDEF whose alignment point is (0, 0) the point as two bit doubles, where
AutoCAD's own DWG has none (bit 0x02 of the data flags set; the reader gives (0, 0) back): 40 TEXT and ATTDEF objects of the 13
`Dynamic Blocks` drawings of AutoCAD 2021 came back one bit off its bytes, 132 bits longer, and are its bytes now. The 63 ARC
objects that remain one bit off are radians no double of degrees divides to (8.9 percent of random radians; none is reached from a
neighbouring double of degrees), which a DXF in degrees cannot carry; AutoCAD itself copies the radians of a DWG it saves as a DWG.
**FIXED.** The `RTMaterial` extended data of a DWG of AutoCAD 2000 or 2004 (the material of an entity, which those formats have no
place for) was passed on to the R2018 file as extended data and the entity left at the material ByLayer. AutoCAD takes it into
the entity's material when it reads the file and writes no extended data: the LINE of the `matvis` drawing with material 78, and the
BLOCK and ENDBLK entities of `xclip` with material 0 (none), are AutoCAD's own bytes now, and AutoCAD's DXF of the rewrite has the
material (347) and no `RTMaterial`. A DWG of R2000 or R2004 rewritten has `AUDIT` as before.
**FIXED.** A dynamic block with a lookup table (`BLOCKLOOKUPACTION`) in a DWG of AutoCAD 2000 or 2004 was left out as broken, and with
it the lookup parameter and grip, the linear parameter, the stretch and the evaluation graph that lean on it: the reader looked for the
table's texts in a string stream that those versions do not have. The 26 R2000 and R2004 files AutoCAD 2021 saves of the 13
`Dynamic Blocks` drawings now read as many objects of each type as AutoCAD's DXF of them (Architectural - Metric had 21 of 391 left out, a panel
made in code with one lookup 14 of its objects).
**FIXED.** The internal writer of R2013 (AC1027; `DwgWriter` writes R2018 alone) made files AutoCAD 2021 refused with `ErrorStatus` 53,
even a drawing of a few lines. AutoCAD's own R2013 file has a long of 0 after the size of its header and of its classes and names the
maintenance release 125; the writer gave neither. With them the 36 drawings of the tests and the samples, written as R2013, open with
`AUDIT` finding 0 errors in 29 and, in the others, the 24, 24, 2, 2, 32, 32 and 10 of their originals. R2010 and R2018 files are unchanged.
**NEW.** WMFIN brings a Windows Metafile in as a block, as AutoCAD 2021's console runs it (probed through standard input). The
presenter reads the metafile itself (the placeable header and the records of lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, ellipses, arcs,
pens, brushes, fonts and text; bitmaps, regions and clipping are read past) and makes block WMF0 of 2D polylines and TEXT, fitted with
its aspect kept into half the view with its top left at the block's origin and y down: a window of 1 000 by 1 000 with a line from
(100, 100) to (900, 900) in a pen of 10 is a polyline from (0.5, -0.5) to (4.5, -4.5) of width 0.05, in a view 10 high. The block is of
inches and its INSERT is placed as INSERT places one, scaled 25.4 in a drawing of millimetres, after `Units: Unitless   Conversion:
25.4000`, the insertion point (Basepoint, Scale, X, Y, Z, Rotate, Explode and REpeat), the scales and the rotation. A pen's colour is
the nearest index (7 for black), a closed shape takes its brush's, a text becomes a TEXT in a style `WMF-Arial0` of its face. The
window's Open dialog is titled Import WMF; a name that is no file is `Cannot find the specified metafile`. The variables WMFBKGND and
WMFFOREGND are kept, as AutoCAD's console keeps them and ignores them. IMPORT still refuses a .wmf, as AutoCAD 2021's does. The
registry is of 263 commands.

**FIXED.** EXPORTPDF's Include hyperlinks through a layout's viewports took the box of the model-space object turned as a box, and
the box of the clip as the place the object shows. A viewport twisted 30 degrees showed a line (1 800, 1 200) to (2 200, 1 800) at 1:20 a
link 32.3 wide where the line is drawn 2.3 wide, and a circle of radius 300 one 41 wide where it is 30; the link is now over the box of
what the viewport draws (the points of the line, polyline, arc or fill taken through the viewport's transformation; the turned box
of an item with no such points, text or an image). An object in the notch of an L-shaped clip (the box of the clip holds it, the clip
does not) had a link over nothing, and has none; one across the notch keeps its box cut to the clip's box. A quarter turn and a
rectangular clip were already exact (tests added with the rectangles in points).
**FIXED.** Find and Replace said `1 matches in 1 objects`; it says `1 match in 1 object`, `2 matches in 1 object` and `0 matches in 0 objects`,
the singular of AutoCAD's own strings (`%d match found`, `%d matches found`; read from its text-find resource DLL).
**FIXED.** The Enhanced Attribute Editor's list cut a long value at the scrollbar with no sign (`Riverside bloc`) and gave the prompt
column 336 of 566 pixels for 10 characters; the Value column is 180 wide, the text ends in an ellipsis before the scrollbar and so does
a long prompt. Drawn with the screenshot mode on a block of ten attributes (`--dialog eattedit`, `battman`, `battman-edit` with its
three tabs, `battman-settings`, `attdia`) with no other fault found: the controls are all there and none overlaps.

**CHANGED.** -HATCH's draW boundary keeps the loops in the order the shapes were drawn and as they were drawn, and flags them as
AutoCAD 2021 does (probed in its console): an island drawn first is loop 0 (the square (10, 10) to (20, 20) and then (0, 0) to
(50, 50) give loops flagged 16 and 1, where the outer came first, flagged 1 and 16), a shape drawn clockwise stays clockwise in the
loop and in the polyline kept, and a loop is flagged External (1) with no loop round it, Outermost (16) inside one and nothing
inside two or more (five squares nested are 1, 16, 0, 0, 0). A loop lies inside another where it lies wholly in it, edges touching
allowed: two squares of 60 and 50 that overlap are each External, where the presenter took the one with a corner inside the other as
its island, and a square sharing an edge with the outer is an island.
**CHANGED.** An open shape drawn by -HATCH's draW boundary (Enter in place of Close) is a loop that is not closed, as AutoCAD 2021
keeps it, where the hatch closed it across: beside a closed shape it is kept as the edges drawn, flagged NotClosed (33, or 48 inside
another loop), so that a line (60, 0) to (80, 0) beside a square is a one-edge loop and an open triangle of two edges stays two; alone,
or with other open shapes only, it makes no hatch and says `Unable to fill the boundary with solid.` (`Unable to hatch the boundary.`
for a pattern), and the gap tolerance closes none of them. A shape left open on its first point is a closed loop of the corners before
it, its polyline kept open with the first point again. Retained, an open shape is still kept as an open polyline where no hatch is
made. The tests that ended a drawn shape with Enter to have it closed across now close it with Close.
**CHANGED.** -HATCH's draW boundary retained under associativity makes the hatch associative to the polylines kept, as AutoCAD 2021
does (HPASSOC 1, Retain Y: group 71 of 1, each loop with its own polyline's handle, the open ones too, HPASSOC left at 1); not retained
it makes none and turns associativity off, as before. The polylines are made before the hatch, as AutoCAD orders them, where they came
after it, and a polyline of a shape whose loop an island style dropped is kept all the same.
**NEW.** A loop of edges flagged `DxfHatchLoopTypes.NotClosed` need not end where it starts: `DxfHatch.AppendLoop` and `InsertLoopAt`
take two lines (60, 0) to (80, 0) and (80, 0) to (70, 20) as `External | NotClosed` and write flag 33 with two edges, which AutoCAD 2021
reads; a loop not so flagged still has to close.

**CHANGED.** MLEADERALIGN in the presenter follows AutoCAD 2021's console run through standard input, which runs the real
current command where a script did not. Make leader segments Parallel is built: each other multileader's first leader line turns
about its arrowhead to run the way the one picked runs, its length kept, the content and landing moving with its end (arrowheads
at (70, 30) and (130, 10) with leaders of 58.31 and 31.62 follow a leader at 45 degrees to (111.2311, 71.2311) and (152.3607,
32.3607)). The line of Use current spacing runs through the landing of the one picked (the point its dogleg ends at), the
direction taken from there; specify Spacing puts the one picked first and the others after it in the order they stand along the
direction, and measures the gap between the boxes of the contents, each the width and height of the words with the landing gap
before and after them (words 1.14, 0.06 and 2.34 wide, a landing gap of 0.09 and a spacing of 20 put the landings 21.32 and 20.24
apart, up the page 0.18 apart for words 0.18 high); Distribute puts the first landing on the first point and the last on the
second, the gaps between the boxes all the same. The prompts are AutoCAD's: `Specify spacing <0.000000>:`, `Current mode: Spacing:
20.000000` and `Current mode: Make leader lines parallel`, the default of the options prompt `<make segments Parallel>` or
`<specify Spacing>`. MLEADERCOLLECT is still not built.
**CHANGED.** TEXTALIGN in the presenter takes Left and Right along a line of two points to the top left and top right corners of
each box, as TL and TR, and Center to its middle, as AutoCAD 2021 does (three texts 2.5 high at (10, 10), (60, 25) and (30, 50) on a
line of slope 1/2 through (30, 50) under Left have their left edges at -45, -15 and 35 where it stands at 12.5, 27.5 and 52.5);
they stood at the middle of the left and right edges.
**CHANGED.** MLEADERALIGN in the presenter holds each content by the left middle of its box, as AutoCAD 2021's console does
(probed through standard input, multileaders made by MLEADER): the box is the words' (measured in the drawing's fonts, which
the presenter did not use here, so that every box was as wide as its two landing gaps) widened by the landing gap each side, or a
block's extents, which it took for a point; the point is the middle of the first line of the words, or the middle of the block,
and the line the contents are put on runs through that of the one picked, from where a direction is taken, whichever side the
leaders are on (a leader on the right of its words used to be put on the line by the end of its box, a box's width off: ONE
landing at (90, 10) from (100, 0) has its box from 88.98 to 89.64 and a direction straight up from 88.98 puts the left of every
other box on that line). The contents stand in the order of their lefts along the line, and Distribute puts the left middle of the
first on the first point and of the last on the second (words 0.48, 0.84 and 2.01 wide, from (0, 100) to (100, 100): boxes at 0,
about 50.6 and 100). A content whose arrowhead ends up past the middle of its box has its leader turned to the other side, as AutoCAD
turns it, the words or block staying where they are: TWO from an arrowhead at (30, 0) aligned to a box from 10.36 to 11.08 is held at
its top right at 10.99, its dogleg against x ending 0.09 past the words and its landing a dogleg further, at y a right attachment
(by the style's right side) below their top; one on the left of its words lands on the left of an arrowhead at 9 or before the
middle (10.72) and is held at its top left. The leader takes the next index (0 becomes 1), as AutoCAD writes it. Only a
multileader of one leader line is turned.
**CHANGED.** TEXTALIGN in the presenter sets and distributes along a line of two points as AutoCAD 2021's console does (four TEXT
2.5 high, A, BBB, CCCCCC and DDDD, from (0, 0), (60, 25), (30, 50) and (45, 40) to the line from (30, 50) to (130, 100)): Set spacing and
Distribute put the texts in the order their corners stand along the line from its first point, the first corner on it, whatever way the
line runs (a level or an upright line is not discarded, as Current Vertical discards it); each next corner stands far enough on along
the line that its box is the spacing from the one before, measured along the line, either across (the width of the box before it,
or of the one after it under TR and other right-hand alignments, over the cosine of the line's slope, plus the spacing) or up (the
height over the sine), the less of the two: under TL and a spacing of 3 the corners are 4.863, 8.59 and 8.59 apart along the line,
in the order A, CCCCCC, DDDD, BBB; Distribute puts the last corner on the second point and gives every two boxes the one gap that
takes it there (32.92 for the same texts). They were stacked from the top by the height of the boxes, as for a text picked.
**NEW.** DIMBREAK Auto in the presenter breaks a dimension at the shapes of a block reference in their places, as AutoCAD 2021
does (a rectangle block 6 by 4 held at (-3, -12) breaks a vertical extension line at x = 0 at -12 and at -8, 0.0625 either side, where
its whole box would give one gap from -12.0625 to -7.9375; scaled by 2 from (-6, -12) at -12 and -4, turned 30 degrees at -10.2679 and
-5.6491), and at TEXT and MTEXT turned off the axes over the stretch of the line inside their turned box (words 15.83 by 2.5 turned
45 degrees at (-3, -21): from -18.0625 to -14.4020), where the box of their extents, which it took for the box they would fill
upright, gave -21.0625 to -7.9739. A hatch breaks nothing (only a boundary that is drawn does), as AutoCAD. The words are
measured in the drawing's fonts.
**NEW.** DIMBREAK Auto in the presenter breaks a dimension at ellipses, splines, xlines and rays, and at TEXT and MTEXT over the whole
box of the words with the break size beyond it each side, as AutoCAD 2021 breaks it (probed in its console: an xline across the
extension lines breaks both, an ellipse crossed at 15 and 17 breaks at 15.0001 and 16.9999, a TEXT 2.5 high standing from 1 to 3.5 across
one breaks it from 0.9375 to 3.5625); it broke at lines, polylines, circles and arcs only. The break size is 0.125 times DIMSCALE (0.25 at a
scale of 2, 0.0625 at 0.5), as before.
**FIXED.** A block cell of a table was drawn at its insertion point and its row left as it stood. As AutoCAD 2021 lays it out
(`GenerateLayout` and `RecomputeTableBlock` in its console, margins 1.5): a block not fitted to its cell asks the box its extents
fill (an attribute definition left out), at the cell's scale and turn, and the margins: a block 10 by 40 at scale 1 makes its row
43, at scale 2 83, over two merged rows of 8 it makes 21.5 each (41.5 at scale 2), shared as the words of a merged block are; one
wider than its column widens the column first (100 wide in a column 30 wide makes 103, a block turned 45 degrees 38.35534 in the
row and the column), and a block fitted to its cell (`SetAutoScale`) asks nothing. `CadTableEditor` (the presenter's editing of
cells, its Redraw, a typed cell and the least a row's line is dragged to) lays the rows and columns out so, and
`DxfTable.RecomputeTableBlock` draws the INSERT of a block cell by its extents: they are aligned in the cell by its alignment,
in from its sides by the margins (the block above, at the middle of a cell 30 wide and 8 high at x 40 and y -18, stands with its
insertion point at (50, -42), where it stood at (55, -22) off the cell), and a fitted block takes the scale that fits the box its
turned extents fill into the cell less its margins, min((W - 2 margins) / width, (H - 2 margins) / height): 0.125 for that block, 1.425
in a cell 40 wide and 60 high, 0.925 turned 90 degrees, 1.29099 turned 30 (some 80 blocks placed and fitted in the 2 by 2 tables of AutoCAD's console). A block turned by exactly
90, 180 or 270 degrees stands where AutoCAD puts it, off its aligned box by the block's own width and height. The scale in the
cell (144) is not changed.
**FIXED.** A line set on the top left cell of a block of merged cells of a table made in code (`SetGridColor`,

to AutoCAD's reading of the same files).
**CHANGED.** A row is laid out by the one line, four thirds of the text height, of its first cell alone, and the other cells ask for

**NEW.** CENTERMARK and CENTERLINE in the presenter, as AutoCAD 2021's console ran them (accoreconsole fed through standard
input, which takes picks after a ZOOM, where a script could not). CENTERMARK asks `Select circle or arc to add center mark:`
until Enter and draws an INSERT of an anonymous block (`*U`) at the centre: a cross of CENTERCROSSSIZE (0.1x of the diameter,
4 long on a circle of radius 20) in ByBlock colour and Continuous, and four lines in the linetype of CENTERLTYPE (Center2)
from CENTERCROSSGAP (0.05x) past the cross to CENTEREXE (0.12) past the rim: from 4 to 20.12 on that circle, from 10 to 50.12
on one of radius 50. CENTERMARKEXE 0 hides the four lines, CENTERLTSCALE scales them, CENTERLAYER names their layer (made where
the drawing has none). CENTERLINE asks `Select first line:` and `Select second line:` (a line or a straight segment of a
polyline) and draws one line between them, along the bisector of their directions, from the line through their two start
points to the line through their two end points, CENTEREXE longer at each end: two parallel lines of 100 and 120 starting 30
apart give 110 about the middle of their middles, and lines of 20 and 40 degrees end where they cross. Both are associative as
AutoCAD 2021 writes them, group for group: an `ACDBASSOCACTION` in the `ACDBASSOCNETWORK` of the space (its extension
dictionary and a dictionary of the named objects), `AcDbCenterMarkActionBody` or `AcDbCenterLineActionBody` (class of
`AcDbSmartCenter`), `ACDBASSOCGEOMDEPENDENCY` on each circle, arc or line with its `ACDBASSOCEDGEACTIONPARAM`, and an
`ACDBASSOCDEPENDENCY` on the INSERT; a DXF the presenter wrote was opened by AutoCAD 2021, audited with no error, and moving
or scaling the circle (or a line) there redrew the mark as it did here. Moving or scaling the circle moves the mark and draws
it again for the new radius; a mark moved on its own is no longer tied (AutoCAD 2021 leaves it where it was moved to), and
erasing it takes its action and networks out. A drawing older than R2010 gets the picture and no action. Registry 262
commands.

**NEW.** OBJECTISOLATIONMODE in the presenter, and what AutoCAD 2021 keeps in the drawing of ISOLATEOBJECTS, HIDEOBJECTS and

**CHANGED.** REFEDIT, REFSET and REFCLOSE use the words of AutoCAD 2021's own string table (AcRefEdRes.dll, read as data: its

**`, `** Cannot REFEDIT anonymous block **` (`dimension or table blocks` for `*D` and `*T`) and refuses a reference
whose scale factors differ in size as AutoCAD does, `** Cannot REFEDIT a non-uniformly scaled block **` (it took one and left
its circle out). REFSET says `Transfer objects between the RefEdit working set and host drawing...`, `3 Added to working set`
or `1 Removed from working set` and `** 2 selected objects are already in the working set **` (`are not in` for Remove);
REFCLOSE asks `Enter option [Save/Discard reference changes] <Save>:` and says `1 object added to BOX`, `1 object removed
from BOX` and `2 block instances updated`. The refusals of BEDIT, a second REFEDIT, QSAVE and SAVEAS, and of REFSET and
REFCLOSE with no edit open, are AutoCAD's lines (`** BEDIT command not allowed during reference editing **` and the rest).
`CadRefEdit.NotAllowed` is `CadRefEdit.NotAllowedFor(command)`, a command's own line, and `CadRefEdit.NotEditing` is AutoCAD's
`** Command not allowed unless a reference is checked out with REFEDIT command **`. Not known: the order of these lines, and
whether the handles of the objects saved back are kept (the presenter writes each as a new object); the console cannot run a long
transaction, which REFEDIT is made on.

**FIXED.** REVCLOUD in the presenter is now AutoCAD 2021's, checked in its console run interactively (14 November: the console

level, not along the line: the line moves by the chord times the sine of its slope towards the side the words lie (1.6577 at 30 degrees,
2.0235 at 90, 1.117 at 200 for a line of 40 with the words put 8 past its end and 5 over it, the other way for a line leaning the other
way and for words before the start) and ends the chord times the cosine short of the words' level; on a short line (7.2 at 30 degrees)
the words stand 12.5711 along, an arrowhead and that share of the chord past its end, where the library put them 13.015. Under DIMTMOVE 1,
words put past an end of a line steeper than a slope of a half have the line run on to the level of their point and a level landing back
to a gap beyond them (an arrowhead long at least, the words moving out where it is shorter: an upright line of 40, words 8 past its end
and 5 over it, a landing of 2.5 and the words 0.765 further out), where the library drew the leader from the middle of the line; and the
line between the extension lines is drawn twice for turned words on the middle of a short slanting line that turn its arrowheads out, as
AutoCAD draws it. Words kept level by DIMTOH or DIMTIH on a slanting line fit between the extension lines by the reach of their box, as
turned ones do (not by the chord: "123456789" on a line of 9 at 30 degrees reaches 10.3 and goes out on a leader), and lose their leader
under DIMTMOVE 1 where half the height of their box across the line reaches twice the leader's rise, as turned ones do. Of the probe
sets of the round, tw17 58 differing of 324 now 6, tw18 (11 more slopes) 186 of 1 188 now 17, tw19 (level words on slanting lines, 1 024
